activity_description_1665968605764070772: When it came time to make her fourth international studio album, Midnight Sun, Swedish pop sensation Zara Larsson had her first choice of collaborators on speed dial. “I knew it had to be MNEK,” she says of her “Never Forget You” duet partner and friend. “I knew it was time to get him back. I love him. We always do the best things together, we've been working throughout my whole career, and every time we're in the studio, it's a banger. I just love what he brings out of me.” Once the British songwriter and producer said yes, Zara put together the rest of her team—up-and-coming producer Margo XS and songwriter Helena Gao—and the core four got to work. On day one, they made “Midnight Sun” and lead single “Pretty Ugly”; looking around at each other, Zara says, they realized there was magic in the room. They felt an energy that connected them, emboldening her to be open, vulnerable, raw, and real in her lyrics, her vocal delivery, and the ambition which she felt safe to express in the songs they were creating. “It’s almost like we all completed each other,” Zara says. “We shared tastes and styles and references and stories—it’s like I never had to explain myself when we were having conversations about what these songs could be. This close-knit group…I love to work like that, with people who understand me and vice versa.” Midnight Sun ripples with that same confidence and trust. Its storytelling bursts with truth and vulnerability, plumbing the depth and growth of Zara’s artistry and journey over nearly 20 years in the public eye. It’s an album unafraid to show all sides of the 27-year-old: lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain, often in the same breath. Midnight Sun follows Zara’s first three albums (2017’s So Good, 2021’s Poster Girl, and last year’s VENUS), building upon her legacy while taking things back to her roots. “Making this album brought me back to the very beginning, my first EPs when I started making music, because it was all about having fun and just creating and speaking honestly,” she says. “I really felt no pressure. I think that made things not only feel more fun for me, but the songs feel more authentic, too. The people who will love this album will love a very true part of me, something that I am very proud of and excited about.” With “Midnight Sun” being the first completed song, Zara knew right away it also encompassed the holistic story she wanted to tell on the album. “In thinking about this album, I thought, ‘What do I want to say? What do I want this to be?’ I really am proud of my Swedish pop heritage, so I wanted to write about a Swedish summer where the sun never goes down,” she says. “I wanted the whole album to feel like it's a summer night and it never ends. And it doesn't matter if it's December: the summer night will be there for you. It's waiting for you and it will come back for you, and you will come back for it. To follow “Midnight Sun” in the same session with lead single “Pretty Ugly,” she admits with a laugh, “is maybe the craziest day of songwriting I’ve ever done. I remember sitting there and just saying, ‘Let’s write a song about going insane.’ And it just felt like it was already sitting there in front of us, this block of ice that just needed sculpting. And I really just wanted to scream—so I did. We went back in the next day after hearing Margo’s production to make the verses live up to how fire the song sounded, but what you hear today is what we sent off to be mixed that day because we knew then it was a smash.” On “Saturn’s Return,” the last song finished for Midnight Sun, Zara goes deep on the changes in her life that turning 27 illuminated. “I used to be so certain about every single thing growing up,” she says. “And I used to love that about myself, having the answer to everything. But the older I get, the less I know, the less certain I am. It feels so good. And it's fine to sway a bit in the wind because I know who I am in my core deep down. But I have allowed myself to open up and view the world from other people's perspectives, to be more understanding, to be more compassionate, to be more empathetic. Like I say in the last verse, I had so much pressure and a lot of big goals when I was really young—I was way more stressed then than I am now. I was disappointed when I didn’t get the things I thought I’d achieve. But then that's followed by acceptance and a new burst of inspiration and rediscovery. For me, this song is about stepping into a new era in my life.” A bookend to “Saturn’s Return,” “The Ambition” leaves no stone unturned when it comes to goals, dreams, and the perception of competition encouraged by social media. “Being born as someone who is ambitious and someone who never wants to do something half ass, I’ve always wanted to be number one. Like, why would I be second when I can be first? But that’s setting yourself up for failure because how I viewed my whole life is that if I win, I'm not really that happy because it's expected. But if I don't win, then the world is falling down upon me. So I never really get to experience true joy in being so ambitious. It can always feel a little bit like: what’s next? I think that is the duality of who I am as an artist.” Other highlights like “Girl’s Girl” might remind longtime Zara fans of “Ain’t My Fault,” dialed up to 11. And “Crush” is the album’s “pop banger,” a roller-coaster of emotions recalling the joy of having feelings you know you’ll (probably) never act on. She calls “Blue Moon” a “straight-up pure love song about my boyfriend” written during a writer’s retreat to Jamaica which Zara’s partner joined her for. “Hot and Sexy” is a “Frankenstein-ed, three songs-in-one” Brazilian funk banger co-produced by Zhone about hitting the town with your friends and the importance of leaving women unbothered. “It’s a bop, but there’s also that message at the end: can’t we just live our lives? Can’t a woman just be beautiful, fly, hot, and sexy? Let her do what she wants!” “Throughout Midnight Sun,” Zara says, “I get to just capture that total Scandinavian vibe, which is something that I have grown up with—it's a huge part of me, my happiest memories and my saddest ones, too. A part of my soul is a Swedish summer night. This record encompasses that, how life is so beautiful it makes you cry.” “But it just feels like me—knowing myself, this album is just really, really me. And also,” she says with a grin, “No one can do me the way I can.”
activity_description_1665968607072693620: Standing out from the masses with his daring and captivating productions, Newcastle-based Ben Hemsley is a force to be reckoned with. Ben Hemsley is one of the hottest ticket in the UK house and techno scene right now. In 2024 Ben sold out a 12,500 ticket headline show in Liverpool on the Pier Head, one of the largest headline shows a DJ has ever performed in the city. Prior to this Ben also sold out Manchester's Iconic Warehouse Project ludicrously fast with general on sale lasting 5 minutes! This was just one of nine shows that made up Ben’s CONNECTION TOUR, a run of shows at the best venues in each city in the UK. Ben sold out the entire tour, selling close to 30,000 tickets in the process. Ben Hemsley has cemented himself as one of Ibiza’s most notable DJs. Back to back residencies at Ibiza Rocks in 2023 & 2024 marked Ben’s intent on the White Isle, both years were hugely successful and allowed Ben to bring his own production & style to the island. 2025 was his most successful season yet; A 16 week residency at Amnesia curating the Terrace every Monday. A dream from the very beginning for Ben and a testament for things to come. With luring melodies and flavours of old school rave nostalgia, Ben’s records have been highly coveted by the leading labels in dance music, with signings on Ministry of Sound, Armada Music, Arcane, Repopulate Mars, Stress, Sola & more, not to mention his own imprint Bebé. Inspired by an early exposure to his mothers passion for 90’s dance music, Ben’s originality has turned the heads of some of the biggest names in the scene such as Calvin Harris, Tiesto, Fatboy Slim, Deborah De Luca, Green Velvet & Fisher to name a few. His tantalising skills as a producer came to light in 2021 with hit ‘Through 2 You’, followed by his anthem ‘Erase Me’ a year later. 2025 saw Ben release his club anthem “If Your Girl” on Ministry of Sound, which in the months leading up to its release was one of the most played tracks across the festival circuit in the UK. Accolades include DJ Mag’s No.1 British DJ of the year in 2023, alongside numerous nominations from BBC Radio 1, such as Breakthrough Artist and multiple "Hottest Record" features for his popular tracks. Not just a talent producer, Ben also decided to create and launch his own label bebé with the aim of creating a space to delve deeper into his influences and become a tastemaker carving out his own scene and shining light on up and coming, like-minded artists. Widely renowned as one of the hottest talents in dance music today, Ben strides confidently into 2026 excelling in every way he can.
activity_description_1665968609102736756: Like all great pop stars, JADE doesn't believe in doing things by halves. Once it was announced that Little Mix – the award-winning, record-breaking British girlband she was a part of – were going on hiatus in 2022, JADE immediately got to work on meticulously building her solo era. Released last September, her debut album That's Showbiz Baby!, featuring a cherry-picked selection of collaborators including Oscar Görres (Troye Sivan), Mike Sabath (RAYE) and Cirkut (Lady Gaga), peaked at number 3 in the UK, securing 2025's biggest opening week for a debut album in the process. Fusing elevated lyrical concepts about the fickleness of fame, the battle between the ego and id, and the self-sabotaging nature of the human brain, with bold and unrelenting bangers that pushed pop's envelope, it quickly established JADE as the force to be reckoned with. “I knew I wanted to be the pop girlie,” she said in 2024. “I'm obsessed with pop, I always will be, so it was how do I become the next pop girlie that does stand out and has something different.” Understanding that pop also needs to be popular, the album was trailed by a spectacular run of attention-grabbing, head-spinning singles, including the commercial and critical smash, Angel of My Dreams (a UK top 10 and Guardian single of the year), the shimmering disco of Fantasy (complete with a video directed by legendary visual experimentalist David LaChapelle), and the sleek electropop throb of Plastic Box, which was crowned winner of the prestigious Popjustice £20 Music Prize. It wasn't the only award to be popped on JADE's mantlepiece either; at the 2025 Brit Awards she went home with the Best Pop Act statuette (she's up for the same award this year, as well as British Artist of the Year), while Rolling Stone UK hailed her as music's trailblazer. This notion of trailblazing is thrown around a lot in music, but in JADE's case there's evidence to back up the claims. She could have played it safe with her debut solo single, but instead chose to follow the likes of post-Spice Girls Geri and post-No Doubt Gwen Stefani by making as big a statement as possible. “From the off I think it's important to put your flag in the sand to be like 'this is what I'm doing',” JADE has said. “My worst nightmare is for someone to hear my song and go 'that's nice'.”Released in summer 2024, Angel of My Dreams still sounds like the future, an audacious, unrelenting mix of a distorted Sandie Shaw sample, delicious swipes at her TV talent show past, and a throbbing electroclash-esque music backbone that screams sweat- soaked drama. It arrived with an audacious Aube Perrie-directed video that referenced everything from the Fifth Element to Britney's Lucky video, while its concepts were mirrored in a show-stealing performance at the Brit awards. The single's reach spread outside of pop too when Florence Welch – who had previously cited the song as an influence on her band's Everybody Scream album – covered it on BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge in 2025. As more singles followed, with each one tackling different pop genres and aspects of JADE's songwriting nous (see the RAYE-assisted fever dream that is FUFN (Fuck You for Now)), thoughts turned to the live shows. Again, JADE had no interest in dumbing down her vision. Dancers, props and an unquenchable party atmosphere cemented stand out performances at various summer festivals, including a politically-charged Glastonbury 2025 set at a heaving Woodsies stage and a celebration of queer joy at south London's Mighty Hoopla. Her Glastonbury performance included a new song, the gloriously camp Gossip with Australian duo Confidence Man, a collaboration that would be followed by musical hook-ups with US superstar Kesha (on BOY CRAZY), rising British star Rose Gray (on heavenly mash-up Angel of Satisfaction) and pop connoisseur PinkPantheress on her star-studded remix project, with JADE joining the likes of Kylie, Zara Larsson and SEVENTEEN. In October, JADE kickstarted a critically-acclaimed sold-out UK tour, celebrating the music she'd crafted and luxuriating in the world of the album she'd sketched out all those years before. Having already given fans an overload of high-art pop music and visuals, JADE didn't stop there; in December, she released That's Showbiz Baby! The Encore, which as well as including her spectacular cover of Madonna's Frozen, also featured seven brand new songs. Once again, the full range of pop was covered, from the stomping LGBTQIA+ love letter, Church, to the rave anthems of Use Me and If My Heart Was a House. Expect a clutch of these newer songs to appear on the setlist for JADE's forthcoming North American tour, which includes sold-out dates at LA's Hollywood Palladium, and a European jaunt that includes two dates at Amsterdam's Paradiso as well as stops in Paris, Berlin and Milan. For a British pop act to tour the UK on their debut album is rare, but for that tour to be followed by treks across America and Europe is rarer still. But then JADE isn't like other pop stars, and she's also not one to play by the rules. She'd rather make them bend to her will. From the very outset, the That's Showbiz Baby! campaign has been anchored by a desire to push the boundaries, from Angel of My Dream's sonic Blitzkrieg, to the eye- popping visuals, to the full-tilt live shows. “I'm very much a kitchen sink girl, I throw it all in,” JADE said in 2024, and the point still stands. “When I look at a pop girl I want the looks, the concepts, the big show, the glam. Everything.” This is JADE's moment, and she's just getting started... But what an introduction it's been so far.
activity_description_1665968609765436788: Loyle Carner is one of his generation’s most important artists. First emerging with 2013’s *A Little Late* EP, he quickly established a singular voice, pairing diaristic, emotionally candid lyricism with ambitious, genre-blurring production. His debut album *Yesterday’s Gone* (2017) explored grief and coming of age, while *Not Waving, but Drowning* (2019) sharpened his gift for marrying introspective rap with old-soul insight. Twice shortlisted for the Mercury Prize and nominated for BRIT and NME Awards, Carner has built a devoted global following, amassing over 1.1 billion streams and selling out major London venues including Alexandra Palace, Wembley Arena and the Royal Albert Hall. His third album, *hugo*, culminated in a landmark 2024 headline show at All Points East and delivered his second UK Top 3 record. In 2025, Carner enters a new chapter with his fourth album *hopefully !*, a life-affirming exploration of fatherhood, childhood and alternative music, alongside his Glastonbury headline debut and first acting role in BBC drama *Mint*.
activity_description_1665968610394582388: Built in Dublin, Ireland. Lorcan McCarthy and Faustas Astrauskas have been meticulously building their own unique sound since 2019. From early success through mega track ‘Bayside’ right up to the current evolution to becoming one of dance musics most promising names. Massive productions like “I’ve Arrived” and “Seen it All Before” have put the pair at the very pinnacle of house music right now. Releases on Eastenderz and NeXup digging deep into house culture - and huge remixes of “The One” by Chloe Caillet and a rework of the classic “Beautiful People” by Barbara Tucker has shown the duos depth. On the live side - Obskür are taking their place on line-ups across the globe. From now iconic sets at venues like The Warehouse Project, Drumsheds, Space Miami and Amnesia to becoming a frequent fixture at parties like Paradise / After Caposile / PIV and Parklife. Kicking things up a level by introducing the world to their very own concept ‘The System’ this year - the duo going on to sell out all 9 shows of the debut tour across the UK & Ireland which saw them play the opening and closing set. Unorthodox. Unpredictable. Turning heads. This is only the beginning."
activity_description_1665968611057282420: Role Model (Tucker Pillsbury) first made waves with his 2022 debut album Rx, a confessional and genre-blurring pop record that introduced him as a bold new voice in alternative music. With his sophomore album Kansas Anymore, Role Model showcases his evolution as a songwriter and performer with 13 folk-tinged, lyrically driven tracks. Working alongside Noah Conrad, Ian Fitchuk, Scott Harris, and Jonah Shy, he crafted standout pieces including the viral hit “Sally, When the Wine Runs Out,” which he performed on Saturday Night Live. Following the success of his No Place Like Tour, which sold over 90,000 tickets worldwide, he released a deluxe edition, Kansas Anymore (The Longest Goodbye), featuring four new songs that expand the emotional and sonic scope of the original album. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Pillsbury is stepping into the world of acting with his debut role in Good Sex, the upcoming Netflix film from Lena Dunham, starring opposite Natalie Portman and Mark Ruffalo.
activity_description_1665968612407848308: The Mary Wallopers - brothers Charles and Andrew Hendy and their friend Sean McKenna - are a rabble-rousing three-piece Irish ballad group who started out traveling the length and breadth of the country singing & collecting songs. Their early live performances exuded a raw energy that could be best described as Dead Kennedys meets The Clancy Brothers. When COVID decimated the music industry and canceled all live music, the first band out of the blocks were The Mary Wallopers. Unfazed by the global shutdown, the three Dundalk men built a pub/studio in their house to connect with their fans again. On St. Patrick's Day 2020 they became one of the first bands in the world to host a livestream. Although there were countless attempts to get livestreaming right during the pandemic, very few matched the Wallopers efforts. Armed with a DIY attitude, they performed live in their homemade clubhouse, creating broadcasts that felt like Wayne's World soundtracked entirely by Irish ballads. The show brought some much needed joy to the 40,000 people who tuned in live. As the streams continued, their audiences both home and abroad grew, allowing them to book their first UK headline tour. To capture the chaotic energy of the livestream, the Wallopers expanded to a seven-piece, including bass, drums, accordion and tin whistle. When lockdown restrictions lifted, the band picked up where they left off, playing to ecstatic audiences of 1500 people a night at two sold out gigs at the prestigious Vicar Street in Dublin before blazing a trail through the UK, ending up with a raucous sold out date at the Powerhaus in Camden. With their debut album on the way in October and a massive tour of Ireland/UK and Europe, The Mary Wallopers are taking their unique and joyous vision of the historic music of their home country out into the world.
activity_description_1665968613078936948: The crowd are chanting N17 even before The Saw Doctors come on stage in a hot, jam-packed Electric Arena. The stage is a busy one, a great mixture of saxophone, guitars, accordions and backing vocalists, creating a fantastic carnival of sound. The Saw Doctors are powered by song writers Davy Carton (vocals) and Leo Moran (guitar) with a lineup that includes former Waterboy Anthony Thistlethwaite on saxophone, Rickie O’Neill, drums, Pearse Doherty, bass guitar and penny whistle, Kieran Duddy, keyboards, Noelie McDonnell and Tommy Carton, backing vocals. When The Saw Doctors play ’To Win Just Once’, the crowd are singing the lyrics so hard and loud that the band could take a breather if they wanted to. Some of the biggest reactions come during 'Joyce Country Céilí Band' and ‘I Useta Lover’, songs by now ingrained in almost every Irish person’s subconscious. A last burst of energy reverberates around the tent when Davy Carton shouts “here we go”- 10,000 fans singing the chorus “I wish I was on the N17’. If The Saw Doctors could bottle the sort of bonhomie that can make an entire arena feel better, they would have the medicine show to end them all.
activity_description_1665968613766802804: North London quartet Wolf Alice first emerged in 2013 with the bruised euphoria of their debut album My Love Is Cool, which featured the Grammy-nominated ‘Moaning Lisa Smile’. 2018’s follow up Visions Of A Life cemented their rise with a Mercury Music Prize win, before the precious hurt of 2022’s Blue Weekend and its resultant number 1 in the UK album charts and Brit Award for Best Group. August 29th, 2025 will see the release of Wolf Alice’s fourth album The Clearing via their new global label home, Sony Music and finds them at the peak of their powers, grown into a band of significant cultural importance. Written in Seven Sisters, North London and recorded in LA with Grammy-winning, master producer Greg Kurstin last year, The Clearing reveals where Wolf Alice stand sonically in 2025, delivering a supremely confident collection of songs bursting with ambition, ideas and emotion; The Clearing is a truly timeless record. Both playful and serious, ironic and straight-talking,The Clearing is a progressive shift from a band whose exploration of love, loss and human connection has already articulated the coming-of-age experience for a whole generation. It’s a classic pop/rock album that nods to the ‘70s while remaining rooted firmly in the present. If Fleetwood Mac wrote an album today in North London, you’d get somewhere close to this run of effortlessly grand tracks, each as distinct as the last. Sonically, there is no waste, no fuss, with more authoritative melodies than the band has ever crafted before. This is a new beginning, and each of the band feels it as keenly as listeners will. Across their career, Wolf Alice have toured the world multiple times on headline sold out tours, gracing numerous festival stages and supporting an array of key artists. This summer so far sees confirmed slots at Radio 1’s Big Weekend and Glastonbury with a huge headline world tour scheduled for the end of 2025.
activity_description_1665968615117368692: In a landscape often bound by formulaic conventions, ADÉLA emerges as an artist who refuses to conform. The 21-year-old singer doesn’t just make pop music — she distorts it, challenges it, and makes it feel larger than life, yet always rooted in unfiltered emotion. “I want to create a world that's relatable on a human level,” she says. “I want to talk about things that are maybe uncomfortable. That’s who I am also as a person: I’m super blunt and kind of clinical, in a sense. Feelings, both positive and negative, hold the same weight to me.” That balance between grandeur and sincerity is central to her debut EP The Provocateur for Capitol Records. It tells the story of a woman who’s willing to do anything to become an entertainer, a dramatized yet deeply personal reflection of ADÉLA’s journey. Like dispatches from the frontlines of fame and ambition, each track marks a chapter in the character’s rise, from the feverish “Homewrecked” — a recounting of infidelity and betrayal — to the defiant “Superscar,” a statement on power, exploitation, and perseverance. “It’s about messed up things happening to you when you want to do this,” she explains. “It’s about her being like, ‘You didn't make me a superstar, you gave me a superscar. But I’ll keep going.’” On her EP track “MachineGirl,” ADÉLA sharpens that narrative through its biting social commentary on the spectacle of female conflict — how, despite purportedly embracing a culture of “women supporting women,” audiences still revel in watching them tear each other down. Produced and co-signed by Grimes, it’s satire drawn from ADÉLA’s own experience in the lion’s den, powered by high-voltage synths, vocoder harmonies, juvenile taunts, and her response to the drama: “Why you comin’ at me, baby? / Yell at the machine, girl.” ADÉLA knows what it means to be shaped by the machine and to fight against it. Raised in Slovakia, the singer, born Adéla Jergova, often felt at odds with her homeland’s conservative values. “In Eastern Europe, we often think in a very limited way,” she says before elaborating. “We don’t see ourselves as worthy or able to achieve huge things because it simply has never happened before.” Rather than allow others to discourage her childhood dream of becoming a pop star, she kept it to herself. ADÉLA channeled that energy into years of rigorous ballet training, her natural talent and unrivaled work ethic driving her to go professional at age 11. By 14, she had moved to Vienna and London to attend elite ballet academies, but when music’s pull became too strong to ignore, she left to pursue it full-time. Outside of school, she studied American pop culture obsessively. “I was like, If I want to be on the Disney Channel, I need to be able to speak perfect English," she says. So every day, ADÉLA taught herself by watching hours of makeup tutorials and celebrity interviews on YouTube, mimicking the way the people on screen spoke. She also took vocal lessons — going as far as successfully seeking out Olivia Rodrigo’s teacher — and eventually began songwriting as a means of processing the growing pains of adolescence. In 2020, ADÉLA’s self-made education led her to her biggest challenge yet. She moved to Los Angeles to join the Dream Academy, where she competed for a spot in a global girl group — a years-long process documented in the Netflix series Pop Star Academy. It was a demanding yet invaluable experience that schooled her thoroughly in the principles of being a performer, reinforcing the discipline, resilience, and artistry she’d been perfecting since childhood. But after pouring everything she had into the competition, ADÉLA was ultimately eliminated. The aftermath was brutal. “The year that followed was the worst of my life,” she says. “Seriously. It sucked.” With no clear path forward, she took the time to experiment, make music, and rediscover who she was outside of the program. “I had to find my people, try different vibes, hair colors, clothes, and just live life.” ADÉLA emerged from that period of reinvention sharper, hungrier, and fully in control of her vision. She’s hands-on in every aspect of her work outside of her music, too, from video treatments and choreography to costuming and makeup — something she can credit to a lifelong study of her musical heroes, Beyoncé and Lady Gaga, and also her years in ballet watching how all the elements came together. As she steps into this new chapter of her career, she thinks back to her time rebuilding. Just as she had set out as a child to learn English and become a Disney star, she opened up a Google Doc and hatched a plan, starting with a written mission statement in answer to one specific question: What does ADÉLA, the artist, want? “I just want to encourage people to fucking be themselves — unless you're a psychopath,” she jokes, before thoughtfully adding: “If I do my job right, people will love these songs because they’ll find themselves in them.” The release of The Provocateur in August of 2025 confirmed ADÉLA’s arrival, garnering her praise from outlets such as Vogue, Interview Magazine, The FADER, Harper’s Bazaar, NYLON, Rolling Stone and PAPER Magazine, the last of which declared that her “fame comes at no surprise.” With this acclaim in tow, ADÉLA quickly sold out her debut solo live performances in London, New York, and Los Angeles. Next year, she’ll take her electrifying stage presence on the road, opening for Demi Lovato on her North American tour starting April 2026. As her rapidly growing fanbase anxiously anticipates her next body of work, it’s clear to see that the sky is the only limit for the rising pop star.
activity_description_1665968615788457332: Audrey Hobert is an American singer-songwriter at just 26 years old. She released her debut album “Who’s the Clown?” on August 15, featuring 12 songs featuring Sue me which was her breakout first single. Audrey enjoys writing, reading, and surfing the net.
activity_description_1665968616476323188: Florence Road are rapidly becoming one of the most talked-about new bands in the world. Making the longlist for the BBC Sound of 2026 poll and earning praise from major publications, the Wicklow four-piece have built a devoted audience of over one million followers before their debut mixtape had even dropped. Bringing a distinct sound that intertwines soft and loud, tender and explosive, Florence Road create music that is both enigmatic and compelling. Fronted by Lily Aron, alongside Emma Brandon (guitar), Ailbhe Barry (bass), and Hannah Kelly (drums), the band’s close-knit connection translates into performances that feel raw, real, and magnetic. After teasing their sound through a rapid run of singles and viral clips, Florence Road have revealed impressive lyrical depth and musical confidence. Their songs explore the anxieties, intensity, humour, and heartbreak of youth, shifting fluidly between indie rock, grunge, and alt-pop, while remaining grounded in emotion and fearlessness.
activity_description_1665968617155800436: As the end of the first quarter of the 21st century inches ever closer, our planet precariously teeters from one crisis to the next. Rather than passively sit back and watch, the high-energy Irish guitar quintet Gurriers are firing on all cylinders and confronting the ills of the modern world on their debut album, Come and See, a truly thrilling collection of razor-sharp progressive punk songs. Recorded in Leeds at the Nave with Alex Greaves, Come and See blasts off to an explosive start with “Nausea”, giving the concept of Jean Paul Sartre's classic novel of the same name a furious sonic makeover. Guitars screech like sirens, creating a curiously catchy clarion call for an album of raucous reflection. Come and See explores many themes, be they the end of the world, the disenfranchised youth of Dublin, emigrant friends, the rise of the far right, desensitisation to violence, a pope struggling with belief and love amongst other things. “Nausea” examine how existential mundanity in the 21st century is now essentially lived in the digital realm, and society has blindly sleepwalked into this actuality without realising the full extent of its corrosive damage. Underpaid and overworked content moderators are forced to watch unspeakable horrors, as social media platforms drip feed its users dopamine, further distracting an already overstimulated and distorted cartoonish world from the harsh glare of too much reality. “Des Goblin” channels the hypnotic energy of dance music and notes how modern narcissism is fuelled by an addiction to online personas. “Close Call” turns up the ferocious guitar intensity to eleven, a fierce hybrid of guitar pop with industrial techno sensibilities. “Dipping Out” is like a post-post-punk version of an Adam Curtis documentary, as the band cite his classic HyperNormalisation as a major source of inspiration. One line perfectly nails the disillusionment of contemporary youth, "Failed by a system that never really lets you exist.” Indeed, if Gurriers weren’t in a band they’d probably be part of a generation leaving Ireland in their droves, driven out by the soaring cost of living and the unattainability of home ownership, left to “live in debt and die in freedom”. “No More Photos” opens with the memorable line, "Gentlemen, no fighting in the bathroom please. You've been caught doing too many Es” and proceeds to reference Caravaggio. Following a brief instrumental respite, simply titled “Interlude”, the album closes with a breathtaking final flourish of songs and a soaring title track, which tantalisingly hints towards an even more expansive, wide-screen sound for a future chapter. “Approachable” is a tongue-in-cheek anthem mourning the rise of the far right (“Damn, I was born in the wrong era”) that kicks off with a monstrous killer riff. “Top Of The Bill” combines an intricate guitar melody with blasts of noise and a knockout chorus, a live favourite and perfect example of how well Gurriers craft inimitable and intense pop music. Taking their name from an antiquated and somewhat charming Irish term for lout, ruffian, or street urchin, Gurriers formed in January 2020, initially comprising Dan Hoff on lead vocals, Ben O'Neill on guitar and backing vocals, Mark MacCormack on guitar, Pierce O'Callaghan on drums and Emmet White on bass, who has since amicably left the band and been replaced by Charlie McCarthy. Hailing from various parts of Ireland, Gurriers met in Dublin. They believed they were destined to connect creatively in a meaningful way, so they formed a band. We don’t need to dwell too much on how events in early 2020 temporarily stalled their progress. "All we wanted to do was be back in a room together and practice," Dan Hoff recalls. "I remember one stage screaming into my pillow because of the extended lockdowns.” Instead of doom scrolling on their phones, baking banana bread, or bingeing on box sets, Gurriers seized an opportunity to hone their vision and advance their ambition. Over numerous Zoom calls, they meticulously discussed every single aspect of the band, plotting strategies at a time when venues, studios, and rehearsal rooms were shuttered shut. The silence spurned the fledgling group on to make a bigger, more beautifully abrasive noise. Thanks to a productive pandemic, when Gurriers played their first gig on Halloween 2021 at Dublin's Workman's Club, they'd evolved remarkably as a band. On the back of earlier singles including “Sign of The Times” and “Nausea”, they have received the seal of approval from The Needle Drop's legendary Anthony Fantano and prestigious support from Steve Lamacq and Huw Stephens of BBC Radio 6 Music culminating in their most recent single “Des Goblin” making it up to BBC Radio 6 Music’s A-List at 6, not bad for an unsigned band self-releasing their own music. Gurriers played festivals throughout Europe and beyond, including SWN, Mad Cool, Reeperbahn, Left of the Dial, London Calling, Latitude, Haldern Pop, Off, The Great Escape, Pukkelpop, Pitchfork Music Festival London, Electric Picnic and All Together Now. Scheduled to play South by Southwest in Austin, Texas last March, Gurriers pulled out alongside virtually all other Irish participants, boycotting the event due to its sponsorship by the US Army. This October, Gurriers will embark on their biggest tour to date in support of their blistering debut. Inspired by timeless first records by The Strokes, Arctic Monkeys, The Chemical Brothers, and Black Midi, Gurriers' first album is no ordinary debut, but an exhilarating statement of intent by five people fed up with tiptoeing politely around the chaos.
activity_description_1665968617818500468: In 2024, Jessie Murph released her debut album That Ain’t No Man That’s the Devil—a certified Gold project that chased her 2023 mixtape Drowning—and ignited what quickly became Jessie’s signature sound. With raw and honest lyrics, mixed with a voice that lives where soul and grit collide, Jessie turned personal tragedy into a genre-blending triumph. The momentum was massive: That Ain’t No Man That’s the Devil cracked the Top 25 on the Billboard 200, while the Platinum “Wild Ones” racked up nearly 300M Spotify streams alone, scoring her two 2024 MTV VMA nods including Best Pop Collaboration and Best PUSH Artist. Other standouts like “Someone In This Room” with Bailey Zimmerman and “High Road” ft. Koe Wetzel marked their strongest chart debuts to date—landing at #29 on the Billboard Hot 100 and hitting #1 at Billboard Country Radio, respectively. But Jessie Murph doesn’t sit still. She headlined a sold-out global tour, packing over 85,000 tickets, including Coachella, Governors Ball, Boston Calling, BottleRock, and a proud return to Hangout Fest. Her In The Sticks North American tour closed with a hometown arena blowout—10,000 fans deep at Huntsville’s Von Braun Center. In July of 2025, she kicked off her largest tour to date, the WORLDWIDE HYSTERIA tour, currently on the North American trek the tour will also hit Europe, and Australia before concluding in New Zealand in November. Her sophomore album Sex Hysteria, which debuted at #8 on the Billboard 200 chart, is her vice-laden manifesto where Jessie trades sorrow for sensation. It’s dopamine in album form—part ‘60s Pop, part early-2000s Trap, yet entirely Jessie. The album debuted at #8 on the Billboard 200 Chart, marking her first top 10 album on the chart. The record’s early breakout “Blue Strips” featuring Sexyy Red skyrocketed her to her highest Billboard Hot 100 peak yet at #15, while “Gucci Mane” (the song) became an underground fan anthem. “Touch Me Like A Gangster” debuted at #56 on the Billboard Hot 100, which saw Jessie chart 2 songs in the top half of the Hot 100 simultaneously. The album also sees real-life Gucci Mane tap in for the bouncy “Donuts,” while Lil Baby’s moody turn on “Best Behavior” is a smooth addition. She also celebrates a nomination for New Female Artist of the Year at the 2025 Academy of Country Music Awards and Favorite Country Song at the 2025 American Music Awards. Sex Hysteria isn’t about what happened to Jessie. It’s about what Jessie’s about to do. From viral TikToks to sold-out tours to genre-defying records, Jessie Murph has made a name for herself without ever chasing fame. What she’s chasing is freedom—and she’s finally caught it.
activity_description_1665968619135511924: Oklou’s deluxe edition of *choke enough* builds on the album’s warm production and its blend of ambient textures with minimal club rhythms. The expanded release adds four new tracks, further widening its immersive universe, including the standout single *“viscus”* featuring FKA twigs. The announcement follows a striking Tiny Desk performance and a Pitchfork cover story tracing Oklou’s breakthrough year and artistic evolution. Alongside a recent appearance on PinkPantheress’ remix album, *choke enough* has been named one of the best albums of the year by Rolling Stone, Pitchfork and Billboard, and won France’s Prix Joséphine Album of the Year. High-profile admirers include Billie Eilish and Ethel Cain. Born Marylou Mayniel in rural western France, Oklou trained in classical piano and cello before embracing electronic production in Paris. Since her 2020 mixtape *Galore*, she has emerged as one of modern music’s most compelling voices, balancing intimacy, innovation and emotional clarity.
activity_description_1665968619789823348: Ravyn Lenae has risen from Chicago’s South Side to become one of the most distinctive voices in modern R&B and pop. Over the past decade, she has developed a fluid, genre-blurring sound—pulling from house, synth-funk and soul—across acclaimed EPs *Moon Shoes*, *Midnight Moonlight* and *Crush*, and albums *Hypnos* and *Bird’s Eye*. Her 2024 sophomore album *Bird’s Eye*, executive produced with GRAMMY winner Dahi, marked a major breakthrough. Led by the global hit *Love Me Not*—co-written with Anderson .Paak—the album earned widespread acclaim and propelled Lenae into the mainstream, alongside collaborations with Childish Gambino and Ty Dolla $ign. Critics praised its adventurous scope and Lenae’s unmistakable, airy soprano. A commanding live performer, Lenae has toured with SZA and Omar Apollo, made her Coachella and Lollapalooza debuts in 2025, and is now headlining sold-out North American shows while supporting Sabrina Carpenter and Reneé Rapp.
activity_description_1665968620486077812: Skye Newman is one of the UK’s most striking new voices, transforming raw talent and lived experience into a fast-rising career. Born and raised on South London council estates, the 21-year-old has turned an extraordinary vocal and fearless storytelling into a breakout moment, becoming the first UK female solo artist in over a decade to score two Top 20 debut singles. Her debut *Hairdresser* went Silver and spent 14 weeks in the Top 40, followed by *Family Matters*, a Gold-certified Top 5 hit that resonated deeply for its unflinching honesty. Skye’s ascent has been fuelled by a fiercely engaged online following and powerful live performances, from sold-out London and Manchester headline shows to appearances at Reading & Leeds, Radio 1’s Big Weekend, and arena tours supporting Ed Sheeran and Lewis Capaldi. Her debut project *SE9: Part 1* reflects on upbringing, trauma and self-worth with soulful pop clarity, cementing Skye Newman as an artist of rare authenticity and emotional impact, and one firmly tipped for 2026.
activity_description_1665968621140389236: Bleech 9:3 were born from shared survival as much as shared sound. Songwriters and guitarists Barry Quinlan and Sam Duffy met in their early twenties while in recovery, discovering near-identical lives shaped by addiction, music and ambition in Dublin. What began as mutual support quickly became a creative lifeline, with songwriting offering purpose, clarity and a way forward. Completed by James Quinlan (bass) and Luke O’Neill (drums), Bleech 9:3 have rapidly emerged as one of the most vital new live acts on the circuit. After relocating to London, the band built momentum through relentless gigging, sold-out headline shows and high-profile support slots in 2025, culminating in a standout residency at London’s Blue Basement. With only a handful of singles, their sound—melding heavy distortion with sharp melody—draws on influences from Radiohead and Nirvana to Fontaines D.C. Breakthrough track *Jacky* confronts addiction head-on, crystallising the band’s raw intensity and fearless intent. As new material arrives and touring intensifies, Bleech 9:3 stand as proof that reinvention can be both brutal and brilliant.
activity_description_1665968621811477876: It’s been a busy and exciting few months for Cliffords as they introduced themselves to the wider world with their second EP, Salt of the Lee. It’s the sound of a band who made their initial moves outside of the glare of the music industry, and whose self-financed debut EP landed with much promise but without any pressure of expectation beyond their own. Salt of the Lee fulfils all that promise emphatically, and another thrilling next step for a band who are quickly on the rise. Whilst Cliffords certainly continue to develop and discover both themselves as a band and their sound, they’ve already become a compelling proposition whose word-of-mouth live shows are the sound of a band on the brink of something very special
activity_description_1665968622474177908: Some artists don’t ask permission, they just land in your gut and stay there. Rising London four-piece Keo have spent the past year proving they belong firmly in the latter camp. After a breakout 2025 that saw their debut EP Siren captivate critics and fans alike, and their first October UK + Ireland tour sell out entirely, Keo now announce their most ambitious chapter yet: a 14-date headline tour spanning March and April 2026, that marks their biggest shows to date and their first step onto European stages. Since the release of Siren, Keo have fast become one of the UK’s most visceral and uncompromising new bands. Across five tracks, from the blistering honesty of debut single ‘I Lied, Amber’ to the aching centrepiece ‘Hands’, 21-year-old frontman Finn Keogh led listeners through the emotional wreckage of youth, identity, and recovery with a rawness that resonated far beyond expectation. Support from Rolling Stone UK, NME, Wonderland, DIY, Dork, Clash, alongside spins across BBC Radio 1 and more, propelled the band from London’s underground to sold-out rooms and festival stages across the UK
activity_description_1665968623178820980: Madra Salach met whilst playing in different outfits on the city's indie scene and bonded over a shared love of the Irish traditional canon which led to them playing impromptu pub sessions. Taking inspiration from the growing experimental folk scene in Ireland, the group added members, instruments and electronic elements to emerge with their own compositions, which are at the same time strikingly modern and written with a voice that could have emerged at any point throughout the last century. Their January 26 debut EP It’s a Hell of an Age blended original songs with reimagined traditional material and reached No. 3 in Ireland and the UK Independent Albums Top 10. Now signed to Island Records, Madra Salach are building strong momentum through festival appearances, sold-out Ireland and UK headline tours and collaborations including upcoming album The Songs of Shane MacGowan out November 26 which includes Bruce Springsteen, Primal Scream, Lisa O’Neill among others.
activity_description_1665968623824743796: Amidst the UK and Ireland music scene one name continues to captivate both newcomers and devoted fans alike: Nieve Ella. She has already gained supporters in BBC Radio 1’s Greg James and Jack Saunders, alongside praise from NME, Rolling Stone UK, DORK and more. With over 20 million streams to date, and back to back sold out UK/EU headline tours including stops at KOKO (London) and New Century Hall (Manchester), Ella’s potent indie-rock confessionals, seamlessly melded with the ambience of 90’s guitar, continue to resonate with her hyper-engaged fan base. She is now poised to continue her impressive rise in 2026.
activity_description_1665968624487443828: People I’ve Met is an alternative rock band based in New York City featuring Moses Martin on lead vocals and guitar, Orlando Wiltshire on drums, and Andrew Suster on bass.
activity_description_1665968625166921076: Rose Gray knows that one perfect night at the club can make you feel reborn. Louder, Please, the long-awaited debut album from the London-based singer, songwriter and DJ bottles up the feeling of that one perfect night – the new faces and the new loves, the invigorating new sounds and the tears that look like glitter under dancefloor lights. Comprised of euphoric electronic pop and spine-tingling maximalist club music, Louder, Please announces Gray as a masterful chronicler of life’s ecstatic highs and soul-crushing lows. Inspired by icons she loves like Robyn, Kylie Minogue and Madonna circa Ray of Light, Gray’s storytelling and lyricism locate everyday truth in big-room anthems. Born in Walthamstow, East London, Rose Gray has been a musician her whole life. Left cold by her early experiences in the industry, she found the club. This is Gray’s ode to the transformative, life-changing nature of a good party. On Louder, Please, Rose Gray reveals herself as a canny bridger between the worlds of club music and pop music, conjuring the feeling of one of the greatest nights out ever.
activity_description_1665968625829621108: Tyler Ballgame’s debut album *For the First Time, Again* introduces a gifted vocalist and songwriter whose journey is as compelling as his songs. Raised in New England by a classically trained music teacher, Ballgame knew early he was meant to sing. Encouraged by mentors at Berklee College of Music, he pursued music relentlessly, though early post-college projects failed to gain traction. During the pandemic, isolated and struggling in Rhode Island, Ballgame reached a turning point. Playing cover-band gigs while battling self-doubt, he made a leap of faith—moving sight unseen to Los Angeles to start over. There, open mics and a growing local community reignited his confidence and creative spark. His remarkable voice and heartfelt songwriting soon caught the attention of producers Jonathan Rado and Ryan Pollie, leading to the creation of *For the First Time, Again*, recorded live to tape with a classic, analog sensibility. The album reflects Ballgame’s rebirth—an artist betting on himself, embracing risk, and finding connection through music rooted in belief, vulnerability, and hope.
activity_description_1665968626542652788: Interplanetary Criminal is the Manchester-based producer, DJ and ATW Records co-founder leading a rip-roaring new wave of UK garage. Straight from the studio to the iconic Arcadia spider, and from Dekmantel to Depot Mayfield, Croatia, Bogotá, Sydney, Miami and all-nighters at Leeds’ beloved Wire, IPC and his speedy, rowdy sets – and speedier, rowdier productions – are connecting with up-for-it audiences. His formula? Fresh, fun and foundation-minded, balancing innovation with a wholehearted appreciation for everything that’s come before, including the enduring influence of the North West. His dedication is paying off. Recent years have seen IPC (real name Zach Bruce) earn DJ Mag’s Best of British awards for Best Producer and Best Track, along with a Brit Award nomination. He’s played ecstatic b2bs with legends like Skream, remixed for formative heroes like Dusky and been a regular on Rinse FM. Not to mention all the music he’s created and shared, counting 2022’s celebratory “All Thru The Night” V/A compilation for the seminal Locked On label. Plus, of course, the chart-topping “B.O.T.A. (Baddest Of Them All)” – an irresistible collab with Eliza Rose. He’s been on a collaboration tip this year as well, releasing the sing-along, 00s-flavoured “No Time” (featuring Canadian artist SadBoi) and the icy, 2-step-meets-drill “Races” (with Harlem Spartans founder Blanco) via Room Two Recordings. And in the afterglow of another packed festival season, he’s just wrapped up a North and South American tour. The UK and Europe are next, with IPC’s hotly-tipped headline show at London’s HERE @ Outernet selling out in hours. It’s going to be a massive club autumn/winter. Perfectly aligned, then, with his new solo EP for ATW Records, which he launched in 2020 alongside Danish artist (and kindred spirit) Main Phase. If you were to ask IPC to describe “ATW007,” he’d say it’s “no-nonsense, brash, rudeboy energy,” primed for club usage and crafted specifically for his USB. The EP features an incendiary link-up with veteran MC Riko Dan (“Gunman”), IPC’s go-to set opener (“The Valley”) and a “classic speed garage” love letter to his hometown (“Manchester” – of course). Listening to it is like being plunged into a peak-time dancefloor, not just in how it sounds but in how it makes you feel – pulled into a crowd, locked in a groove, in the thick of something special. This new EP (much like IPC’s output at large) is dedicated to the underground, which makes total sense. When it comes to IPC personally – but also UKG more broadly – context and authenticity are everything. ATW Records champions that, aiming to capture the energy and perspectives of today’s garage scene while carving a distinct identity. For IPC, this is the key to all that he does: taking in, giving back and staying true to what he stands for.
activity_description_1665968627222130036: Over the last year, Irish DJ producer CamrinWatsin continued to build on the extraordinary momentum of his breakout year in 2024. Following the release of his track: “Kisses” - the record achieved multi-platinum certification in the UK alongside attaining platinum status in multiple countries across the globe, earning a BRIT Award nomination for Song Of The Year and hitting a height of over 10 million monthly listeners across streaming platforms. Live shows continued to grow from strength to strength for CamrinWatsin - consisting of two sold out shows in Dublin, a busy summer schedule with an Ibiza residency, as well as two touring runs across the globe in Australia and New Zealand. Stand out performances took place at Ireland’s Longitude Festival and major British electronic dance music festival Creamfields & finally concluding with a slot at Dublin’s premier live music venue, the 3Arena.
activity_description_1665968627876441460: Clouds are a Scottish techno/hardcore DJ and producer duo consisting of Liam Robertson and Calum Macleod. Known for their high-energy, "post-industrial" sound, they have garnered support from artists like Richie Hawtin and The Chemical Brothers. They frequently release on Speedy J's Electric Deluxe and have toured extensively since the early 2010s.
activity_description_1665968628564307316: DART is emerging as one of Irelands leading underground figures - a breakthrough year and a list of massive sets both at home and abroad has put the Dublin based producer high on the list of hard houses must see talents. The now iconic 'Emergency' put him on radars all over Europe and follow up anthems like 'Always & Forever' and 'Dance N Move' has kept the momentum moving at nuclear pace. Fresh off the back of a sold out Index show and a massive District X appeareance in Ireland - as well as now legendary sets all over Europe in Thuishaven Amsterdam, Mondo Disco in Madrid and Terminal V in Scotland - he sets his sights on Electric Picnic.
activity_description_1665968629277338996: Sophie “Effy” Cooper has quickly emerged as one of the most exciting new voices in UK club music. A producer, DJ, radio host and label founder from the North West of England, she has released four EPs, a run of acclaimed club singles and sold out headline tours across Europe, Australia and North America since her 2020 debut. Raised near Blackpool, Effy discovered DJing at house parties, drawing early influence from The Prodigy, The Chemical Brothers and pioneering producers like Maya Jane Coles. Her debut single *Fluffy Clouds* premiered via Mixmag, earned BBC Introducing Dance support and led to a residency on Rinse FM. Blending breaks, electro and UK bass, she quickly became known for high-impact club productions, playing venues and festivals including Fabric, Parklife, The Warehouse Project and Amnesia Ibiza, alongside support slots for Helena Hauff and Honey Dijon. Her debut EP *Not What It Seems* sparked international touring, followed by Boiler Room Sydney and the launch of Fragrance Recordings with Mall Grab. In 2025, Effy released *The Syndicate*, a punchy tribute to her Blackpool roots.
activity_description_1665968630720179572: Kayleigh Glynn is a rising DJ and producer hailing from Ringsend, Dublin. Known for her energetic sets and infectious passion for dance music, Kayleigh has quickly become a standout name in the Irish scene. Her talent has taken her far beyond the local circuit — with multiple appearances across the legendary party island of Ibiza, she’s brought her sound to international crowds. Back home, Kayleigh has earned her stripes supporting some of Ireland’s biggest names in dance music, including Belters Only, Jazzy, Kettama, and Dec Pierce. With her deep roots in the Dublin underground and a growing European footprint, Kayleigh Glynn is a name you’ll be hearing a lot more of.
activity_description_1665968631408045428: Duke Dumont has spent the last decade building one of the most successful and uncompromising careers in electronic music. With over 4 billion global streams and UK #1 singles like Need U (100%) and I Got U, his music has become both culturally resonant and club-defining. But chart success has never been the goal — it’s the byproduct of a deeper passion for dance music. Now fully immersed in evolving the live electronic experience, Dumont is forging a path few dare to follow. “I’m not concerned with playlists or charts,” he states. “My only focus is building the best live show I can, giving the best experience I can.” That ethos powers records like The Chant, a euphoric anthem built purely for the stage, and his long-running For Club Play Only series — a cult favorite that continues to shape his distinct sonic world.
activity_description_1665968632070745460: Men I Trust, a Canadian indie band formed in 2014, has quietly but profoundly left its mark on the music scene. Comprising Emma Proulx (guitar and vocals), Jessy Caron (guitar and bass), and Dragos Chiriac (keyboards), the trio’s enchanting sound, blending dream pop and indie elements, resonates with a global audience. Renowned for their hypnotic melodies and captivating vocals, the band has earned acclaim for their distinct approach to music. Self-producing their tracks, they showcase a maturity beyond their years in the industry. Men I Trust’s influence extends from their evocative compositions to their understated yet compelling live performances, offering audiences a genuine and intimate musical experience. In an era where music defies easy categorization, Men I Trust stands out for their ability to create a sound that transcends genres, shaping the indie music landscape with grace and authenticity.
activity_description_1665968633446477172: Galway songwriter Jamie McIntyre has enjoyed a breakthrough year, with his summer single “Over Galway Town” becoming a viral hit, amassing over 2.5 million Spotify streams and charting alongside some of the world’s biggest artists. The song’s success has carried his music far beyond Ireland and shows no signs of slowing. In 2024, McIntyre was hand-picked by Gavin James to support him in Paris on his European tour, leading to further opportunities including working with Imelda May and performing at Electric Picnic. He also joined Jamie Webster for sold-out shows in Dublin and Belfast. Momentum has continued into 2025, with McIntyre selling out his debut Irish tour in Dublin, Limerick, and Galway, before announcing larger shows for October. His recent EP, “Chapter 23”, has surpassed 750,000 streams, with tracks like “West Is Home” and “Grá” quickly becoming fan favourites.
activity_description_1665968634251783540: MALUGI’s happy place is the dance floor. That’s where his cheeky smile and penguin moves turned into global fan favorites, creating an infectious presence that earned him the title of “The Happiest Man in Dance Music.” But don’t let it fool you — underneath is a powerhouse ready to tear clubs apart without hesitation. Driven by pumping club productions and just the right amount of mass appeal, MALUGI has created a niche for himself in fast-paced, UK-influenced house. It’s a formula that has quickly made him a household name among dance music’s tastemakers and earned him the BBC Radio 1 Future Star 2025 award. As showcased on his Resident Advisor podcast, MALUGI has brought his signature energy to some of dance music’s most prestigious spaces, from Panorama Bar and Warehouse Project to Amnesia Ibiza and Awakenings. A relentless creative force, he has toured the US and Australia, amassed millions of streams on his original productions, and delivered two viral Boiler Rooms in 2024. Looking ahead, the mission stays the same: bringing fun to club music — only the scale is growing. Whether it’s his stacked festival summer with highlights like Glastonbury and Tomorrowland, or his own Happy Hour event series, MALUGI brings big feelings for big rooms.
activity_description_1665968634922872180: Contrary to the name, there’s nothing secret about X CLUB. anymore. The London-based duo of Ben Clarke and Jesse Morath have spent the past few years refining a sound that’s as explosive as it is expansive. What began as a raw, high-energy take on ’90s techno has evolved into something broader, pulling from breakbeat, jungle, trance and beyond. It’s functional, high-impact club music built with patience and longevity in mind. That evolution is mirrored on the road. Across 2024 and 2025, X CLUB. sold out headline shows across multiple continents, closed festival main stages, and cemented their reputation as one of Australia’s most exciting electronic exports. In the studio, their catalogue balances club-ready impact with left-of-centre ideas, from crossover moments like “Frankie Knuckles” and “HU4D” to their 2025 Stay With Me EP. With their Hide The Junk platform continuing to grow, the duo show no signs of slowing down — louder rooms, sharper records, and zero interest in smoothing the edges.
activity_description_1665968635577183604: Few artists have risen through the ranks of UK Dance Music as quickly as Liverpool born, Manchester based Joe Germains, aka Faster Horses. Jumping into the scene as a fresh-faced 18 year old back in 2020, they quickly made a name for themselves pushing a unique brand of trance-tinged techno, drawing inspiration from the vibrant dancefloor culture of cities like Copenhagen and Berlin. This led to a slew of international debuts across the continent before he had even stepped foot in the booth of a UK club.
activity_description_1665968636273438068: In a league of their own when it comes to live performances, the high-voltage folk-metal band have been busy touring the past few months. From hitting the road with the Dropkick Murphys across the US, packing-out festival sets across Europe, supporting Dermot Kennedy in Australia and performing at the UK’s Download Festival, the band are showing no signs of slowing down. The band’s third album Pull Like A Dog is a refinement of the acoustic/electric, folk/metal fusion they laid out on Mind Yourself, resulting in the band’s most polished, high-octane album to date. “As a band, this feels like a new beginning,” says Conor (guitar, backing vocals). “I think the changes we’ve faced have given us a lot of room to grow, maybe into roles we felt were off limits before. Openness, perseverance, and positivity – this album embodies all of that.” The Scratch is Conor Dockery, Cathal McKenna, Daniel Lang, and Gary Regan.
activity_description_1665968636910972276: The cathartic communion between James Marriott and his ever expanding following has been a hallmark of every moment in his rise to date. Those scenes have been replicated at every stop since, from playing The Royal Albert Hall with Jake Bugg to storming the Reading and Leeds Festivals, and selling out his biggest headline show to date at KOKO. “I feel like my music is my space to be honest about everything because it feels so validating.” “There’s nothing really like the validation of when you play a show, and you're singing about something that's really important to you, and people are singing it with you.” There was less than a year between his first show and the Reading / Leeds Festivals, and even now he has played fewer than 100 gigs in total. It only took another few months to catapult into the UK’s Official Album Chart at #17 with his self-released debut album ‘Are We There Yet?’. Not even 18 months on, and James is now readying the release of his second record, ‘Don’t Tell The Dog’. “I just want people to feel that I’m never going to phone it in.”
activity_description_1711518959704347748: Meet some of the artists and activists from Global Green as they share stories from the frontlines of change - from ecological restoration to creative resistance.
activity_description_1711518960283161700: MarkO blends Irish folk tradition with shamanic and atmospheric soundscapes to create deep connection and reflection. Inspired by nature and ancient storytelling, their music uses voice and melody to offer an uplifting, grounding experience that transcends genre. Whether in intimate settings or on festival stages, MarkO’s performances aim to touch the heart, awaken emotion, and leave audiences feeling moved and renewed through soulful, intuitive expression.
activity_description_1711518960887141476: The Savage Jim Breen are an Irish alt-folk band formed in 2012, though its members, James Haughey, Greg Breen, James Savage and Manus Crowley, have been playing together in various forms for many years. Their music offers a rare blend of original songwriting, uplifting harmonies and folk-rooted storytelling, capturing something of life in 21st-century Ireland: its pressures, contradictions, humour, hope and humanity. With multiple songwriters in the band, their sound shifts through folk, roots and alternative landscapes from one song to the next, while still holding a distinctive shared voice. By their own admission, all songs are translated through a single gaze, that of the mysterious figure known as the Savage Jim Breen
activity_description_1711518962229318756: Luke Clerkin is a two-time Sports and Cultural Council songwriting competition winner from Tallaght. He has performed at festivals and venues all over Ireland and abroad including in Germany, Londonkelsey, LA and Bulgaria. His songs have received airplay on RTÉ Radio One, BBC Northern Ireland, Spin 1038, Spin South West, KCLR, FM104, and Today FM, among others. Luke released his debut album 'Orpheus' to critical acclaim in January 2025
activity_description_1711518963328226404: West of Ireland duo Riddim & Ting bring reggae soundsystem culture to Global Green, blending reggae, dub, dancehall, ska, jungle and DnB into an irresistible dancefloor journey. Working in the classic reggae soundsystem style of DJ juggling the riddims and live MC laying down her own unique take, their goal is to nice up the place and put a smile on your face…yes now!
activity_description_1711518963948983396: Dynamic booty rave merchants full of bass and sass. Big baselines and all kinda beats - baile funk, dancehall, tropical techno - via DJ Kelsey Sheridan; vocals and antics via the incomparable Lady Grew, electric and live drums extravaganza via Iarla Fox. Expect raucous festival party vibes, with live elements, guests and mad vibes.
activity_name_1711518965098222692: DJ Ruari-Santiago McBride and Ollie Moore
activity_description_1711518965098222692: Dancehall and beaty tropical vibes for the floor. From Colombian to the Caribbean, all over Turtle Island, and over to West Africa too, these tunes are made for dancing. Bringing beats and glitches, organica and electronica, kicks and groves together in a way that grabs, jolts and shakes the floor! Regulars at their own Eats and Beats events in Cloughjordan, and at festivals and quirky cosy things all over, expect to get up to get down.
activity_description_1711518966297793636: DJ Kelsey's sets are a vibrant fusion of global sounds, techy rollers, and baile and dembow riddims, all wrapped in bass-driven beauty. Expect high energy and a lot of booty from this one on the dancefloor.
activity_description_1711518966893384804: Weaving warm sets with worldwide bass wobbles and beautiful melodies to move you! Recent sets set the scene with transcendent electronics (melodic house/techno, EDM with meltingly velvet vocals), or ground stomping earthy-hard drops (DnB, electro-swing, and glitch-hop)
activity_description_1711518967983903844: California born, Donegal based, Eli is an enthusiast of contemporary psychedelic techno and aims to create a hypnotising atmosphere that invites people to dance themselves out of their heads and into their bodies. For the last 10 years Eli has been exploring different sounds and genres through his dj sets but has always found techno closest to his heart.
activity_description_1711518968571106404: Shake off that fuzzy festival head, wake up your body and get your energy flowing with Majella O’Connor. No experience needed. Just bring yourself (and a mat if you have one). Come early as this is popular. Leave feeling relaxed, centered and ready for the day ahead
activity_description_1711518969191863396: Join Dr. Laura Kehoe for a joyful protest singing workshop. Learn powerful songs of resistance and solidarity, then belt them out with kindred souls - no experience needed, just bring your lungs and your spirit.
activity_name_1711518970324325476: Feeding Ourselves - Food System Transformation with Siolta Croí
activity_description_1711518970324325476: A panel discussion facilitated by Cultivate's Davie Philip with Siolta Croi, Talamh Beo and more from our global green community, exploring the potential of local food economies and innovative approaches to reshape the wider agri-food system - as if people and planet mattered. Agroecology, food sovereignty, and a whole lot more.
activity_name_1711518971507119204: Decolonising Agriculture with Rupa Marya and Ollie Moore
activity_description_1711518971507119204: Ollie Moore and Rupa Marya in conversation hosted by Joanne Fullerton of Siolta Croí. What happens when we peel back the layers of colonisation and begin anew, with fresh eyes, at our land, our farming and our food? What can we learn from the past and from our speculative futures via time travelling and imagination? Join us on this journey.
activity_description_1711518972614415460: An all-singing, all-dancing, emotionally charged performance from Young Voices of Africa - a diverse and dynamic group of young people from across the African continent and diaspora, raising their voices on the issues affecting their communities and the wider continent
activity_name_1711518973738488932: Caoimhe Butterly and Rupa Marya in Conversation: Palestine - what next?
activity_description_1711518973738488932: Caoimhe Butterly Caoimhe Butterly is a human rights activist, educator, documentary filmmaker & trauma-informed psychotherapist. She has worked as a volunteer ambulance worker in Gaza, alongside Palestinian paramedics, and has also spent years in the West Bank. She has worked with refugee and displaced communities for over 25 years in Palestine, Iraq, Lebanon, Syria, Mexico, Guatemala, Haiti, Ukraine, Greece, Calais and elsewhere & currently works in psychosocial and trauma support work, with humanitarian and frontline responders. Caoimhe has been involved in flotillas to break the siege of Gaza since 2008, including sailing with the most recent Global Sumud Flotilla, as part of an onboard mental health supports team. Rupa Marya is a physician, activist, writer, mother, soil lover and composer. She was Professor of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, practicing and teaching hospital medicine for 23 years until she was fired in May 2025 for her advocacy of Palestinian life and liberation. Now in Ireland her work focuses on food sovereignty, community health and decolonial practice.
activity_description_1711518974854173796: Palestinian-Lebenese singer with a spell-binding voice. Leen Maarouf is a multi-talented Palestinian singer/songwriter from Lebanon who uses art to craft her unique story and views on the world. With insightful lyrics and powerful vocals Leen has delighted huge audiences at protests, festivals and gigs all over Ireland. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.
activity_name_1711518975978247268: Palestine - what now, what next in Ireland?
activity_description_1711518975978247268: Taking action: stop the game, stop the occupation, stop colonisation. With Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Belfast BDS, Mothers Against Genocide Neart Nur and more. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.
activity_description_1711518977119097956: Abood Aladham is a Palestinian Jordanian multifaceted artist and activist. A champion, dexterous, playful beatboxer, this cheeky chappie also uses looping and other elements to bring you on an amazing and unexpected journey. Abood has pioneered Jordanian beatboxing and is the founder of the Jordan beatboxing championship. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session
activity_name_1711518978226394212: Yalla Craic - Play Roots and Resilience
activity_description_1711518978226394212: Yalla Craic is a cultural and educational game development studio that creates engaging learning experiences designed to bring people together across cultures. Roots and Resistance, is a unique trilingual card game: Irish, Arabic, and English. The game offers four different games in a single deck, providing players with multiple ways to explore and engage with the shared histories, cultures, struggles, and resilience of Ireland and Palestine. Through storytelling, memory challenges, creative connections, and discussion-based activities, players discover common values and experiences while developing a deeper appreciation for both cultures. Designed for young people and adults, Roots and Resistance transforms learning into an interactive and enjoyable experience that inspires curiosity, empathy, and meaningful conversations. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.
activity_description_1711518979392410724: is an Offaly-born, Dublin-based folk musician and multi-instrumentalist. Known for playing guitar, mandolin, bouzouki, and banjo, he blends traditional Irish folk with original songs and is an advocate for the healing and community-building power of live music. Part of the Taking Action for Palestine afternoon session.
activity_description_1711518980508095588: A West Belfast band pulling from post-punk tension, Irish- language revival, and heavy, atmosphere-driven guitar music. Rooted in the streets and memory of their fractured city, the band make songs that move between place, history, and mythology.
activity_description_1711518981607003236: Evolving from their roots as a live dance anthem band, RobotRock is bringing a new chapter to Electric Picnic 2026. Stepping out of the mash-up realm, the band now performs their own tent-shaking original beats. Heavily influenced by big beat era dance music, RobotRock's fresh sound channels the floor-filling energy of pioneers like The Chemical Brothers, Daft Punk, Underworld, and Fatboy Slim. Expect the same massive, live experience that has captivated festivals, clubs, and venues across the country, now fueled by hard-hitting, synth-driven original tracks.
activity_description_1711518982722688100: Artists Cliff Mashetti and Raphael Olympio, founders of Sauti Studios in Cork, use poetry, spoken word, music, and storytelling to explore identity, belonging, and social justice. Through powerful performances and creative expression, they challenge racism in Ireland while celebrating resilience, diversity, and the power of community.
activity_description_1711518983846761572: The HIP HOP HOORAY party makes a welcome return to Global Green this year for a late night celebration of the golden age of hip hop. Expect 90's hip hop classics and a party atmosphere all expertly mixed by DJ Rosko with Reo Oderile on live drums and guest MC's.
activity_description_1711518984937280612: Hlymrekr is a Limerick based club night and collective led by friends Eamonn Walsh and Ethan Madden. Limerick has a small but very rich music scene and they have carved out a notable space as an underground force built for the love of the dance. Hlymrekr, is a translation from Old Norse, meaning 'The Mighty Noise', and references the Viking's discovery of Limerick and the sound heard around The River Shannon. Eamo & ecat will shift between deep grooves, cosmic disco, percussive heat and beyond. Like their project's namesake, this sonic pairing promises to be mighty!
activity_description_1711518986044576868: Sophie Shaw is a Belfast-based DJ and promoter whose sound is rooted in bass-driven music, drawing from techno, house and leftfield influences. With forward thinking selections and a sharp instinct for the dance-floor, she brings an energy that is deeply rooted in underground club culture. In 2024, Sophie founded Social Sounds, a Belfast-based event series that has quickly become a vital fixture in the city’s nightlife. Sophie’s musical passion and work reflects a deep commitment to underground music - both as a selector and a scene builder - making her a standout voice in Ireland’s new wave of club culture.
activity_description_1711518987160261732: Cork based KNUM has been steadily contributing sets not only across Cork City but also across some of Ireland’s most renowned venues over the last number years, through his alias MUNK . Though originally rooted in groove-based techno as MUNK, his new style under KNUM has slowed down the pace and put focus on a wide-angle of genres, often weaving through house, prog-house, tech and even elements of trance. A rising star in Cork’s thriving musical landscape where the scene is forever pushing forward and driving towards its underground roots, KNUM represents the next generation of local innovators building on the city’s legacy of raw, boundary-pushing electronic culture.
activity_description_1711518988259169380: B.R.E.D has established himself as a dynamic force in the Irish electronic music scene. Having performed at Electric Picnic for the past number of years and Fuinneamh in 2024, he never fails to captivate audiences with his deep soundscapes which keep you on your toes. Each year, he has delivered sets that have kept crowds grooving until the early hours, no matter the day. Beyond the festival circuit, B.R.E.D has left his mark on the Irish music scene, having performed at well known venues and events across the country. From intimate club sets in Galway to outdoor gatherings in Cork, his sets never fail to impress. B.R.E.D's recent shift in sound has led him to exploring many new genres and the links found between them, so expect a set that leans on the experimental but relies on the groove.
activity_description_1711518989374854244: Shake off that fuzzy festival head, wake up your body and get your energy flowing with Majella O’Connor. No experience needed. Just bring yourself (and a mat if you have one). Come early as this is popular. Leave feeling relaxed, centered and ready for the day ahead
activity_description_1711518989987222628: Explore how joy, play, and movement can challenge systems of oppression and reimagine community spaces. This lively session invites you to get curious, get moving, and maybe get a little messy - all while seeing social justice through a lens of pleasure and access to third spaces. Expect paint splattering, wild body movement, and playful conversations. Bígí linn!
activity_name_1711518990607979620: Honouring the Dexter – Stories, Heritage & Waste Not, Want Not
activity_description_1711518990607979620: A Local Green Box Cavan initiative - The Story of a Native Breed with Pauric Farrelly – exploring the heritage, resilience and importance of Dexter cattle within regenerative and local food systems. Waste Not, Want Not with Imelda Mullen – a practical and engaging demo showing how we can honour the whole animal: from transforming bones into nourishing broth to rendering fat into a natural skin cream, rooted in traditional thrift and circular living.
activity_description_1711518991706887268: The Wellbeing Economy Alliance hosts a conversation with artists working at the intersection of ecology, social change, and degrowth. Together, they explore how creativity can deepen connection, provoke dialogue, challenge consumer culture, and inspire transformation towards more just and regenerative futures.
activity_description_1711518992780629092: A panel discussion with activists from community-led housing, community energy, and community-supported agriculture exploring how people are coming together to meet real needs, share resources, and build more resilient local places.
