activity_description_1739221673984715232: Meascáin trad agus funky folk.... I nGaelinn, Spáinnis agus Francis. Cloisfidh tú tionchar Meiriceá Laidineach, Aifric Theas agus Chroca Dhuibhne!
activity_description_1739221675310115296: Is cumadóir, Gaeilgeoir agus ceoltóir traidisiúnta as Béal Feirste, Éire, é Seosamh Mac. Meascann Seosamh ceol traidisiúnta le blasanna ó sheánraí eile le hinsint scéalta faoinár ndaonnacht chomhroinnte, agus le cruthú ceoil chun an corp a bhogadh agus an t-anam a mhúscailt.
activity_description_1739221689965013472: Amhráin Ghaeilge agus Arabacha ó amhránaí ar an sean-nós, Eoghan Ó Ceannabháin, agus amhránaí Éireannach-Liobánach, Niamh Keady-Tabbal. Tagann an bheirt le chéile ag casadh amhráin a bhaineann le himirce, le streachailt, le grá agus le dóchas.
activity_description_1739221691231693280: Is banna ceoil traidisiúnta agus tíre iad The Gladstone Band ó 2024 i mBaile Átha Cliath le deartháireacha Adam agus Patrick Hutton agus Timmy Sheridan. Seinneann siad bailiúcháin ceol traidisiúnta agus tíre agus a gceol bunscríobhta féin.
activity_description_1739221702539536864: Is banna folk-rock é Jessie & the Veil atá lonnaithe i mBaile Átha Cliath. Spreagtha ag ceoltóirí cosúil le Clannad, Florence and the Machine agus The Cranberries. Meascann a chuid ceoil gnéithe do cheol traidisiúnta na hÉireann le fuaim mhothúchánach agus neamhshaolta.
activity_name_1739221711204968928: Seisiún Rúnda: Cúán de Búrca x hHH
activity_description_1739221712463260128: Seit DJ le Cian Ó Curnáin a chuirfidh clabhsúr ar oíche Shathairn in An Puball Gaeilge — ceol agus craic go luath ar maidin.
activity_name_1739221713687996896: ‘Coinneáil Orainn’ Cumann Drámaíochta Ollscoil na Gaillimhe
activity_description_1739221713687996896: Nuair a théann Cigire deireanach na roinne sa tóir ar an mbeirt chainteoir dúchasacha deireanacha sa tír, ardaítear ceisteanna a théann buille beag róghar don chnámh.
activity_description_1739221714988231136: Craic leis na cailíní - scéalta agus scannal leis na mná thar chúpla deochín
activity_description_1739221722990963168: Oíche ghrinn dhátheangach Funny Focail a bhunaigh fuirseoirí Diane O'Connor agus Louise O'Toole anuraidh. Is spás speisialta é chun taitneamh a bhaint as an teanga cibé caighdeán atá agat.
activity_description_1739221732293929440: Ceiliúradh ar chruthaitheacht Mhná na hÉireann le ceol agus filíocht. Bígí linn don seit spreagúil suimiúil seo!
activity_description_1739221744910395872: Is grúpa drumadóireacht é Buail Feirste; grúpa "batería" atá ann, bunaithe ar thraidisiún ceoil an charnabhail, nó "Samba" ón mBrasaíl. Úsáideann siad meascán uirlisí traidisiúnta ón mBrasaíl le píosaí traidisiúnta a sheinm agus ceol nua a chruthú – ag baint inspioráid ó mhiotaseolaíocht na hÉireann agus ón saol comhaimseartha.
activity_description_1739221753223506400: Grúpa ceoltóirí óga fuinniúla as Béal Feirste atá sa bhanna ceoil traidisiúnta Dall. D'fhoghlaim na baill conas ceol a sheinnt i Scoil Cheoil Traidisiúnta Glengormley agus chuir siad snas ar chúrsaí faoi threoir na gceoltóirí is fearr i gcathair Bhéal Feirste i Tigh Mhadáin, nó baile an cheoil thraidisiúnta mar fheictear do mhuintir na háite é. Grúpa spleodrach bríomhar craiceáilte is ea é.
activity_description_1739221766662056416: Soláthraíonn TART punkcheol corparáideach don aois nualiobrálach.
activity_description_1739221773700098528: Ceol agus amhránaíocht thraidisiúnta ó Ghaoth Dobhair, Dún na nGall
activity_description_1739221781820271072: Le rithimí beomhara, agus fuinneamh tógálach, tugann The Railway Boys beocht úr don cheol traidisiúnta. Seinneann Piaras Ó Lorcáin, Mickey Fearon, Oisín Ó Murchú, Seán Ó Briain agus Brian Ó Gallachóir meascán d'fhidil, bainseó, giotár agus dord, cruthaíonn siad fuaim bhríomhar atá chomh hoiriúnach do sheisiúin bheaga is atá do stáitsí móra. Tá siad ag bailiú lucht leanúna ar fud na tíre – agus ní gan chúis!
activity_description_1742033269190792076: The Picnic's beloved morning ritual: speed debating over tea, coffee and biscuits. Pick a topic from the menu, sit down opposite a stranger and talk — properly. Chat, without the chit. Runs every morning of the weekend.
activity_description_1742033278057550732: The Human Library is an interactive workshop where our "books" tell a story about their lives and our "readers" have a chance to discuss and ask questions. This offers open dialogue about themes and topics that others may resonate with. You may find similarities in your own story with our books, or break down prejudices you've held by hearing someone else's experience and having a conversation. This falls in line with our slogan, "unjudge someone."
activity_description_1742033287192744844: An intergenerational discussion with Traveller women on navigating a more feminist society while maintaining traditional Traveller values. Gossip Bures is an entertaining yet educational podcast of Traveller mothers and daughters. For the first time they leave the podcast studio and camp up on stage at MindField. Chaired by settled Journo Bure, Jennifer O'Connell.
activity_name_1742033294415336332: History Ireland Hedge School A 'unique relationship'?—Ireland & the US 1918-present - Tommy Graham with Dan Mulhall Michael Kennedy Bernadette Whelan)
activity_description_1742033294415336332: History Ireland Hedge School A 'unique relationship'?—Ireland and the USA 1920-present. While the UK claims to have a 'special relationship' with the USA, we claim a 'unique relationship', exemplified by the now traditional bowl of shamrock presentation in the White House each St Patrick's Day. But the relationship hasn't always been cordial: Dev failed to get recognition for the Irish Republic from the US government in 1920; the biggest threat to our neutrality during the Emergency came not from the Nazis or the British—but from the USA; and today by far the biggest source of far-right misinformation and disinformation is from the USA. To assess this roller-coaster relationship join History Ireland editor, Tommy Graham, in discussion with Dan Mulhall (former Irish Ambassador in Washington), Bernadette Whelan (University of Limerick), and Michael Kennedy and John Gibney (both Royal Irish Academy's Documents on Irish Foreign Policy).
activity_name_1742033309338669964: Screening: My Friend Kev (Winner of Best Short at Galway Film Fleadh) Colin Peppard (director) in conversation with Donie O'Sullivan
activity_description_1742033309338669964: Winner of Best Short Documentary at the 38th Galway Film Fleadh 2026 — and now Oscar-longlisted — 'My Friend, Kev' is the debut documentary from director Colin Peppard. Set against a winter in West Clare, it follows a filmmaker reconnecting with an old friend he hasn't seen in years. Kev caddies on the edge of a Trump-owned golf course and dreams of escaping to Florida, until his visa is denied. Over a few days their conversations drift between old memories, new beliefs and the fractures of the present, asking how strong shared memories must be to hold a friendship together when everything else is pulling apart. Colin Peppard is a director from Monaghan, based between Belfast and Dublin, whose work spans documentaries, music videos and commercials. Following the screening, he joins Donie O'Sullivan in conversation.
activity_name_1742033318675190668: Divorcing the Superpower: The US, Europe and the Next 250 Years. Leviathan panel hosted by Andrew Maxwell with Donie O'Sullivan, Eric Lonergan, Dan Mulhall(?), Jennifer O'Connell
activity_description_1742033318675190668: America turns 250 and the transatlantic marriage is on the rocks. Comedian Andrew Maxwell referees as CNN's Donie O'Sullivan, economist Eric Lonergan and The Irish Times's Jennifer O'Connell ask whether Europe should fight for the relationship, file the papers, or quietly change the locks.
activity_name_1742033328573748108: Amnesty Hour: Republic of Conscience: Speaking Out Against the Global Disorder
activity_description_1742033328573748108: Amnesty's annual MindField hour takes its title from the poem Seamus Heaney wrote for the movement, and asks what speaking out means when the global order is coming apart: who defends the defenders, and what conscience costs in 2026.
activity_name_1742033340275856268: Leviathan - Europe: Accession. Ambassador Larysa Gerasko of Ukraine, Ambassador Larisa Miculet of Moldova, Barry Andrews MEP and host Shona Murray
activity_description_1742033340275856268: Two countries fighting for their futures make their case for Europe. Ambassador Larysa Gerasko of Ukraine and Ambassador Larisa Miculet of Moldova join Barry Andrews MEP and journalist Shona Murray to talk enlargement in wartime: what accession asks of them, and what it asks of the rest of us.
activity_name_1742033346701529996: Chats in the Flats: Brian Branningan, Anita Reilly, Willa White
activity_description_1742033346701529996: Chats in the Flats is a storytelling project dedicated to preserving voices, stories and rich culture of working class communities. 'Sure, Isn't That Just Life?' brings together Brian Brannigan (singer, A Lazarus Soul), Willa White (comedian) and Anita Riley (TV personality) for a conversation about life's ups and downs. Through humour, honesty and lived experience, they'll share the moments that shaped them, the setbacks they overcame and the resilience that carried them through.
activity_name_1742033354351940492: No Filler presents: Who Killed the Dancefloor (Spoiler: It's Not Dead Yet) hosted by Anthony Remedy
activity_description_1742033354351940492: Club-culture chronicler Anthony Remedy convenes an inquest into Irish nightlife: the closures, the costs, the licensing, the phones. Reports of the dancefloor's death prove premature — the suspects are rounded up and the survivors get their say.
activity_name_1742033361155101580: Exploring Abandoned Places: A Visual Tour. Lou UrbEx and Robert O'Byrne
activity_description_1742033361155101580: Ireland is a country of empty rooms: famine cottages, forsaken factories, cinemas gone dark, great houses quietly returning to the ivy. Lou UrbEx, the urban explorer whose films and reels from inside Ireland's forgotten buildings have captivated millions online, joins architectural historian and Irish Aesthete Robert O'Byrne, author of Ruins of Ireland, for a stunning image-led journey through the places we walked away from. Expect short shrift for the clout-seeking explorers who kick down doors for clicks — this is exploration as record-keeping, done with respect for the buildings and their ghosts. And expect answers too: how we tackle a dereliction crisis hiding in plain sight, and how DIY meanwhile use can turn empty buildings into galleries, gig venues and studios before the ivy wins.
activity_name_1742033369174610828: No Filler presents: The Only Camera in the Room. Photographs of Clubbing in the 1990s and 2000s. Brendan Duffy with Anthony Remedy
activity_description_1742033369174610828: Before every night out was documented to death, Brendan Duffy was often the only camera in the room. He joins Anthony Remedy to show his photographs of Irish clubbing in the 1990s and 2000s: the outfits, the sweat, the faces mid-euphoria, from an era when the moment was the point.
activity_name_1742033376606917516: Fair Play: Can a Generous Ireland Persuade the Rest of Europe to Invest in a Common Global Future. David McNair, Neale Richmond, Emily Wigens, Shona Murray - in partnership with the ONE campaign
activity_description_1742033376606917516: Ireland punches above its weight on aid, but the world's wallet is closing. David McNair and Emily Wigens of the ONE Campaign join Neale Richmond TD and journalist Shona Murray to ask whether a generous Ireland can talk the rest of Europe into investing in a common global future — and what happens if nobody does.
activity_name_1742033383493964684: Move Fast and Break the State: The Politics of Populism and the Broligarchy: Leviathan panel hosted by Andrew Maxwell with Donie O'Sullivan, Mark Little, Eric Lonergan
activity_description_1742033383493964684: The broligarchy gets its day in court. Andrew Maxwell hosts CNN's Donie O'Sullivan, disinformation expert Mark Little and economist Eric Lonergan on populism, platforms and the billionaires treating the state like a startup to be disrupted. The weekend's closing Leviathan panel, and probably its loudest.
activity_name_1742049609435580248: Poetry: Jan Brierton and Maia Dunphy
activity_description_1742049609435580248: Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words does Teenage Kicks. Dublin poet and performer Jan Brierton — whose collections What Day Is It? and Everybody Is a Poem both hit the Irish book charts in the same week — opens her Manifesto weekend alongside writer and broadcaster Maia Dunphy. Dunphy spent over a decade writing and producing behind the camera before stepping in front of it, has made twelve documentaries for RTÉ, presented three seasons of What Planet Are You On?, and ghostwrote the Mr Tayto autobiography that famously kept Bertie Ahern off the Christmas number one. Expect poems, stories and a nod to the music, telly and misadventures that shaped them.
activity_name_1742049618134566744: Activism: Anna Cosgrave and Ailbhe Smyth in conversation
activity_description_1742049618134566744: Two generations of Irish activism in one hour. Anna Cosgrave is a facilitator, researcher and campaigner who founded the REPEAL project and played a prominent role in the abortion referendum; she has worked across climate action and social entrepreneurship, sits on the West Cork Islands' Ocean and Environment advisory panel, and trained as a death doula. She is joined by Ailbhe Smyth — feminist, academic and LGBTIQ+ activist, central to both the Marriage Equality and abortion referendums, founding member of Le Chéile: Diversity Not Division and patron of Women's Collective Ireland. A conversation about what changes a country, and what it costs. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words.
activity_name_1742049626867107672: Fashion: body image, male gaze, waste, sustainability, fair trade. Caryn Franklin & Brendan Courtney in conversation
activity_description_1742049626867107672: Fashion under the microscope: body image, the male gaze, waste, sustainability and fair trade. Caryn Franklin MBE, former fashion editor of i-D and BBC's Clothes Show presenter through the eighties and nineties, has spent a career challenging unachievable beauty ideals — co-founding All Walks Beyond the Catwalk and writing SKEWED: Decoding Media Bias. She's joined by broadcaster and designer Brendan Courtney, whose documentaries on housing, ageism and healthcare have driven real policy reform and earned him a ministerial appointment to the Department of Health's Executive Advisory Board. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words.
activity_name_1742049635356378968: The Word: Terry Christian & Muireann O Connell in conversation
activity_description_1742049635356378968: The man who gave Oasis their television debut, in conversation. Born in Old Trafford to Dublin parents, Terry Christian became the youngest-ever winner of a Sony Radio Award and the first broadcaster to win two — giving The Stone Roses their first regular radio play and championing The Charlatans, M People and White Town, before fronting Channel 4's era-defining late-night show The Word. He's joined by Muireann O'Connell, the Limerick native and Ireland AM host whose wit and candour have won her a huge online following, and who describes herself as a 'failed radio and podcast presenter' who has managed to hold onto a job in TV. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words.
activity_name_1742049645095552856: Friendship: 'Our Deadly Summer' Sarah Breen and Emer McLysaght in conversation
activity_description_1742049645095552856: Emer McLysaght and Sarah Breen met studying media at Ballyfermot College. Their careers pulled them in different directions until 2016, when they reunited to co-write Oh My God, What a Complete Aisling — an instant Irish Times bestseller. Four more Aisling books followed, three of them An Post Irish Book Award winners, and their sixth novel Our Deadly Summer landed in May. They join Jan Brierton's Wild Words to talk friendship: the writing kind, the lasting kind, and how you keep one going through decades and six books. They are, they report, still friends too.
activity_description_1742049656722163544: The iconic voice of the Happy Mondays. Rowetta rose to fame as the powerhouse vocalist who helped define the sound of Manchester's rave and indie scene, her soulful, gritty vocals the backbone of Step On, Kinky Afro and some of the most memorable tracks of the nineties. Beyond the Mondays she has built a thriving solo career, collaborating with artists, producers and DJs worldwide, and her voice moves easily across genres. She joins Manifesto for an hour on Madchester, survival and a life in music. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words does Teenage Kicks.
activity_name_1742049662711629656: The Irish Times Women's Podcast with Róisín Ingle, in conversation with Dearbhla Mescal
activity_description_1742049662711629656: Having retired as a member of An Garda Síochána, reared her three children and experienced cancer, Dearbhla Mescal is now finding the time to follow her own dreams and enjoy her second act of life. Finding Joy is her first book. She joins Róisín Ingle — columnist, features writer, author of Pieces of Me and Public Displays of Emotion, and producer and co-presenter of the award-winning Irish Times Women's Podcast — for a live conversation that the Irish Times will record for the podcast. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words.
activity_name_1742049668684318552: Bodies: Katriona O'Sullivan and Tanya Sweeney in conversation
activity_description_1742049668684318552: Katriona O'Sullivan is a professor of psychology, bestselling author of Poor and Hungry and one of Ireland's leading voices on inequality, education and social justice — she has spoken at the UN, Westminster and the European Parliament, blending research, lived experience and humour to challenge how we think about class, trauma and belonging. She's joined by Tanya Sweeney, who began writing for her local West Dublin paper at eleven and has spent twenty years as a columnist across the Irish Times, STELLAR, Irish Tatler and the Irish Independent; her debut novel Esther Is Now Following You was published in January. Part of Jan Brierton's Wild Words.
activity_name_1742049678054393688: Gaza Flotilla: Liam Cunningham and Mikey Cullen in conversation
activity_description_1742049678054393688: Two Dubliners who sailed for Gaza. Liam Cunningham, born in Dublin's north inner city, has an international acting career spanning nearly thirty years — an IFTA winner for Steve McQueen's Hunger, Davos Seaworth in Game of Thrones, and more recently 3 Body Problem — and has been active in pro-Palestinian solidarity campaigns for over four decades. He's joined by Mikey Cullen, award-winning Dublin poet, teacher, actor and filmmaker, whose poetry film The Heart in the Black won Best Irish Poetry Short at the Bloomsday Film Festival 2026, and who was a participant on the 2026 flotilla to Gaza. A conversation about witness, solidarity and what art can do.
activity_name_1742049684161300312: Fools in Love: Jane Austen's Cast vs. Contemporary Love Interests
activity_description_1742049684161300312: It has been over two centuries since readers first swooned over Jane Austen's most enduring romantic heroes, namely Darcy, Wentworth, Knightley and Colonel Brandon. Love interests came in two types: the dashing and the deserving. Ross Kelly chats with novelists Charleen Hurtubise, Louise Nealon, Niamh Ní Mhaoileoin and Clíodhna O'Sullivan, examining how Austen's ideals stack up against a cast of contemporary romantic interests across genres and orientations.
activity_description_1742049694714169176: One of Ireland's most distinctive comic minds and burgeoning artists steps into Manifesto for a conversation like no other. Dylan Moran — comedian, artist, novelist, and a lifelong chronicler of ordinary despair rendered gorgeous — talks life, art, ageing and the absurd with the same restless intelligence that's made him one of the great tragicomic voices of his generation.
activity_name_1742049702121310040: In Defence of the Happy Ending: Anna Carey in conversation with Deirdre O'Kane
activity_description_1742049702121310040: Anna Carey — novelist and unrepentant romantic behind Our Song and Love Scene — defends the happy ending against a culture obsessed with misery lit. Deirdre O'Kane, comedian, actress and professional skeptic, is here to poke holes in the theory and possibly her own love life. Expect warmth, wit, and a spirited row about whether we all just want the kiss at the end.
activity_name_1742049707439687512: The 1,000th Best Band of All Time: Patrick Freyne in conversation with Sinead Gleeson
activity_description_1742049707439687512: Patrick Freyne spent most of his twenties trying to be a rock star before turning to the much more stable and secure world of journalism. He has had short stories and essays published in The Dublin Review, Harper's, the FT Magazine, Banshee and Winter Papers, and is a features writer at the Irish Times. His book of essays, OK, Let's Do Your Stupid Idea, was published by Penguin Sandycove in 2020 — nominated for an Irish Book Award, longlisted for the Rathbones Prize and shortlisted for the Dalkey Emerging Writer Award. His debut novel, Experts in a Dying Field, was published by Penguin Sandycove in June.
activity_name_1742049715056543576: Stealing Culture, Selling It Back: The USA at 250. Liam Lynch in conversation with Patrick Freyne
activity_description_1742049715056543576: America turns 250 this year — and acts every inch the late teenager: brilliant, volatile, and unsure what it's becoming. All the while, in the cross-hairs of a culture war, the Arts appear under siege. But who is up for the fight? Liam Lynch, a cultural nomad native to Ireland, began his 33-year journey into human experiences by creating music festivals, concert tours and integrated entertainment content. He's spent a career between two worlds, and from that mid-Atlantic vantage he watches American pop culture mine, repackage and sell back the heritage it once funded for free. Part fireside, part provocation, this is a conversation about the great cultural heist of our age — and why the art-makers might be the only ones who can change the ending.
activity_name_1742049726808983384: Feeding the Hunger: A Life Told Through the Fridge Door: Dawn O'Porter in conversation with Sinéad Gleeson
activity_description_1742049726808983384: Dawn O'Porter opens the fridge door on a life built from meals — the ones that comforted her after loss, the ones that fuelled ambition, and the odd bag of Wotsits eaten for dinner along the way. Fresh from her memoir Hungry Eyes, she talks food, grief and appetite with Sinéad Gleeson, one of Ireland's sharpest interviewers, in a conversation that's equal parts hunger, heart and honesty.
activity_description_1742086223671271780: A gripping, accessible one-hour play about the fight against the cholera pandemic in 1840s–50s London, following pioneering outsider doctor John Snow as he challenges medical orthodoxy and lays the foundations of modern epidemiology and data science. A medical detective story as much as a drama, Miasma explores good science and bad science, groupthink and dissent, and the cost of standing against accepted wisdom when lives are at stake. Told by five actors, it combines sharp storytelling, historical insight and contemporary relevance for specialist and non-specialist audiences alike. 'An hour of tightly-tuned drama' — The Irish Times. Written by Colin Murphy; produced by Verdant Productions with UCD Centre for Cultural Analytics and Research Ireland.
activity_description_1742086237126599012: A post-show panel discussion following Miasma, unpacking the play's themes — the 1850s cholera outbreak, John Snow's real-life medical detective work, and how the story resonates with today's conversations about public health, evidence-based decision-making and trust in science. In association with Science Week.
activity_description_1742086248778375524: David Bolger's "expertly ingenious" (The Irish Times) duet sets two dancers loose in a surreal dancehall at dusk, where a giant disco ball drops and dreams and nightmares share the bill. A sell-out at Dublin Fringe and Edinburgh, and The Arts Review's Outstanding Dance Production of the Year. Fifty minutes, straight through the heart.
activity_name_1742086265698197860: Irish National Opera: The Greatest Hits You Didn't Know Were Opera
activity_description_1742086265698197860: Discover the songs behind some of the most memorable moments on screen.
activity_name_1742086273323442532: Niall Breslin and the Polaris Quartet perform The Place That Has Never Been Wounded
activity_description_1742086273323442532: Built around Breslin's cinematic compositions, the performances unfold as a fully integrated live work. Music, spoken word, and visual design are interwoven throughout, with lighting and imagery responding in real time to the players on stage. Rather than functioning as accompaniment, the visual elements shape the pacing and emotional contours of each performance, drawing the audience into a shared, concentrated space.
activity_description_1742086280923521380: One of the most listened-to podcasts in the country, recorded live: essays, tangents and questions nobody else thinks to ask, delivered from behind Ireland's most famous plastic bag. In association with Science Week.
activity_description_1742086288943030628: Climbwallscabaret is a burlesque and circus spectacle soundtracked by eight-piece Dublin jazz band Lavery, brought to you by showgirl and hostess with the mostess Betty Beour.
activity_name_1742086300485755236: Brendan O'Connor Show on RTÉ Radio One - Live broadcast
activity_description_1742086300485755236: The Sunday-morning national institution broadcasts live from the middle of a festival. Watch the radio being made: guests, papers, tangents, and the small miracle of a live national broadcast with a festival raging outside the tent. Bring your hangover, Brendan will understand.
activity_name_1742086308933083492: Miriam O'Callaghan Picnic Brunch with Alison Spittle, Frank McNally, Dawn O'Porter, Colm O'Regan, Deirdre O'Kane
activity_description_1742086308933083492: Miriam O'Callaghan assembles a Sunday brunch table like no other: Alison Spittle, Frank McNally, Dawn O'Porter, Colm O'Regan and Deirdre O'Kane on the weekend just gone, the week ahead and whatever else comes up. Sunday papers energy, festival edition.
activity_description_1742086315501363556: One man, one wedding too many, on a hilarious search for connection in a world of plus-ones.
activity_description_1742086322170306916: Professor Luke O'Neill's band of doctors and scientists, out to prove that rock, funk and a tight rhythm section beat any prescription. Veterans of Trinity Ball, Body & Soul and several international conferences that got out of hand. The science says dance.
activity_description_1746322900962905316: DJ Scenic is a rising name on the Dublin dance music circuit, known for seamlessly blending driving techno, high-energy grooves, hard house classics and more. Her genre-blurring approach to mixing 4-on-the-floor beats brings a fresh edge to the dancefloor. Having played multiple renditions of Otherside Festival and supporting some of the biggest international names in the scene such as Fjaak, 9x9, and Partiboi69, she is no stranger to getting the party going.
activity_name_1746350702688900008: Ceili Mor presented by the renowned Lynam school of Irish dancing
activity_description_1746350702688900008:
Céili Mór for all 
Our Ceili session ‘Caller’ and team of dancers will guide everyone through the steps and movements as the dances progress, so that everyone can join in without prior experience. With Ceili classics like The walls of Limerick or The Siege of Ennis, this lively session is bound to bring energy and most of all a bit of ‘craic’ to the Croi area.
activity_description_1746350711429829544:
Energy Dance Fitness & Zumba Class 
Donna is a core force behind Move Me Ireland, the collective renowned for delivering sold-out dance experiences across the country. Specializing in Zumba Dance Fitness, no experience is necessary—just bring your fun-loving crew or come solo and discover your tribe! Join us at the Crescent Earth Stage in the Croí area at Electric Picnic 2026 to find your flow, amplify your energy, and set the momentum for the best weekend of the year.
activity_description_1746350720925733800:
Sunflower Sessions: Yoga, DJ & Live Music
"Kick off your Saturday at Electric Picnic the right way. Sunflower Sessions brings their iconic yoga and live music experience to the festival, a high-energy, dynamic flow set to live Irish DJ Kipunji, designed to get you out of your head and completely into your body. Whether you've never done yoga in your life or you're on the mat every day, this one's for you. It's lighthearted, it's upbeat, and falling over is absolutely encouraged.

After the flow, Irish artist Taylor Byrne takes to the stage to bring it all back down, lie on your mat, close your eyes, and just let the music wash over you.

Hosted by Sunflower Sessions, the Irish wellness and culture collective behind sold-out yoga and live music events across Ireland. 🌻"
activity_description_1746350731201778600:
BollyBeats: Shake, Smile &Sweat - The ultimate dance party of Bollywood Music
BollyBeats is thrilled to come to Ireland for its Electric Picnic debut! BollyBeats is a high-energy fitness format that blends the infectious rhythms of Bollywood with a dynamic workout similar to Zumba. Designed for everyone from absolute beginners to intermediate movers, this session requires no previous dance experience. Expect infectious beats, easy-to-follow choreo, and a feel-good workout where fitness meets festival vibes. Get ready for a fun-filled experience packed with catchy Bollywood beats that will keep you moving and smiling.
activity_description_1746350742543176616:
Sculpt & Flow: 80's Power Flow
On Saturday, Allan Müller brings Sculpt & Flow: 80s Power Yoga to the festival, a feel-good, high-energy class designed to get you moving, sweating, and smiling.

Set to uplifting 80s beats, this is a playful yet powerful flow that builds strength, boosts your energy, and leaves you feeling strong and alive in your body. Expect a full-body workout that tones and energises, without taking itself too seriously.

Whether you’re coming with friends, flying solo, or just curious to try something new, this session is open to all levels. Come as you are, move at your own pace, and enjoy the ride.
activity_description_1746350759471387560:
Afro Twerk 
Discover the power, rhythm, and confidence of Afro Twerk. This high-energy class blends Afro-inspired movement with twerk fundamentals, focusing on body isolation, musicality, and self-expression. Open to all levels, expect great music, empowering vibes, and plenty of opportunities to move, sweat, and have fun.
activity_description_1746350776055665576:
The Complete Sunday Reset 
A weekend of music, connection, and adventure can leave you buzzing—but also a little disconnected from yourself. This session is the antidote. Through dynamic breathwork, intuitive movement, somatic exploration, and a liberating yoga flow, we'll clear out the mental clutter and awaken the wisdom of the body. Expect moments of play, freedom, catharsis, and deep presence as you move beyond thinking and into feeling. No rigid sequences, no pressure to perform—just an invitation to trust your instincts and follow what feels true. Perfect for anyone looking to recharge, reset, and end the festival feeling more energised than when they arrived. No previous yoga or breathwork experience required.
activity_description_1746350799912866728:
FONDA JANE
DANCE WORKOUT
Seize your inner Power, Glory & Sass with Fonda Jane!
Its a Full body stretch, bend and tone in the comfort of your own incredible body!
This workshop is about pleasuring the dance, body positivity and slaying to the beat!
The funnest dance in town!
Get ready to Fonda Jane!"
activity_description_1746350811245876136:
EP banger dance class
Release your inner dancer with a dancercise class. Whether you're a first time mover or professional, everyone is welcome. Come join us for some EP BANGERS. Finish off your weekend with us and on a high.
activity_description_1746350820305572776:
Dance is free Medicine
Celebration to move and dance ,  getting out of your comfort zone through music and dance . building confidence. bringing everyone together , a nonstop music , no experience needed, dance with total strangers and sing with your heart.
activity_description_1746365138140949624:
Exploring the Divine Masculine & Feminine Energies
"Step into the sacred dance of Divine Masculine and Divine Feminine energies and explore the magic that lives within us all. Through breathwork, movement, Hara activation, meditation, authentic sharing, and deep attunement practices, we’ll awaken the body’s wisdom and reconnect to our inner compass.

Expect energy, presence, connection, and transformation as we journey through breath, movement, active listening, and embodied exploration. Come curious, come open, and discover what it means to stand fully in your authentic energetic expression.

"
activity_description_1746365146001075320:
Didgeridoo Tribal Dance
"Didgeridoo Jedi's performance is a sonic initiation.
A raw convergence of tribal electonic music and live didgeridoo, where deep, rolling basslines intertwine with ancient breath and bone. Each sound is sculpted in real time, reading the crowd, the didgeridoo layered on the music, breathing through it.
Hypnotic rhythms, primal pulses and ecstatic grooves unravel like a living presence. 
The dancefloor becomes a ritual space: a place where instinct awakens, bodies remember, and something older than language begins to move.
Rooted in shamanic sound traditions and driven by modern electronic force, this is a journey through shadow and light, tension and release, earth and electricity."
activity_description_1746365154825890936:
Flow & Grow with Lurienne Jewel
Flow & Grow is an uplifting, all-levels vinyasa class designed to help you reconnect with yourself in the midst of festival magic ✨ Through breath-led movement, mindful transitions, balance, and gentle strength, we’ll create space to move, breathe, and simply be. Expect an energising yet grounding practice that builds warmth in the body, calms the mind, and invites you to embrace the present moment. Come exactly as you are and leave feeling refreshed, centred, and ready to embrace the rest of your festival adventure 🌸
activity_description_1746365162316917880:
Cacao Croí Ceremony 
A heart-opening cacao ceremony inviting you to slow down, reconnect and come home to yourself. Through ceremonial cacao, breathwork, movement and music, Lorraine creates a warm, uplifting space to awaken your heart, connect with community and experience the magic that unfolds when we gather with intention.
activity_description_1746365176426556536:
An Táin Bó Yoga
An Táin Bó Yoga is a unique Irish cultural wellness experience inspired by the epic tale of Cú Chulainn. Through fun yoga flows, captivating storytelling, and live Irish music, participants embody the characters who shaped Cú Chulainn's journey, weaving movement and stillness into an immersive, embodied experience. Delivered bilingually in Irish and English, the session invites you to immerse yourself in Ireland's greatest epic while moving at your own pace.
activity_description_1746365188061555832:
Stretch & Restore (Vinyasa & Yin Yoga) 
Take a break from the buzz of the festival and give your body exactly what it needs. We'll begin with simple breathwork to regulate the nervous system before moving through an uplifting Vinyasa flow to awaken tired muscles, improve mobility and boost energy after days of dancing, walking and sleeping in tents. As the pace slows, we'll ease into long, nourishing Yin postures to release deep tension, improve flexibility and encourage complete relaxation. We'll finish with a guided savasana, leaving you feeling grounded, refreshed and ready to make the most of the rest of your Electric Picnic weekend. No experience is needed, just bring yourself, an open mind and a willingness to tune inwards for an hour.
activity_description_1746365196357889144:
Rince Electronica yoga w/ live dj!
"Not your average yoga class — Rince Yoga (pronounced Rin-ka, Irish for “dance”) is a high-vibe, music-fuelled experience, to get out of our minds and into our bodies.

A chance to move, breathe, and shake it all off — to rinse the body of tension, stress, and mental noise, and reconnect with your raw, radiant joy.

With a live dj set dropping energising, uplifting beats, we flow through:
•⁠  ⁠Dynamic breathwork to clear the mind
•⁠  ⁠Shaking and playful movement to release stuck energy
•⁠  ⁠Creative, freeform flow to awaken and connect to your inner self

Come as you are, leave rinsed, recharged, and reconnected — body, mind, and spirit.

Think yoga meets rave - a flow of breath and beat.
"
activity_description_1746365207514737784:
Reggae Yoga
Fun engergising session combining simple yoga asanas and light choreographed dancing.
activity_description_1746365216213724280:

"Whether your energy is hitting a wall just as the main stage headliners are gearing up, or your body is feeling the beautiful chaos of Stradbally, it’s time for a total reset. Join Aoife Smith, Systematic Kinesiologist, for an energy re-balancing session designed to get you out of your head, back into your body, and perfectly balanced for the rest of the weekend. activity_description_1746365236228942968:
Sacred Rhythm - A Shamanic Drumming Meditation
"Step into a space of stillness, connection, and deep restoration through the ancient power of rhythm. In this immersive shamanic drumming meditation, Christine Higgins guides participants on a gentle inner journey using live drumming, breath awareness, guided visualisation, and meditation.

The steady beat of the drum helps quiet the mind, regulate the nervous system, and create space for reflection, insight, and healing. Suitable for all experience levels, this session offers a chance to step away from the noise of the festival, reconnect with yourself, and experience a profound sense of calm and clarity."
activity_description_1746365257586338936:
Breathwork-reconnect through the POWER of your breath 
"Step away from the noise and discover one of the most powerful tools you carry with you every day your breath.

This session combines gentle movement, breath awareness, and practical breathing techniques designed to help regulate stress, calm the mind, boost energy, and reconnect you with your body..

Inspired by nature, resilience, and years of guiding people through breathwork, cold exposure, and mountain adventures, Marta creates a welcoming space where participants can slow down, reset, and explore their inner strength.

Suitable for complete beginners and experienced practitioners.

Pause. Breathe. Reconnect"
activity_description_1746365268676078712:
Disco Yoga 
"Disco Yoga by Yoga Parties is a unique and fun wellness experience, as featured on Ireland AM.

Disco Yoga is a fluid and energetic class combining traditional hatha yoga with disco moves. Expect savage tunes, yogic flow, lycra fun, new friends and good endorphins."
activity_description_1746377689788637800: Reclaiming Pleasure in the Modern World In a world that rewards productivity, urgency and disconnection, this is an invitation to return to the body and remember pleasure as a source of wisdom, vitality and connection. Through gentle somatic practices, sensory exploration and embodied reflection, we will explore what it means to feel deeply alive.
activity_description_1746377699519423080: Connecting with the Wild Being An invitation to connect to the inner wild being within you through a combination of breath, movement and play. Expect to leave feeling alive, energised and connected to the untamed wildness in you.
activity_description_1746377715273228904: Imagination Liberation: Creative Play Session "Imagination Liberation is an immersive, game-based workshop designed to help participants step out of the analytical mind and into the intuitive, imaginative realm of play. Drawing inspiration from Dada, Surrealism, divination practices, and embodied movement, this session invites participants to reconnect with their inner child—the part of themselves that creates instinctively, dreams freely, and trusts curiosity over certainty. Through playful exercises involving movement, chance operations, cut-up poetry, bibliomancy, scrying, costume play, and collaborative games, participants will bypass habitual patterns of thinking and discover unexpected creative possibilities. Chance and synchronicity become collaborators, revealing surprising images, characters, and stories that emerge beyond conscious control. Rather than focusing on producing polished outcomes, Imagination Liberation celebrates experimentation, spontaneity, and joyful creative risk-taking. Participants leave with a newfound sense of creative confidence, a playful alter ego, and practical techniques for accessing imagination whenever they need it. "
activity_description_1746377729374478952: Remember Who You Are | Soul Awakening "Life doesn't always unfold the way we planned. Sometimes we find ourselves questioning our direction, repeating the same patterns, or feeling ready for something more without knowing where to begin. Real transformation starts by looking beneath the surface. If the foundations are no longer supporting the life you want to create, they need to be rebuilt. Join Soul Architect Amber Doyle for a powerful and uplifting workshop that combines intuitive channelling with practical tools for lasting change. Amber will share the guidance the group most needs to hear while helping you uncover what may be holding you back, reconnect with yourself, and create stronger foundations rooted in clarity, confidence, and self trust. This is an opportunity to clear space for new possibilities, trust your own path, and step into your next chapter with intention. You will leave feeling lighter, empowered, and ready to move forward with a renewed sense of purpose and a deeper connection to yourself. "
activity_description_1746377739046543976:
Meet the tarot deck: The story of the fool Join Hannah to learn all about the rider waite tarot deck as we see the story of the fool card unfolding. Hannah will be teaching you the numerology, symbols, astrology and meaning of the major arcana cards helping you to understand how to read tarot that little bit more. Suitable for beginners and advance, no experience needed

Additional session: Let the body talk- exploring the energetic body Explore the energetic body with Hannah as we discuss what energy is and how to work through healing modalities and chakra work. activity_description_1746377760974365288: From Chaos to Calm: Festival Recovery Yoga with Maura "Join Maura for a feel-good festival recovery yoga class designed to release tension, restore energy and gently rebalance your seven chakras. Whether you're feeling tired, buzzing or somewhere in between, you'll leave feeling more open, refreshed and ready for whatever the rest of the weekend brings. Come as you are. activity_description_1746377774043816552:

activity_description_1746377797808743016: Sass & Shimmy with Polaris Fusion Bellydance "Discover the magic of fusion bellydance in this fun, feel-good workshop perfect for complete beginners. activity_description_1746377806650335848: Womb Wisdom Through the Celtic Seasons "Join us for a nourishing and empowering journey into womb wisdom. activity_description_1746388528717457408:
Energy Reset Session: Reiki, Human Garage & Pychosenasry 
Join Nicoline & Luke (2 very expreniced Remove Blocks Coaches) from The Healing Forest in Kilternan in Dublin at Electric Picnic for a energy clearing and reset session designed to bring your body, mind, and energy system back into balance.

We’ll begin with Human Garage-inspired techniques, combining gentle functional movement, fascial unwinding, and breathwork to release physical tension and open the body’s energy pathways. Next, we move into Pychosenasry—a quiet yet powerful practice that uses visualisation to support deep internal release, helping to shift blocked or stagnant energy without sound or active movement.

We’ll close with Reiki, guiding you into a deeply relaxed, meditative state while working to clear energy blocks from your chakras and remove energetic cords or ties that may be draining or holding you back. This final phase supports full-body integration, clarity, and energetic renewal.
activity_description_1746388535034079232:
Tune into Peace - Soundbath with Alchemy of Sound
A gentle, restorative soundbath with crystal and tibetan singing bowls, designed to help you to relax easily and effortlessly. Expect a soothing, nurturing soundscape accompanied with Caroline's intuitive vocals to help you tune into peace.
activity_description_1746388541610747904:
Tai Chi
"A session with Ross Cousens exploring the principles of Tai Chi — a movement-based mind/body system cultivating centeredness, relaxation, flow, stability, and a little fun along the way.

The benefits are threefold:

Stillness Within — Developing inner calm in mind and body. Like standing in a sunlit field with a gentle breeze, stillness brings clarity, the way still water runs clear.

Stillness in Motion — Carrying that calm into action. Moving through life with awareness intact — like walking that same field, warm sun on your skin, present and appreciating every step forward.

Stillness Preserved — The real test. When clouds gather and pressure mounts, the stillness doesn’t leave — because you’ve made it yours. Whatever the challenge, you carry the warmth within you.

Tai Chi isn’t just movement. It’s learning to remain yourself, whatever life brings.
"

activity_description_1749186567974900416:
Whether you know him for Kearney, Karney, Kearnage or Key4050, under ‘K’ in electronic music’s encyclopedia is where you’ll find him. Powered by life, musically Bryan’s either done it, is about to … or it just ain’t his thing. Covering the broadest-of-broad electronic music scopes, ‘energy’s Kearney’s only keyword … and ‘why limit yourself?’ his only maxim. Where those points cross lies the ignition for every one of his K-initialled enterprises.   

 Many will best recognise him for his solo work, or his smartly cultivated production/vocal team-ups – ones that have brought a convoy of floorward-thinking anthems and future classics to fans. Notably among them have been two ASOT Tunes of The Year (most recently with 2022’s Plumb-sung ‘Take This’).

Under his Karney mask, tech-infected numbers like ‘Snarl’, ‘Rumination’, ‘Smiler’ and ‘Compromise’ have served his darker, dirtier studio inclinations, finding set-favour with scene icons like Adam Beyer and others. Through their back-to-the-roots ‘Tales Of The Temple’ project and globe-circling shows, as Key4050, he and John O’Callaghan elevated the collaboration dynamic to an entirely new level. 

However, it is as a standalone artist and mainstage operator that he’s today most swiftly recognised. He’s a DJ who can read an audience’s innermost desires at a thousand yards and hold them rapt in his palm for seven or more concert-performing hours.

Be it Kearney, Karney, Kearnage or Key4050, his position in electronic music’s hall of fame’s long since been secured ... Find him there under ‘K’
activity_description_1751420273183499020: Described as 'Ireland's darkest jewel' and 'like an episode of Twin Peaks in female form', Laura Sheeran has always pushed the boundaries – from her earliest CD-R releases in the 2000s to her accomplished and critically acclaimed album releases in the 2010s. Now, after a seven-year hiatus from music, Sheeran returns with a new multimedia project, PERSONA.
activity_description_1751420285296648972:
Formed in 2023, Huartan have created an original blend of Irish traditional music and electronica, quickly earning them recognition, including the 2025 BBC Introducing NI Artist of the Year award, the 2024 NI Music Prize Live Act of the Year, and the inaugural Amhrán na Laoch competition by Hot Press. Through bold reinterpretations of at-risk Irish language songs, their mission is to connect contemporary audiences with the oral singing tradition and native language of Ulster.

Emerging from the Gaeltacht quarter of West Belfast, Huartan is formed by three Irish traditional singers and musicians — Catriona Ní Ghribín, Múlú, and Stiofán Ó Luachráin, who also serves as the band’s producer — alongside masked performers who embody the presence of the síogaí (fairy folk).  Each artist is highly accomplished: Catriona also performs with the Mary Wallopers, Múlú with Biird. Together, they share a commitment to preserving and pushing the boundaries of Irish language song.
activity_description_1751420301125952268:
From national and regional press and Brian Eno joining them on stage, to providing the soundtrack to one of the biggest trials in modern music history - Na Cairde was born out of a necessity for silenced voices, and have already divided opinions. The all-Irish band performed at all of Kneecap's court dates outside of British courthouses and led the protest with Irish rebel songs in reaction to Mo Chara's slanderous terror charges.
The group had been individually making their own music separately for a few years before coming together to form the group right there on the steps of Westminster Magistrates Court in front of a crowd of a few hundred flag-bearing protesters, and have since put together a setlist of their own fuzzy blend of rock n roll anthems. Bordering between Celtic hymns and psychedelic grunge.
activity_description_1751420310110151436:
Dublin-born Irish-Greek artist Melina Malone is quickly becoming one of the most exciting voices in neo-soul. Praised for her powerhouse vocals and emotive songwriting, Melina has carved out a unique space for herself with her debut album Aphrodite (October 2023). Drawing from iconic neo soul stars Erykah Badu and Jill Scott, alongside modern artists like Lianne La Havas and RAYE - her sound is a captivating blend of honest lyrics, sultry melodies, and an eclectic mix of genres.


Since the release of Aphrodite, Melina has made waves in both the Irish and international music scenes. She opened for Grammy-winning jazz legend Gregory Porter at his sold-out Cork Opera House show and has shared stages with iconic acts like Macy Gray and Morcheeba. Her breakout year also saw her perform at Ireland Music Week, receive a stunning 9/10 album review from Hotpress Magazine, and garner support from BBC Radio 1, RTE 2FM, Notion, Noctis Mag, Today FM and more.
activity_description_1751420334101570316:
The Leon Stax Equation are a 6 piece soul band based in Galway, Ireland. Since forming in 2023 they have released 2 albums, made #3 in the Irish independent album Charts and toured the UK, USA, mainland Europe and of course, Ireland. Born 2nd youngest in a family of 10, band leader Leon Stax took influences from all genres coming through the stereo in his vibrant home. Through playing in various bands with his 2 brothers, Leon finally came to find that his true calling was in Soul music.

After many years of quietly writing he put together a band in Galway in 2023 which became The Leon Stax Equation. They are a group driven by breakbeat drumming, smoky vocals and catchy brass hooks. It is music meant to make you feel...
Live they are a force to be reckoned with. Their most recent Irish tour saw them sellout shows in Galway, Cork and their hometown of Trim. They are no strangers to the festival stage either, with high energy shows at Electric Picnic, Ealu Le Grá, Love Is a Stranger, Beyond the Pale and of course, Cork Jazz Festival. 
They have played abroad including the famous Next Door Records London, the City Winery Manhattan and Shrine, Harlem NYC. Self produced and working out of their barn studio in County Meath. In the studio the band have a live recorded feel and analog sound that picks up where the Soul and Rock classics of the 1960's left off.
activity_description_1751420346407658252: The Weaving is Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich (accordion, vocals), Owen Spafford (fiddle) and Cáit Ní Riain (piano, vocals). This trio brings together the rich musical traditions of three counties Kerry, Tipperary and Yorkshire, their three regions of origin. Their music is imbued with the driving rhythms of the Gaeltacht of West Kerry where they first met; fierce dance music and raw harmonies inspired by a deep understanding of their musical inheritance.
activity_description_1751420356759200524: An Chéad Ghlúin Eile (The Next Generation) is an award-winning sean-nós folk duo formed by native Irish-speaking sisters Étáin and Máire Ní Churraoin from the Ráth Chairn Gaeltacht in County Meath. The grandnieces of the legendary singer Darach Ó Catháin, they are renowned for blending rich, contemporary vocal harmonies with traditional Irish music.
activity_description_1751420364157952780: Featuring Domhan, Julie Goo & TransAtlantic. The "Mnásome Lives" initiative, spearheaded by creator Breda Larkin, focuses on celebrating and elevating female voices across music, art, and entertainment. It has featured high-energy cabarets and discos at venues like Cyprus Avenue in Cork, with a specific focus on highlighting that "female is not a genre".
activity_description_1751420374417220364:
Just Alice’ is a rising singer-songwriter from the Irish midlands, blending folk, Americana, and country influences with heartfelt, honest storytelling. She takes inspiration from artists like Dolly Parton, Adrienne Lenker & Passenger. 
Her love of songwriting comes from her roots in the traditional Irish music scene, as well as her musical theatre background, where she picked up a love for storytelling.
Known for her intimate live sets and lyrics that stay with you, she brings emotion to the forefront of every performance. From the quiet corners of the midlands to festival stages, she wants to share her music and connect with every listener. She is currently working on her debut EP which will be released later this year.
activity_description_1751420385339187980: Rory Sweeney is a hard artist to define, having made a name for himself as one of the key artists in the Irish Underground. His solo music is high drama, defined by glitchy electronics and cinematic balladry. He is mostly known for his acclaimed production work for artists such as Sello, Curtisy, Kojaque, Aoife Wolf, EMBY, Sloucho and Pippa Molony amongst others, seamlessly traversing mainstream and underground sounds. "Undoubtedly one of the most exciting producers to emerge from Ireland in the last few years, Rory’s sound is untameable; floating anywhere between autotuned hyper-pop, grime, footwork and hardcore" - Plain Sailing Belfast
activity_name_1751420393417417484: Mungo's Hi Fi feat Cian Finn & Special Guests
activity_description_1751420393417417484: Mungo’s Hi Fi is a renowned Scottish sound system, production house, and record label based in Glasgow. Founded in 2000 by Tom Tattersall and Doug Paine, the group is known for pioneering a modern, heavy, and dancefloor-friendly blend of Jamaican reggae, dub, dancehall, and UK bass music.
activity_description_1751420423792567052: Denise Mwaka Chaila is an Irish-Zambian rapper, singer, poet, grime and hip hop artist based in Limerick. The singer went on to release her first album ‘Go Bravely’, in October 2020 and has been a favourite in the local music scene throughout her career.
activity_description_1751420433917616908: Hidden Orchestra is an "imagined orchestra" created by composer/producer/multi-instrumentalist , its sole constant member. Recordings feature a wide variety of guest musicians from different musical backgrounds; they're recorded separately and combined by  in his studio to create the illusion of an orchestra. His dark, orchestral textures are layered with field recordings, basses, and layers upon layers of drums and percussion. Originally formed in Edinburgh in 2009 and currently based in Brighton,  also serves as musical director and assembles musicians to perform live.
activity_description_1751420441870017292: John Francis Flynn is an Irish singer and multi-instrumentalist whose work traverses the worlds of traditional and contemporary folk music. He is a founder member of the Traditional Irish folk band Skippers’ Alley. His solo work combines traditional material with influences from the worlds of post-punk, electronica, improvisation and contemporary music. His second album Look Over the Wall, See the Sky was released in 2023 and was nominated for the Choice Music Award.
activity_description_1751420449713365772: Felispeaks, also known as Felicia Olusanya, is a prominent Nigerian-Irish spoken-word poet, performer, and playwright based in Ireland. Her work powerfully explores themes of feminism, coming-of-age, and the Black-Irish experience. She is well-known for her Leaving Cert poem "For Our Mothers"
activity_description_1751420456097096460:
Eleanor McEvoy is one of Ireland's foremost songwriters. She is the composer, co-performer and producer of "A Woman's Heart", the title track for the best selling Irish album in Irish history. In May 2019, the song was voted by the Irish public as being in the top 10 of Ireland's favourite folk songs. It features regularly on screen, most recently in 2019 in the award winning sit-com "Derry Girls".

Eleanor began her career as a session musician in Dublin, playing for numerous recordings and artists including U2, Sinead O'Connor and Mary Black. Eleanor released her eponymous debut on Geffen Records in LA, followed by tours in the USA, Europe and the Far East. She moved to Columbia Records in New York for her second album "What's Following Me?". Since then, Eleanor's gone on to become an artist and performer known throughout the world. Her critically acclaimed cannon of work spans sixteen albums, there are numerous cover versions of her songs by performers such as Emmy Lou Harris, Mary Black, Phil Coulter, Mary Coughlan, Eliza Carty, Jack L, Derek Ryan and band Saint Sister.
activity_description_1751420463361630988: Mairéad has been producing recordings of integrity, vision and passion as well as unforgettable moving performances for almost four decades. Her music has journeyed through the road less traveled since departing her hometown of Dublin some 30 years ago. Now, in 2026 she is releasing her most ambitious works to date, a triple album of originals, cover recordings, and a compilation of live concert recordings from her famed Muse Garden & Muse Room Shows over the past ten years.
activity_description_1751420470441616140: The Inishbofin Céilí Band is a traditional Irish music group deeply rooted in the culture of Inishbofin Island, County Galway. Featuring a core of local multi-generational musicians, the band performs regularly at island events, pubs like Day's, and major regional festivals, keeping the spirited rhythms of West of Ireland traditional music alive.
activity_description_1751420486438691596:
‘Millennium Madness’ is the first full-length project from Shampain - The EP is set across 12 months spent in Galway’s city centre. It explores the sounds and atmospheres of the town. Its structures, nature, surrounding suburbs and villages across the four seasons in the tumultuous seaside town.
Themes of night and day, good vs evil, technology vs humans and city vs nature are all apparent from track to track. In that vein, the EP is split in two halves; Spring/Summer & Autumn/Winter - loosely depicted by the front and back artworks by Sean Kennedy & Conor Ostheimer. Contributions across the EP come from talented Irish artists and fellow Galwegians Bethany, Julie Dawson (of Newdad fame) and Rachel Trench, while Cork’s Elaine Malone also adds some vocals to the final track ‘Tearduct’. Spinning from ambient to intense, ‘Millenium Madness’ is set to reflect the contradictions that run throughout G Town; the constant chaos and noisiness to total serenity within 5 minutes of each other; something akin to a Shampain DJ set. The cold rigidity of its infrastructure takes on the form of drum machines, pedals, mixers and synths that’re set against real, raw recordings taken from the River Corrib, pub smoking areas, walks to and from work and many, many days of pouring rain.
‘Millenium Madness’ - much like the Salthill disco its name is taken from - takes you on a trip through subversive and effective dance music and spits you right back out again into the real world.
activity_description_1751420494768579340: The Latchikos are an electrifying acoustic band formed on the west coast of Ireland, known for originating "Gyp-Hop" (Gaelic gypsy hip-hop). Fronted by charismatic actor, musician, and storyteller Aindrias de Staic, the trio fuses traditional Irish fiddle with Spanish flamenco guitar, driving tribal percussion (cajón), and rapid-fire spoken word
activity_description_1751420502435767052: A story-teller, word-smith and dexterous musician with a strong imagination, Kean’s career is set to project far beyond his Irish roots with his unique blend of Indie Rock, Americana and Irish folk influences, Kean’s music is resonating far and wide since the release of his critically acclaimed debut album ’The County Star’ which was released last year.
activity_description_1751420511059256076: Music Generation Harp Collective (30 Harps) is a unique collaboration of harp ensembles from MG Laois, Louth, Mayo, and Waterford. Bringing together talented young harpers across Ireland, the collective performs at events and festivals nationally and internationally. The ensemble is known for its creative approach, composing and arranging much of its own repertoire while collaborating with leading professional musicians and composers, including Gráinne Meyer, Catriona McKay and Michael Rooney. Previous performances have included the World Harp Congress in Cardiff, the Edinburgh International Harp Festival, Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann, CÉHI’s Harps Alive Festival, and St. Patrick’s Festival, Dublin. Most recently, the collective performed in the National Concert Hall as part of the Festival of Youth Orchestras. The Harp Collective is directed by Siobhán Buckley, Deirdre Ní Bhuachalla, Gráinne Hambly, and Jill Devlin. The project is co-funded by Music Generation, the Arts Council, the Department of Education, U2, and The Ireland Funds.
activity_name_1751420522484540172: Dónal Lunny, Máirtín O'Connor & Zoë Conway
activity_description_1751420522484540172:
This super group brings together the dazzling talents of three of the country’s finest traditional musicians; button accordion master Máirtín O’Connor, fiddle player Zoë Conway and guitar and bouzouki player Donal Lunny. Don’t miss this illustrious trio in what promises to be an atmospheric and unforgettable gig, drawing on an eclectic mix of the old and new where traditional tunes and songs meet each of their diverse influences and unique compositional voices.
 
"Donal Lunny, a man who has been at the coal face of Irish music for the past five decades."
Hot Press

"Virtuoso - one of Ireland’s most gifted young musicians."
The Irish Independent on Zoe Conway 

"“Máirtín O’Connor is a squeeze box player in the very top echelon."
Irish Music Magazine
activity_description_1751420531921724172:
Sisters Maighread and Tríona Ní Dhomhnaill belong to a renowned singing family originally from the Donegal Gaeltacht. The unique style and repertoire of traditional singing they represent so gloriously comes down to them through generations of the Ó Domhnaill family. Added to this is
their distinctive unison and harmonic interpretations of Donegal songs and their fluent and accomplished singing to instrumental accompaniment.
activity_description_1751420541258244876: The Celtic group Dordan consists of a trio of women from County Galway, including tin-whistle player Mary Bergin, harpist Kathleen Loughnane and fiddler Dearbhail Standun. Dordan, whose name means "drone" in Gaelic, released their first album Jigs To The Moon in 1994, and gained more attention for their Narada Christmas album The Night Before … A Celtic Christmas. They released another album for Narada, Celtic Aire, in 1999 and one for Shanachie, Irish Traditional & Baroque Music, the same year.
activity_description_1751420548212400908: Inni-K (Eithne Ní Chatháin) is a singer, multi-instrumentalist, and songwriter whose music draws from her background in sean-nós and traditional Irish music, while boldly venturing into new sonic territory. Her fourth studio album, Still A Day (out 26 Sept 2025 via Green Willow Records), is her most emotionally charged and sonically expansive work to date. Produced by Seán Mac Erlaine, the album weaves Ní Chatháin’s voice and fiddle into ambient textures, hushed jazz motifs, and rich harmonic landscapes—shaping a sound both rooted and radically open. Though sean-nós is absent in form, its spirit lingers in the phrasing and poise that underpins the record. Her 2022 album Iníon was a contemporary sean-nós triumph, earning two RTÉ Folk Award nominations and being named a Top of the World release by Songlines. Earlier releases The Hare & the Line (2019) and The King Has Two Horse’s Ears (2015) established her as a vital voice in Irish songwriting. Known for powerful live performances, Inni-K has played Irish Arts Center (NY), Centre Culturel Irlandais (Paris), Symphony Hall (Birmingham), and National Concert Hall (Dublin). Joined for this very special show by the UCD Gamlan Orchestra.
activity_description_1751427903469724476: Laoise Kelly, from Westport, Co. Mayo, now based on Achill Island, is regarded as one of Ireland’s leading harpers. A pioneer of a distinctive, driving style of Irish harping, she has released the acclaimed solo albums Just Harp, Ceis and Fáilte Uí Cheallaigh. Laoise has collaborated with artists including Seamus Heaney, The Chieftains, Christy Moore, Sharon Shannon, Kate Bush and Tim O’Brien, appearing on more than 80 recordings. She has performed at major festivals worldwide including WOMAD, Celtic Connections and Celtic Colours. She recently performed for President Connolly at Áras an Uachtarán and for President Zelensky at the opening ceremony of Ireland's EU presidency. She was awarded TG4 Gradam Ceoil Musician of the Year in 2020, recognising her outstanding contribution to Irish traditional music.
activity_name_1751427920062391100: Luke Webb, Robert Harvey & Oisín McCann
activity_description_1751427920062391100: Luke Webb is an exciting young Irish traditional harper. To date, Luke has performed at an array of spectacular venues and festivals such as the National Concert Hall, Edinburgh International Harp Festival & Electric Picnic. His upcoming debut album will be released in late 2026 featuring some of his nationally and internationally debuted compositions. Joining Luke are fellow musicians Robert Harvey (whistle) and Oisín McCann (bodhrán & guitar) for a performance celebrating the richness and versatility of Irish traditional music.
activity_description_1751427928341947196: BRÍDÍN, modern folk harper, singer songwriter and composer from County Sligo, Ireland creates her music in her own modern and ethereal style. BRÍDÍN was brought up surrounded by Irish traditional music. When writing her own music in her creative new style, she is inspired by her roots and her natural surroundings in County Sligo. Over the years she has achieved many accolades for her musical ability including RTÉ Folk Awards Nominee and All Ireland Fleadh Titles. Her love of music led her to pursue a musical career, having studied music at University College Cork achieving a degree in Music and Irish and Masters in Music and Performance. She released her debut self-titled album in 2022 and has since been performing solo shows and with her band in Ireland and abroad.
activity_description_1751427946587169596: Jennifer Leahy is an award-winning harper and composer from County Meath. Rooted in the Irish harping tradition, she brings a fresh, contemporary perspective to the instrument through performance, composition and collaboration. Jennifer’s music explores Irish folklore and the supernatural through a neo-traditional lens. She is currently preparing for the release of her debut solo EP, comprised of original pieces influenced by the myths of County Meath. An international performer, Jennifer has toured across Europe and internationally at events including the World Harp Congress in Sydney. In 2025, she performed as a special guest alongside Alex Warren at Dublin’s 3Arena.
activity_description_1751427955755918140: Having met while studying at TU Dublin Conservatoire, TRIAD, an Irish harp trio, is a highly sought-after ensemble that boasts three exceptional talents active as performers and teachers across Ireland – Dublin, Meath, Westmeath, Wexford and Wicklow. An active group with a passion for sharing their love of Irish harp, TRIAD gave their inaugural performance at the Highlanes Gallery, Drogheda as part of An Chúirt Chruitireachta 2021 and performed at An Grianán, Co. Louth for the 2022 festival. Other performance highlights include at the CÉHI Harps Plus + Symposium at TU Dublin, Farmleigh House, Cornstown House ‘Music on the Farm’ series, Stoneybatter Festival, the inaugural Smithfield Fleadh and in CÉHI’s online programming for Lá na Cruite| Harp Day, St. Patrick’s Day celebrations and their ‘12 Days of Christmas’ series. The trio recently premiered Seán Doherty’s ‘Three Great Waves’ at Cairde na Cruite’s An Chúirt Chruitireachta 40th International Harp Festival.
activity_description_1751427964782060348: As Ireland’s foremost harp duo Cormac and Anne-Marie have been playing together for many years.  Their original and inventive presentations reflect the marriage of Ireland’s oral musical heritage and the classical tradition from baroque to the present. Highlights of their Irish performances include an appearance at the Beó Festival at the National Concert Hall and the World Harp Congress in Dublin. They have performed throughout Europe at international events such as the European Harp Symposium in Amsterdam and Lyon, the inaugural concert of the Irish Cultural Centre, Paris, Harpe Diem in Belgium, and for Cruit Éireann|Harp Ireland in South Korea. They have made numerous appearances on radio and television in Ireland and elsewhere in Europe.  Their duo albums, Double Strung and Duopoly have received critical acclaim following their release.
activity_description_1751427972650574652: Úna Ní Fhlannagáin is an award-winning exponent of the modern Irish harp, fusing the nuance and 'drive!' of Irish traditional music with jazz and pop influences. Prizewinner of the Riada Gold Medal for Harp, she has performed all over the world, with Grammy and Emmy-winners. Entranced by the bell-like resonance of the ancient Irish harp, supported by Music Network, she plays a brand new type of harp - a hybrid of the early Gaelic harp and the modern Irish harp. Her revolutionary new instrument has the bronze strings and the one-piece soundbox of the early Gaelic harp, while having the string-spacing, range and ‘sharping’ levers of a modern Irish harp, thus enabling the player to perform a wide range of textures and genres. Úna will share this magical new sound with Electric Picnic listeners at this year's festival.
activity_description_1751427982289085244: Eimear Coughlan from Tulla in Co. Clare continues the musical heritage of her grandfather Paddy Canny. As a multi-instrumentalist, she has performed on several music tours throughout Europe and the US. Over the past number of years, Eimear has accumulated many All Ireland titles at Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann and has performed and taught at numerous Traditional Irish Music festivals throughout Ireland and abroad. While also a fiddle player, Eimear learned her music from her grandfather and in more recent times, she has been performing with the highly acclaimed Tulla Céilí Band.
activity_description_1751428000601416508: Belfast harper and composer Ursula Burns has spent over three decades challenging perceptions of the harp, contrasting sharply Romantic and Troubled Ireland with her upbringing on the Falls Road. Through her fearless stage persona The Dangerous harpist, she has taken the instrument on a journey across theatre, circus, magic, dance, comedy, and performance art. She has built a unique style, blending technical skill with personality and innovation. Burns draws on Ireland’s roots while pushing the harp into new territories. Her seventh album, The Secret Melodies of Trees, produced by Dónal O’Connor and featuring John McSherry, has received worldwide acclaim as “a timeless masterpiece of contemporary music.” Critics praise its instrumental mastery, dreamlike innovation, emotional depth, and ability to redefine the harp while honouring its heritage. At the CÉHI stage, Ursula will focus on her core harping and composition, performing a selection of tracks from The Secret Melodies of Trees.
activity_description_1751428011506606908: Deirdre Granville and Aoife Granville are sisters from Dingle rooted in the musical traditions of Corca Dhuibhne and the Blasket Islands. Acclaimed performers and recording artists, they have toured internationally and collaborated with leading Irish musicians. Their new duo album Ceo Draíochta was released in July 2026.
activity_description_1751428020750852924: Cruitirí Loch Garman/Wexford Harp Ensemble was launched in 2008 by the late Mercedes Garvey (née Bolger), a proud Gorey native. Since then, the Ensemble has grown from strength to strength, becoming an important part of Wexford's musical life. From its inception, the Ensemble has been led by Aileen Kennedy, whose original compositions feature prominently in its repertoire. Under her guidance, the group has developed a distinctive musical identity. The Ensemble has performed at a range of festivals and celebrations, including Artswave Festival in Wales, Music in Monkstown, Music for Wexford concerts, and An Chúirt Chruitireachta. Annually, the Ensemble presents a Harp Day concert, complemented by a series of pop-up recitals, bringing the beauty of harp music to communities throughout Wexford. Cruitirí Loch Garman is united by a shared passion for the Irish harp and a commitment to preserving and promoting its rich musical heritage.
activity_name_1751428033308599100: Aisling Lyons, Becky Ní Éallaithe & Muireann Ní Shé
activity_description_1751428033308599100: Three exceptional artists working at the forefront of the Irish folk tradition: harper, concertina player and composer Aisling Lyons, sean-nós dancer, singer and concertina player Becky Ní Éallaithe, and uilleann piper and singer Muireann Ní Shé. Drawing on the rich traditions of their homeplaces – Cork, Connemara, and Clare, this newly formed trio presents a programme of traditional music, song and dance that honours Ireland's living oral tradition while embracing fresh creative perspectives. Themes of the feminine voice, place, and the natural world emerge in a programme developed through an ongoing artistic collaboration. Bí Liom Bí weaves together music, song and dance in performances that are both deeply rooted in tradition and unmistakably contemporary, featuring newly composed works by Lyons, Ní Shé and Ní Éallaithe. This performance is a celebration of tradition as a living, breathing artform, grounded in authenticity while driven by curiosity.
activity_description_1751428040136926012: Kathleen Loughnane and Catriona Cannon are a mother-and-daughter harp duo whose performances celebrate the rich tradition of Irish harp music while embracing a broad range of musical influences. Kathleen Loughnane is an internationally recognised harper and scholar. Co-founder of the widely acclaimed ensemble Dordán, she has toured throughout Europe, Japan and the US, taught at major harp festivals, and released five solo recordings and collections of harp arrangements. Her publications are widely used by harpers and feature on the Royal Irish Academy of Music harp syllabus. Taught by her mother, Catriona Cannon has performed across traditional, contemporary and experimental genres. She toured Europe with the award-winning Irish reggae band Intinn and has collaborated with artists including Laura Sheeran, Holly Cook, and Cian Finn. She is Head of Heritage Collections at the University of Galway, where her interests in archives and cultural heritage complement her lifelong engagement with Irish musical traditions.
activity_description_1751428051117613884: Irish harper Tríona Marshall is celebrated for the expressive depth and radiant tone of her playing, combining Irish traditional, classical, and contemporary music. Her performances are marked by emotional clarity, subtle virtuosity, and a profound sense of connection with audiences. Trained in Den Hague and London, she became principal harper with the RTÉ Concert Orchestra before launching her solo career in the care of The Chieftains in 2003 with whom she toured internationally for almost two decades. Tríona has performed in many of the world’s leading concert halls and collaborated with artists across a wide range of styles. Returning to her roots Tríona performs with a more personal voice, weaving together traditional airs, contemporary Irish compositions, and her own arrangements. Whether in an intimate theatre or a grand concert hall, Tríona’s playing draws listeners into the stillness, clarity, and deep resonance present in the sound of the Irish harp.
activity_description_1751428069966816060: Music Generation Mayo Harp Ensemble is made up of young musicians hailing from all parts of County Mayo, directed by acclaimed musicians Gráinne Hambly and William Jackson. Their repertoire includes a mix of traditional and newly composed Irish and Scottish tunes. Recent performances include annual Harp Day performances at Foxford Traditional Weekend, An Chúirt Chruitireachta Ensemble Day, Tionól for Harps and Pipes, and the World Harp Congress in Cardiff. In 2025 the ensemble was honoured to perform support for trad supergroup BIIRD at their sold-out show in Claremorris Townhall Theatre. The ensemble are performing at the World Harp Congress in Toronto this July and are excited to perform on the Cruit Éireann|Harp Ireland stage at Croí/Electric Picnic for the first time.
activity_description_1751428081551483708: The Music Generation Laois Harp Ensemble was established in 2015 under the direction of Siobhan Buckley and has collaborated with many musicians and composers to create new music. These include Catriona McKay and Chris Stout, Michael Rooney, Maeve Gilchrist, and Ernestine Healy. Live performances include the US Ambassador to Ireland's Residence, An Chúirt Chruitereachta International Festival for Irish Harp, The Edinburgh International Harp Festival, Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann, St Patrick's Festival Dublin, The World Harp Congress in Cardiff and Toronto, Forest Fest, Electric Picnic, and a 10 day tour of Japan with Michael Rooney and June McCormack with performances in Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka. TV appearances include The Ray d'Arcy Show, News2Day, Morning Ireland, Fleadh TV, Ceiliúradh LGFA Peil na mBan, Ireland AM, they also featured on Morning Ireland on RTÉ Radio 1 and recorded on the title track of singer songwriter John Spillane's recent album '100 Snow White Horses'.
