activity_description_1751428097993155388: Music Generation Louth Harp Ensemble, founded in 2014, under the direction of Deirdre Ní Bhuachalla, offers opportunities for young harpers in Louth, to perform at the highest level. They have performed at World Harp Congress in Cardiff, Edinburgh Harp Festival, Féile na Tána and An Chúirt Chruitireachta. Alongside other MG harp ensembles, they form Music Generation Ireland Harp Collective, which has performed at Belfast TradFest, Féile na Tána, CÉHI’s Harps Alive Festival, and the National Concert Hall. Collaboration and creativity lie at the heart of the Music Generation ethos. The MGL Ensemble and the Harp Collective are experienced in composing and arranging music in collaboration with professional artists, including Michael Rooney, Alannah Thornburgh, Gráinne Meyer, Máire Ní Chathasaigh, and Catriona McKay. Locally, they composed original music for Indian Classical dancer Karinova Mathew, and are currently working on a Cruit Éireann commission with local award-winning harper and composer Donnchadh MacAodh.
activity_description_1751428117236622140: Uaithne are five acclaimed Irish harpers and Music Generation ensemble directors — Gráinne Hambly, Deirdre Ní Bhuachalla, Siobhan Buckley, Rachel Duffy, and Jill Devlin — who came together through their work leading youth harp ensembles across Ireland. United by a shared passion for performance, education, and collaboration, they combine their diverse musical influences to create engaging and innovative harp ensemble music. Returning to Electric Picnic on the Cruit Éireann|Harp Ireland stage for the second time, their collaboration celebrates both the rich heritage and contemporary evolution of the Irish harp, showcasing the instrument’s beauty, versatility, and enduring relevance.
activity_description_1752209373792603072: A thoughtful selection of curious electronica, lazy beats and spacious dub to soundtrack the morning after.
activity_description_1752209400535485376: Kerry DJ & vinyl collector blending African rhythms, funk and electronic sounds
activity_description_1752209416406731712: Checkpoint Charlie brings a vibrant mix of Balkan beats and global grooves. Known for blending traditional sounds with fresh rhythms from around the world.
activity_description_1752209423755152320: For over twenty years Eddie B has been one of Kilkenny’s most popular selectors, having racked up a series of residencies over the years in venues such as Billy Byrnes, Cleeres Theatre and Set Theatre. He has filled dancefloors at numerous festivals in the city such as Kilkenny Pride, Kilkenny Cat Laughs and Kilkenny Animated. With his magic box of vinyl tricks, he spins an eclectic mix of disco, funk, soul, 90’s R&B and a never ending supply of pop bangers to suit eveyones tatse.
activity_description_1752209439609621440: French native Cyriac is the host of the excellent The Main Ingredient on DDR. Driven by a bottomless thirst for musical discovery, his sets span genres and regions but with special mention for his forays into music from the Nordeste of Brazil, and the caribbean islands of Martinique & Guadeloupe.
activity_description_1752209448803535808: the se7en inch collective, for the love of 7" vinyl. The genre bending soundclash jukebox !
activity_description_1752209459935218624: Spinning vinyl since the 1990s, Mattie B has been delivering raw and soulful grooves from underground clubs to outdoor festival stages for over three decades. Cutting his teeth in the golden era of rave and early house, his sets have blended gritty soul and funk classics with rare disco pressings, house classics, and electrifying breakbeats. Like many seasoned selectors, the focus is always on the record and the crowd crafting moments that feel timeless he has a reputation for dynamic sets that traverse decades of dancefloor history. Each performance is an invitation to get down and groove and feel the soul in the music expect warm rhythms, tribal drums, vintage basslines, and impeccable groove selection
activity_description_1752209471134010304: The Woohah Hip Hop & Chess events were started by Chris Thomas in Bristol before he eventually relocated to Cork and linked up with renouned record digger and turntablist JusMe. The concept is simple. Classic hip hop records and Chessboards. No Tournaments or Formalities. Just good music, relaxed atmosphere and Chess including a jumbo board with pieces that are almost 3ft tall! Chris and Jus are bringing a couple friends along. Cuttin Heads Collective residents Rostah and Itchi will be helping out on the decks for the afternoon too!
activity_description_1752209480017546176: Jonezy has been hustlin around the Irish bass music scene for about 15 years now. Following several years as a resident at flagship Irish dubstep crew, DubCulture, Jonezy launched his own promotion concept, Riseup!, in 2010 to explore a broader take on modern rave sounds and bring key, cutting edge acts to Cork. High profile acts such as Mala,Objekt,Pangaea,D-bridge,Skeptical and Youngsta all made appearences.In addition to his hard-won mad-skills behind the decks, Jonezy’s vast horde of ridiculous records is as fine an anthology as any in Ireland. Soulful reggae classics, hidden jungle gems, the latest Machester hybrid halftime weapon – Jonezy mashes the dance and puts it back together with ease.In 2014 Jonezy & his dad a trained chippy started building The RiseUp! Soundsystem and it was ready for it's first outing in 2016. The RiseUp! Sound is known for it's heavy rumble, precision top end and is known as one of the best Soundsystems in the country .
activity_description_1752209499864992704: Dj, producer and owner of Crossroads Recording Studio in Kilkenny, Ireland. Home to a wall of boutique analog gear and a vinyl cutting lathe. His love for analog sound is very noticeable not only in his music but also in his vinyl only DJ sets. Expect lots of Funk, Soul, Disco, House and everything in between. Swiss has released music on Kingstreet Sounds NYC, Maison Roughe UK and has a release dropping this year on Lumberjack’s In Hell and a debut album with his live band East West Assembly, forthcoming on the iconic Sound Signature run by Theo Parrish.
activity_description_1752209508572367808: Local Groove Records is a DJ duo and independent record label founded by two lifelong friends from Waterford, Ireland, brought together by a shared passion for digging records and uncovering forgotten gems. What began as years spent collecting vinyl and DJing together evolved into a distinctive sound rooted in rare boogie, disco, and world groove records.Known for their deep crates and carefully curated selections, Local Groove Records deliver energetic, groove driven sets packed with records rarely found on streaming platforms.
activity_description_1752209525316029376: Obsessive record collector, turntablist and party rocker JusMe began DJing in Cork at the end of the 90s. He got his start battling as a Hip Hop DJ before moving on to promoting shows through the Hobo Convention and Cuttin' Heads Collective crews, with a focus on championing forward-thinking Irish artists. Over the years hes warmed up for artists such as DJ Shadow, Havoc (Mobb Deep), The Pharcyde, Nightmares On Wax and Macy Gray to name a few. Owner of one of Corks deepest and most eclectic vinyl collections, JusMe's sets are driven by a lifelong obsession with good music. Drawing influence from Classic House and Disco, Latin Grooves, UK Bass Music, and Detroit Techno, his sets blend turntablism with thoughtful selections, unexpected transitions and an infectious sense of fun.
activity_description_1752209534811933632: Rockin Records, Rockin Records, Rock The Records, The Guy Rocks Rocords
activity_description_1752209545129921472: Chartini is a Waterford based vinyl collector  with a deep love for rare funk, boogie, Afro beat and disco sounds. Expect timeless rhythms and soulful selections chosen with real love behind them.
activity_description_1752209555741510592: Rooted in rhythm and guided by feel, Eile sets are inspired by R&B and Latin sounds. Expect earthy grooves, sun-soaked beats, and an open invitation to move.
activity_description_1752209563425475520: Whether dropping an Afrobeat gem into a set of Latin boogaloo or seamlessly bridging SWANA grooves with American soul, Jacqui loves nothing more than a dance at the cultural crossroads filled with musical handbrake turns. Jacqui is fresh from playing The Cambium Club at ATN, and is thrilled to be back at the Heart and Anchor Bar again this year.
activity_description_1752209579087006656: Daria's vinyl sets blend disco, soul, boogie and global sounds, celebrating connection, energy and the joy of sharing music with others. Always led by the groove...
activity_description_1752209591225322432: Since the early 90's Dandelion has been running club nights and spinning 45's in Bars, Nightclubs & at events throughout Dublin City. Her thrilling Dj sets and Iconic look have enthralled and bedazzled night owls in every corner of the capital. She has held residencies in legendary Dublin clubs Ri Ra, POD & The Kitchen and has shared stages with such luminaries as lan Dury, Kevin Rowland and Iggy Pop. Expect a hip shaking barrage of Up-tempo Northern Soul, Dancefloor Jazz, Motown, Disco, Femme &
activity_description_1752209599429381056:
An award-winning, international DJ, Sinéad Ní Mhórdha has been working her musical and production craft on-air, at residencies, events and festivals for over 20 years. 
She cut her teeth on the decks whilst working at Dublin’s Temple Bar Music Centre (now the Button Factory) where she co-founded the all-girl DJ trio - Chicks on Decks.  From there she took to the radio airwaves and TV, hostng shows for Phantom FM, FM104 and Radio Nova in Ireland and further afield in Australia, for Balcony TV in Sydney, to America’s  longest running, independent free-form radio station, WFMU in New York, then returning to Europe for Radio Monaco.  
Her musical genres are vast and woven to include Indie, Alternative, Funk, Soul, Disco, House, Electronic and ‘90s hip hop, all of which create a musical feast for the ears and body.  You’ll savour the sounds of “Ireland's First Female DJ Superstar” – The Star, at this year’s Electric Picnic 2026.
activity_name_1752209611609639872: The Night Mayor & ED IS ON
activity_description_1752209611609639872:
Two longtime stalwarts of the Irish music, festival and nightlife scene finally come together for one monumentous set — a mere five years in the making.

The Night Mayor of Dublin, aka Ray O’Donoghue, aka DJ Razor, joins forces with Edison Waters, aka EdIsOn, for a back-to-back midnight set at the Jerry Fish Stage.

With a frankly alarming 60 years combined experience in the business, expect the best tunes from over 3 decades of questionable decisions, late nights and impeccable musical taste.

Midnight.  Fish Town. History, of sorts, will be made.
activity_description_1752273223548165256:
Sir Van Morrison is one of the most influential singer-songwriters in modern music. Born in Belfast in 1945, Morrison first rose to prominence as the frontman of Them before launching a remarkable solo career spanning more than six decades. His distinctive blend of soul, R&B, blues, jazz, folk, rock and Celtic influences has produced a catalogue that includes enduring classics such as Astral Weeks, Moondance, and Into the Mystic. 

A prolific recording artist, Morrison has released more than 40 studio albums. His most recent original album, Remembering Now, was released in June 2025 and reached the UK Top 10, marking his return to original songwriting following a series of albums exploring skiffle, jazz, traditional songs and reworked material. 

In January 2026, Morrison released Somebody Tried To Sell Me A Bridge, a 20-track blues album featuring collaborations with legendary artists including Buddy Guy, Taj Mahal and Elvin Bishop. Now in his ninth decade, Morrison continues to record and perform, maintaining an extraordinary creative output and touring career.
activity_description_1752274293993268052:
Channelling the power of tried-and-true friendship and tapping into the serenity of the surrounding

countryside, Irish trio Amble harness a rare magic threaded into the fabric of their novelistic folk. The

group—Robbie Cunningham (lead vocals/guitar), Ross McNerney (mandolin/bouzouki), and Oisin McCaffrey (guitar/vocals)—have unassumingly gone from quitting their day jobs in rural Western Ireland to the doorstep of an international breakthrough buoyed by over 100 million streams and sold-out shows around the world. After just one gig together, they unlocked uncanny creative interplay with each member penning songs and pouring life experience into the lyrics. Amble fueled buzz with breakouts “Mariner Boy” and “Lonely Island,” but life changed when the band received a call from Warner Records with an offer. Signing to the label in 2024, the band had an unimaginable past year that spawned their latest EP The Commons and a captivating live presence, as they canvased North America and Europe with packed houses on both sides of the Atlantic. Their relatability, intimate storytelling, and authenticity marry seamlessly with no-frills acoustic instrumentation, serene soundscapes, and heavenly natural harmonies.
activity_description_1752311643750391320: Widely credited as one of the pioneers who brought credible underground dance music to Irish audiences, Scurry’s influence extends far beyond the dance floor. He remains a respected mentor and cultural figure within Dublin music circles, inspiring newer generations of DJs, producers and artists. His legacy is intertwined with the evolution of Dublin nightlife itself — from the early warehouse and club movement through to today’s modern electronic scene.
activity_description_1752311663513951768: Renowned as the drummer / vocalist and driving force behind Dublin's enigmatic proto prog rockers TWINKRANES. Anthony Wrasse returns to the stage as 7)LZ (Seven Levels of Lift). Swapping the acoustic drum kit for the kick drum of the 909, electronic circuitry and modular polyrhythms. The project marries unconventional song structures, avant garde compositions and dancefloor heavy arrangements, channeling kosmiche, new age, primitive techno and machine driven electronica.
activity_description_1752311679007710744:
‘Groev’ (pronounced Grove) is a Galway-based indie folk six-piece made up of Joe Sweeney, Rory O'Regan, Jack Lennox, Mike Glynn, and brothers Evan and Keagan Forde. Hailing from across the West of Ireland and formed from late-night sessions and pints, they've fully leaned into what they call a 'drinking band with a music problem'.
Drawing on Irish tradition while reaching further afield, they've carved out a sound that sits comfortably in the indie-folk world, threaded through with the craic of the West. Five songs in, each track represents a distinct slice of life in their twenties, shaped by the lived-in honesty of their influences like Amble, Kingfisher, Sam Fender, and Paolo Nutini.
With over 450,000 Spotify streams and Tara Grove landing on the Spotify Viral 50 Ireland, the numbers are growing, but it's live where Groev really comes alive. From Jack's (now legendary) dance moves to Joe and Keagan sinking pints mid-set, there's a warmth to their shows that makes you feel like you've known them for years.
With sold-out headline shows at Róisín Dubh Upstairs and Whelan's Upstairs, and having already played Momentum Festival, Galway Folk Festival, and Doolin Folk Fest, Groev are only getting started.
activity_description_1752311698108571160: Known for his seamless blending of deep house, Detroit techno, disco and acid house, Scurry earned a reputation as a “DJ’s DJ” — revered by peers and club-goers alike for both his technical skill and musical knowledge. Over the decades he has shared stages with many of the world’s leading electronic artists and played seminal clubs and festivals throughout Ireland and Europe. His appearances at legendary Irish nights including Temple of Sound, Transmission, Influx and Sea Sessions cemented his standing as a cornerstone of the Irish electronic scene.
activity_description_1752311716437679640:
Madams Last Discovery nicknamed 'Madams' are a tyrannical mix of Sean Ryder’s Happy Mondays, on a three-week Belfast bar crawl, having run into David Byrne, Grian Chatten and the devil along the way. 
Madams spent 2025 appearing at Stendhal festival, Output Belfast Festival, touring the UK/Ireland, featuring on the Scratch my Progress talent development programme as part of the Oh Yeah Music Centre, and supported artists including Inspiral Carpets and The Howlers.
The band released 3 singles throughout the year gaining them traction on BBC Introducing, RTE 2FM's New Music Show by Beta Ba Silva and Dan Hegarty's Alternative show in addition to a feature on the BBC Radio Ulster 'Where Music Matters' playlist.
To kick off 2026 Madams performed at Whelan's Ones To Watch festival and released "Orange Juice". This track was featured on BBC Radio 1 with Jess Iszatt, Radio X, RTÉ 2FM as Beta Da Silva's Track of the Week, Hot Press and more. To follow this up the band released their debut EP on the 11th of March and are performing at Ireland Music Week 2026.
activity_description_1752311728005570072: Camp flair and raw feeling, structured chaos and cinematic charm: Jean Pack introduces herself as a bold, emotionally saturated presence, a cocktail of melancholia and mischief, poured neat. Describing her sound as “a dirty aperitif with the first pint of the night,” she blends lush harmonies, lo-fi edges, sly lyricism, and storytelling that's part cabaret, part confessional. Whether performing solo or with her Slay Babies, Jean Pack has quickly built a strong reputation on the live circuit. Recently named one of the Irish Examiner's Ones to Watch for 2026, she is currently working on her debut album, with new singles set for release throughout the year. Influences span The Shangri-Las, Nancy & Lee, and The Velvet Underground, yet her voice remains unmistakably her own: vulnerable, glamorous, and half-laughing through the ache.
activity_description_1752311746057854488: Child of Prague is a band formed in 2022 born out of the alternative rock scene in Dublin. Composed of six multi-instrumentalists, each member comes from a different musical background which seamlessly blends jazz, classical and Irish traditional music influences into their folk-rock sound. Their debut EP ‘Clothed in the Sun’, was met to critical acclaim and they have been pulling live audiences across Ireland, the UK and Europe. They are set to play at the widely renowned music festival Left of the Dial in Rotterdam this October, and are supporting Irish punk band Gurriers for their Dublin headline show at the Olympia Theatre in November.
activity_description_1752311747089653272:
Jinx Lennon sings about what he believes is happening in the real world as seen through the
eyes of his border schizo punk fffolk music emanating from the Irish borderlands .Subjected in
his youth to the split screen of Republic Ireland and Northern Ireland volatile goings on and the
sort of doublethink politics no one would wish on any young head thus Jinx ended up throwing
it all into a blender along with his favorite sci fi books and mindfuckery of living in joyless holy
Eire.Now he sings it all with the aim of not making life any more unbearable for the listener
overwhelmed by modern existence
activity_description_1752311748037565976:
MayKay is one of Ireland's most distinctive and compelling performers, renowned for her fearless voice, magnetic stage presence and genre-defying songwriting. First rising to prominence as the frontwoman of Fight Like Apes before joining Le Galaxie, she has spent nearly two decades pushing creative boundaries with some of Ireland's best artists including Kormac, Elaine Mai, Jerry Fish and Jack O'Rourke. 
Her critically acclaimed self-titled debut solo album, released in 2025, marked an exciting new chapter, showcasing a more intimate and deeply personal side of her artistry through songs exploring relationships, grief and resilience. This summer, MayKay brings her super group full band show to festival stages including Beyond the Pale and All Together Now, delivering the powerful, emotionally charged live performances that have made her one of Ireland's most captivating artists.
activity_description_1752311755411152408:
He’s the Joker in the pack and he’s back, at Electric Picnic 2026! 

An Indie legend and ringmaster of exceptional renown, Jerry Fish has evolved into a showman extraordinaire, capturing the hearts and minds of audiences all over with his now legendary live shows, a unique live theatrical experience that dissolves all boundaries between performer and audience. 

“Our live performances at Electric Picnic are a mix of alternative music, theatre and the spirit of the carnival," says Jerry ”Wherever I go, the circus is never far behind." A true carnival creator, all-around entertainer, and slightly deranged proprietor of Fish Town.
We love the madness and drama of Fish Town: Get yourself down to our crazy anything-can-happen late night shows ~ Which this year will happen after midnight at 1:30am on Friday Night and experience The ultimate Jerry Fish Party!
Jerry Fish blasted onto the Music Scene in the 1990's touring the globe as front-man of alternative rock outfit An Emotional Fish, the band who gave us the indie rock anthem “Celebrate”  ~ These days the name Jerry Fish is synonymous with Festivals, Carnival Sideshow, Circus, Cabaret and Theatre.  

A highly charismatic performer who refuses to countenance audiences having anything but a good time, accentuating the positive and bringing smiles to troubled faces with his swaggering vocal, generous and infectious smile and that fantastic vaudeville moustache. 

Let your inner child run away with the Circus at The Jerry Fish Electric Sideshow.
activity_name_1752311769931832856: R.S.A.G. & Kilo presents Decks N Drums
activity_description_1752311769931832856:
R.S.A.G. (Jeremy Hickey) and Kilo (John Kealy) have been friends and collaborators for over 30 years. Their partnership began during the recording of R.S.A.G.’s Choice Music Prize-nominated debut album, Organic Sampler, and has since evolved into the explosive Decks & Drums live experience.
From late-night parties and intimate venues to some of Ireland’s biggest festival stages, the duo have built a reputation for high-energy, genre-defying performances that keep crowds moving. Expect pounding rhythms, infectious beats, and a set that refuses to be boxed into one style.
Get ready for an unforgettable performance when R.S.A.G. & Kilo bring their unique festival energy to Fish Town at EP26.
activity_description_1752311779050249752: ‘Growing up in a coastal town, the presence of the sea is ever felt and for Cobh-born singer-songwriter Rua Rí, aka Seán Damery, it is no different. It is rare that the sea does not bleed into the soft and serene folk music he has become known for, his work echoing tradition while forging a path that feels wholly his own.
activity_description_1752311792992116248:
Dear Willow formed in December 2024 is a fresh new Irish trad and folk style band with over 14million views on TikTok and 72 thousand followers across their social media platforms within their first year together.
Dear Willow consists of lead singer Katie Phelan, guitarist Dave McCabe, banjo player Eoin Brosnahan, fiddle player Aoife Nolan and drummer lan Bailey.
Dear Willow has a distinct sound which has become extremely popular landing them opportunities like trad fest, electric picnic, the ruby sessions and support slots for the high kings on their
'Rocky road to Dublin' tour.
They have recently sold out Whelans for their first headline show. 
They are releasing new music very soon.
They have catchy original music along with heartfelt relatable originals which cater to people of all generations.
Dear Willows goal is to create traditional style Irish folk music with a twist and bring it to new audiences and people of all ages.
activity_description_1752311802840342040:
Dublin-born singer-songwriter Lucy McWilliams blends indie, R&B, acoustic pop, and ‘90s rock to tell honest stories of love, loneliness, and mental health. With over 16 million Spotify streams, her sweet, expressive vocals and emotional openness define her sound.

In 2024, released her debut EP Third Second Chance with Zach Dawes adding a sharper edge to her music.

Having supported Arlo Parks and Two Door Cinema Club, and performed across Ireland, London, and Paris, McWilliams continues to evolve—always grounded in heartfelt songwriting.
activity_description_1752311811170229784:
Grown from the boggy outcrop of the Muskerry Gaeltacht, Leevy are finding beauty and madness in the harshest corners of the Irish psyche.
Through relentless gigging and word of mouth, they have built a reputation for live shows where laughter, introspection, dancing and crying all go hand in hand.
From Gothic revenge tales and sacrificial burnings at wakes, to forlorn songs of loss and the death of the natural world, Leevy’s songs dance around the threshold of this world and the next.
With a sound that can roar with pounding drums, banjos, whistles, and heavy guitars or can just as easily sway with beautiful folk arrangements and harmonies that tie their raucous performance to tradition and culture.
activity_description_1752311827427352088: Despite decades at the forefront of club culture, Billy Scurry has retained the authenticity and passion that made him a standout figure from the beginning: a selector driven purely by music, energy and connection with the crowd.
activity_description_1752311840337419800:
Bursting through the heart of Cork City, BABYRAT is cutting through the noise with razor-sharp riffs, anthemic choruses and the kind of edge that power-pop has been missing. 
Their self-proclaimed ‘bitch-pop’ sound has sonically landed the bright-eyed five somewhere between The Strokes and Olivia Rodrigo, a sound which they have taken from battle of the bands in local bars to arena support slots in just one year. 

“BABYRAT are something special, embodying everything great about live music. There’s little doubt they’re destined for bigger things — so catch them while you can. An amazing band, an amazing gig.” - Gig Noise
activity_description_1752311853046160920:
Rowetta is the original female singer with t Madchester band, Happy Mondays, singing on all their hits & until last performed with them all over the world.

She is the voice on the renowned 1989 track "Reach Out/ BE", which has been sampled by many, Slam - (Eterna), Black Eyed Peas (Boom Boom Pow), Steve Angello, DJ Zinc, Todd Terry & many more.

She played herself in the Michael Winterbottom film 24 Hour Party People 
Rowetta also sings with Peter Hook (Joy Division / New Order)
Rowetta performed with Hacienda Classical at Glastonbury’s Pyramid Stage
Special guest appearances with Blossoms, Gorillaz & James.
2024 - Rowetta toured with Shed Seven on their Sold Out 30 year anniversary tour. celebrating 2 Number 1 albums in 1 year.
Currently recording & touring with a future legend, Tom A. Smith.
activity_description_1752311860965006872:
The Donnys are an exciting and vibrant rock and roll experience born and bred in Kilkenny.
Described by Hot Press magazine as “raucous rhythm ‘n’ booze” their infections brand of music is both steeped in 70s blues rock while dabbling in more modern punk and noise rock influences.
activity_description_1752311862038748696: Sideshow disco welcomes you to the world of swinging grooves and the  bigbeat sound !
activity_description_1752311869353614872: From his early days Billy developed a deep connection to soul, funk, hip hop and disco before becoming immersed in the exploding house and techno movement. His early residencies at influential clubs such as Sides and later the iconic Temple of Sound established him as one of the country’s premier selectors. Alongside fellow DJ and promoter Johnny Moy, he helped transform Temple of Sound into one of Ireland’s defining clubbing institutions during the 1990s rave era.
activity_description_1752311887498173976: Billy Scurry is one of the most respected and influential figures in Irish dance music culture. Emerging from Dublin’s underground scene in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Scurry became synonymous with the rise of authentic house and techno music in Ireland, helping shape a generation of club culture through his legendary residencies, eclectic musical taste and uncompromising approach behind the decks.
activity_description_1752311904401219096:
Kelly-Anne Byrne is regarded as one of the finest selectors on Irish airwaves, and, with a
career spanning two decades, one of Ireland’s most revered DJs. It all began in 2000 when
a large vinyl collection and a love of soul and disco prompted her to drop a mixtape into The
Dice Bar. Over twenty years later, she is still headlining many of Ireland’s top festivals,
including Electric Picnic, Longitude, Body & Soul, Sea Sessions, Night & Day and All
Together Now. She has supported Chic, Dave Lee, Dimitri from Paris, Black Pumas, Peter
Hook, Annie Mac and Mark Ronson. In February 2013 she began presenting The Saturday
Weekender on Phantom 105.2 which earned her a nomination for Best Newcomer at the PPI
Radio Awards. She later presented The Evening Show on TXFM for two years and The Beat
Goes On on Today FM for six years (named ‘The Best Show on Irish Radio’ by Jim Carroll in
The Ticket). In 2021 she took The Beat Goes 0n to The Face Radio in Brooklyn, NY, where it
was broadcast worldwide.
activity_description_1752311915096694296: Olivia is a ghost is a post-punk and shoegaze band originally formed in Madrid, Spain, in 2019 by María and Marcos. Blending atmospheric guitars, haunting melodies, and emotionally charged lyrics, the band quickly gained attention with their debut EP People Talking at the Movies, touring across Spain, Portugal, Italy, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Their music explores themes including mental health, feminism, antifascism, climate change, and personal loss, creating a sound that is both introspective and politically conscious. Following the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic and industry challenges, the band disbanded in 2021 after releasing their debut album Bees Are Dying. In 2024, María relocated to Ireland and reformed Olivia is a ghost, joined by drummer Rory Lahart and guitarist Riccardo Militerno, with co-founder Marcos later returning on bass and vocals. The reunited four-piece is finally taking Bees Are Dying on the road, bringing their immersive blend of shoegaze and post-punk to audiences across Europe.
activity_description_1752311935069969944: Crayfish is an Indie band based in Dublin. Formed by Barry McNamara in 2025 and featuring the musical talents of Jules Farrell, Tosh Molloy, Marcus Dalton, Claudia Verdecchia and Rory Lahart. Throughout 2025 the band released a new single for every month of the year and received widespread national and international airplay. The beginning of the year saw Crayfish perform at Hi How Are You Day in the Grand Social with Jerry Fish, May Kay, Sexy Tadhg and Child of Prague.Summer 2026 is set for some new releases and more live shows so stay tuned!
activity_description_1752311944431656472:
Calum Agnew is one of Ireland’s most exciting emerging soul-pop artists and was recently named an Irish Times Ones to Watch for 2026. He released his hotly anticipated debut EP Bad Boy in February 2026 alongside a sold-out headline show at The Grand Social and packed slots at all the major festivals.
Agnew has supported acclaimed artists including Tolu Makay, Shobsy, Róisín Ó, SexyTadhg, Sam Wills, Curtis Harding and Jessica Doolan (London and Dublin). He was also selected as one of the faces of Culture Night 2025, appearing live on Virgin Media’s Six O’Clock Show.
Agnew is carving out a chic, soul-infused space in Ireland’s music scene. With a seductive vocal tone and a gift for weaving irresistibly catchy pop melodies through soulful, jazz-leaning arrangements, his sound draws comparisons to Amy Winehouse, Joy Crookes, Olivia Dean and RAYE, while remaining unmistakably his own.
Agnew brings a mischievous, mod-meets-modern energy that has quickly made him one of the most compelling new voices in Irish music.
activity_description_1752311959019445784:
Led by Regina George and co-host Dylatrix, with special guests Alexis McQueen, Anita Hero, Ellis Dee Grainne Knees, Jaded, Lucina Shining & Sasha Fierce this fabulous collective of drag sisters and siblings delivers a one-of-a-kind show packed with dazzling lip-syncs, dirty dance, and unforgettable moments under the big top tent. 
Regina and the Queens is a celebration of drag, community, and pure entertainment. Expect glamour, laughter, big personalities, and a whole lot of heart as the queens invite everyone to join the party. 
Whether you're singing along, dancing in the crowd, or getting pulled into the action, one thing is guaranteed: you'll leave smiling.
activity_description_1752311966451752472:
After a whirlwind few months including performances in LA and across Europe,
signing an international publishing deal, signing to influential UK Independent
label SO Recordings, Shobsy released his debut EP ‘Own The Night’ last Autumn.
Dance Or Cry’ (the first release from the ‘Own The Night’ EP) reached Number 4 on
the Influential Irish Radio Breakers Chart and achieved significant airplay on
Ireland’s most listened to station RTE Radio 1 and was ‘Track of the Week’ on RTE
2fm as well as being playlisted on stations such as Sydney Radio in Australia, Radio
Excalibur In Greece,  KOWS 92.5 (Santa Rosa, CA) and WXDR-LP 98.9 FM (New
Orleans, LA),

Shobsy recently completed a 14 date UK & European tour with SO Recordings
labelmates and he recently returned from LA where he was the Special Guest
performer at The International Music Industry Person of the Year Award
presentation to Kirk M. Sommer (WME Global Head of Music)

Shobsy’s current single ‘Silver Line Livin’ was ‘Track of the Week ‘on the Louise
Cantillon show on Today FM.

Shobsy recently released ‘OH!’ Which was his most successful streaming release.
He completed a sold out Irish acoustic tour taking in stops in Dublin, Cork
(Coughlan’s) & Listowel (Mike the Pies) He also recently performed at Beyond the
Pale Festival and at the Greenfields Festival in County Laois and has announced an
Irish tour for Autumn / Winer 2026 which includes a headline show at Whelan’s,
Dublin on Sat Nov 14 th .

Hot Press - “It’s not being unduly hyperbolic to say that Shobsy could soon be sitting
at Pop’s top table with the likes of Harry Styles, Lewis Capaldi and Sam Smith”
'If there is a better male singer in the world than Shobsy I have not heard him. He
has more octaves to climb and descend than evolution usually
allows. Champagne and Entertainment sound like George Michael style hits in-
waiting' 
 (Danny McElhinney - Irish Daily Mail on Sunday)
activity_description_1752311988723506712: Following a triumphant electric picnic debut last year, DELUSH return for what promises to be an electrifying set at the legendary Fish Town stage. Tallaght's finest have been building a hugely dedicated following recently. If you know you know. Miss it at your peril.
activity_description_1752312001709071896:
Dose brings together the formidable talents of Lizzie Fitzpatrick (Bitch Falcon), bassist Lauren Heron (Merpire), synth player Aoife Spratt, and drummer Nicki Meehan. Their sound is a bold fusion of dream pop, post-punk, grunge, shoegaze and synth-pop, drawing inspiration from DIIV, Cocteau Twins, Beach House and Slowdive, while also channeling the surreal atmosphere of David Lynch’s films.


The band’s debut single, “Cuckoo”, arrived in 2024 to widespread acclaim, earning 2FM The Alternative’s Track of the Week. The Goo described it as “a fuzzy pitch shifting cross between shoegaze, coldwave with some post punk thrown in. Sung by The Roches and mixed by Eno,” and predicted big things for the band. Their debut EP, Sycophantic, produced by Joey Edwards (Pizza Pizza, Just Mustard, The Altered Hours), was released in May 2026, with The Goo declaring that “Dose can do no wrong.” Following appearances at Beyond the Pale and a support tour with US indie legends Throwing Muses, Radio X’s John Kennedy called Dose “iconic” and selected them as Track of the Week. With a growing catalogue of self-produced videos - including a striking homage to The Shining - and a live show that balances raw intensity, cinematic atmosphere and theatrical flair, Dose have quickly become one of Ireland’s most compelling new acts, leaving audiences captivated.
activity_description_1752312002799590936: The YEAR Grunge BROKE are live at The Jerry Fish Electric Sideshow at Fish Town / Electric Picnic 2026, bringing an electrifying celebration of Grunge and '90s Alternative Rock. Calling all fans of Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Alice In Chains, The Smashing Pumpkins, Stone Temple Pilots, Mudhoney, Tool, Rage Against The Machine, Screaming Trees, and more! This is the show for you. With nearly a million social media followers and sold-out performances throughout Europe, Ireland, and the UK, The YEAR Grunge BROKE is the ultimate grunge and '90s alternative rock experience on tour today.
activity_description_1753007940954370192:
When you watch Aaron Rowe on stage, he anchors himself behind the mic, broad shouldered and wide eyed whilst telling stories. Song histories, personal anecdotes or just random thoughts and funny observations are blurted out with erratic but effortless charm. His smile is so sunny and wide it feels permanent and his laugh is hoarse, warm and totally infectious. When he speaks his eyes glisten, but when he sings, they close as his head lulls onto his shoulder and tilts back. For Aaron, singing and playing guitar is not a choice, it’s an extension of himself - he has to do it. You can tell as soon as he begins it offers him not only freedom, but focus.

 

It wasn't always that easy, though. When he first started playing music as a teenager, Aaron tried to keep it a secret. “Where I'm from, you can’t show people you’re soft, so playing music and singing was just off the cards.” However, it got tricky once he started walking around the area with a guitar strapped to his back. One day he was finally pulled over by “a few of the lads, they asked me ‘you playing music then, Aaron? Play us a song;” And when he humbly refused? “Play us a fucking song”. Reluctantly, he sang to them, sitting on a brick wall behind those tightly closed eyes. When he opened them, instead of laughter he was met with acceptance. “All they said was, ‘That was class,’ It was a really nice moment for me, and after that exact day I was like fuck this, this is what I want to do, and this is what I’m going to do for the rest of my life”. He decided then and there that he was going to be a musician.

 

Aaron grew up in Monkstown Farm, Dun Laoghaire on the southside of Dublin with his three sisters and single mother. “It was rough. Do you know what I mean? But rough in the sense that it was tough seeing her go through it. We never went without a hot meal but she went without everything.” Because his mum wanted him and his sister to be educated in the irish language, he ended up going to a different school to the boys in his area. He quickly began “living a double life”, softening his accent and picking up middle class manners. “When I was in primary school I just wanted to fit in, but when I got to Secondary I found that my strength was that I wasn't like the kids around me, and so I played up to it a lot. Once, someone in school called me a scumbag and I said ‘grand, now i'm going to give you full scumbag!’”

 

So far, the story of Aaron Rowe looks like what fate feels like: paths crossing and stars aligning.

Almost exactly a year ago, Aaron was singing covers at his regular Saturday gig in The Dame Tavern when one of his future managers would walk in and discover him playing. A few weeks later, Lewis Capaldi would also stumble into Aaron’s usual Sunday sessions at Cassidy’s on a stag do. Like fate, a few weeks after that, he would bump into Lewis again whilst performing at an open mic in Nashville, where Lewis introduced him to his best friend, now Aaron’s  manager, who just so happened to have listened to his demos that very morning.

 

Far from an overnight success, after nearly thirteen years of gigging five days a week, his moment finally came. Call it fate, call it what you will, a good story is the least you can expect from a generational voice like Aaron. His own life experiences leading up to this moment means there is an unmatched maturity and vulnerability to Aaron’s songwriting, Somehow, he can balance the heart wrenching with the heartwarming, all the while holding open the door to us into his very personal world. This dichotomy he often explores on upcoming releases lies not only in its sometimes frank, sometimes devastating lyrics, but crucially in the old soul of Aaron’s voice, where he wears his influences on his sleeve; from Sam Cooke to Nina Simone to Paulo Nutini. 

 

What separates Aaron from his contemporaries is the everlasting quality to his songs - it's as though his voice trips and falls seamlessly through a melody, forever wounding its listener. You can see the mansion/ from the council estate,” sings Aaron in the opening line of his first single, ‘Hey Ma’. On the surface, it's a song written to his Mum about missing home and living vicariously through her whilst working over in England. However, through his colloquial and very intentional way of lyric writing, Aaron can encapsulate an entire world in a single line. ‘And down here no one's special,/ And they’d kill if you tried,/ But they’d help you in a heartbeat,/ And if they couldn't stop you bleeding,/ They’d die there by your side.’ The sharp inhalation of breath that cuts through the opening seconds of the song seems to warn us that what's about to follow is truly exceptional, because although grounded in a cold, casual reality, ‘Hey Ma’ feels transcendental. It’s what you’d call a forever song; a song that will stand the test of time, and Aaron doesn’t so much sing the words, as live them. As we climb the final moments of the song, hundreds of years shatter through the vocal, turning it to gravel, and Aaron throws away the melody in favour of mesmerising runs, so powerful and painful it is as if you can hear his heart breaking. 

 

A lot of the songs on the upcoming project are inspired by his home and the people Aaron grew up with. Talking With You, for instance, is about his uncle Mick: “Mick has no kids and adopted me, in a way. We used to drink cans of Guinness and watch the horses on TV.”  When Aaron had to start going over to England a lot, he felt guilty leaving Mick behind. “Shooting the bullshit/ watching the news/ picking a winner/ watching him lose… wish i was somewhere just talking with you.”  The Lane touches upon a similar subject, but holds even greater meaning for Aaron. “It's been a few years in the making, this song. When I used to go on the hop from school, I’d end up at my da’s place with his eccentric friend, Terry. One day he went ‘I have a song name for ya: Down Through The Lane’ and I was never sure what he meant by that. But then we started talking about my dad and his own dad, and the geography of where they lived and how we got to where we are today, and how you had to walk down this little lane off the main road to get to the gaff…” A few years passed and still no song, even Terry himself passed away, but Aaron always had that title in the back of his mind. It was only when he was up one night having a few drinks with his Dad, that the inspiration for the song finally came. “When my grandad was dying on his deathbed, my dad said he was holding his hand- imagine that, two hard men of that generation holding hands- and even when he was finally unconscious the only thing he wanted to say to his dad was I love you, and he couldn't. He just didn’t know how to say it. And he never got to say it.” However, Aaron is able to say it, and that’s the whole point. With the lyrical dexterity of Damien Dempsey and the visceral melodic nuance of Damien Rice, Aaron’s capacity for empathy within his songwriting is unparalleled, and he often becomes the perfect voice for that which cannot always be expressed.

 

Over a month before the release of his first single, ‘Hey Ma,’ people were already sharing their own versions online by piecing together the song through snippets that had surfaced on social media. Something within just a few seconds of that song had broken through and touched people. He's played in pubs with Ed Sheeran, who is a fan, and supported David Gray at the 3arena without a single song out. Earlier on in the year he was invited to sing ‘The Parting Glass’ with Dermot Kennedy in Boston in front of 20,000 people who hadn’t a clue who he was, and yet the entire place erupted after he sang one line. Saying this, it doesn't take long to realise it’s not just his voice that has captured the hearts of so many people so early on in his career - its Aaron. His ability to blend this kind of timeless songwriting - whether singing about Monkstown, his ma or his uncle Mick - is truly part of what will make Aaron Rowe a touchstone for his generation, and will ensure he’ll always be sat on that wall, eyes closed, straddling the line between Ireland’s culturally rich past and trailblazing present.
activity_description_1754430581208732384:
Mills is a DJ & Producer from Dublin. Who has made a name for himself as a passionate supporter of Irish-made productions.

Now a regular in venues all around Ireland, he has also secured international gigs in Ibiza, Magaluf, Santa Ponsa, and Liverpool, sharing the stage with renowned artists like Weiss, Ejeca (Trancewax), Shermanology, Biscits, Yasmine Gardezi, Morgan Seatree, Camrin Watsin, Evan McGee, Caz, and Jess Bays.

Mills this year looks to reach wider audiences with his rolling rave synth lead tracks this year at Electric Picnic
activity_description_1754430592206197472: King Kong Company (DJ Set) brings the festival energy they're famous for straight to the decks. Expect a genre-hopping journey through house, rave, breaks, bass and feel-good anthems, packed with big drops and infectious vibes. Whether you've seen their legendary live show or not, this DJ set is guaranteed to keep the dancefloor moving from the first beat to the last.
activity_description_1754430606315836128:
Together as One is a 6-piece reggae band from Dublin, Ireland. 

We came together in early 2025 — six musicians from different corners of the Dublin scene who have been friends for 25+ years off the back of playing in multiple successful bands together. What started as after-hours sessions turned into a band with a clear purpose: make music that unites people

Our sound is classic roots reggae with a Dublin heartbeat: one-drop rhythms, heavy bass, conscious lyrics, and live energy every time. From Northside Street busks to late nights in Fibbers, we mix lovers rock, dub, and ska, with a touch of Irish soul in the craic agus ceoil.
activity_description_1754430619318178528:
danzi is an Irish-based alternative R&B artist blending elements of Hip-Hop, Rock, and electronic music to create emotionally driven, introspective songs. Through atmospheric production and honest songwriting, he explores themes of identity, relationships, ambition, and self-reflection, developing a sound that is both personal and genre-fluid.

His single “BLEAK” is his most streamed release to date, while fan favourites such as “iknow” continue to resonate with listeners. Previous releases including “SUNRISE,” “SLUMDOGBOY,” and “danceforme” have helped establish his growing catalogue, while his most recent feature, “NO LGHT / NO LOVE,” appears on Fortune Igiebor’s latest mixtape, “VSTW.”

As a live performer, danzi. has built a reputation for engaging and energetic sets, selling out headline shows at both The Cobblestone and Whelan’s. He has also supported Bawo at The Academy and performed at festivals including Ones To Watch, Summerwatch, and Beyond The Pale.

With a growing audience and a strong live presence, danzi. continues to establish himself as one of Ireland’s emerging alternative artists.
activity_description_1754430637345297120: Your granny’s secret sauce, Avenue 68, has quickly become a standout act in Ireland’s music scene. Through silky vocals and intricate guitar lines, this infectiously groovy 5-piece crafts a soundscape full of soul and energy.
activity_description_1754430654021849824:
Sugabooo the “WhatsApp rapper” released his debut mix tape Kimmagination in August 2025. The collaboration with Luke Nelson organically reached 21K monthly listeners. His track Goin Ballistic reached the Viral top 10 in Ireland and Lewis Capldi’s Spotify wrapped. The moniker was coined in 2022 when his initial underground material was virally circulated in Dublin via WhatsApp. He is known for his hyper energetic flow and his sharp Dublin wit.

Sugabooo's debut headliner in Whelans was completely sold out. 2026 saw his American debut at SXSW, The Great Escape in the UK, Trinity Ball, Paris and The Workman’s Club with talk of the town Reggie.

Sugabooo's first public release was early in 2025, a Feat on Lil Skags Pilgrimmage to Kimmage. It received track of the week on the Nialler9 blog. They released a mixtape together this spring; SKAGABOO and drew a crowd of 2000 at Forbidden Fruit on the undergrowth stage.
activity_name_1754430664247562976: P H Λ L L O U T
activity_description_1754430664247562976: P H Λ L L O U T bring hip-hop’s most iconic tracks to life — live and instrumental. No words, all soul. Old-school and modern classics are mixed and blended seamlessly, DJ-style, keeping the groove locked from first note to last. High-fidelity, authentic, and atmospheric — a set that hits different. Catch them live at Electric Picnic.
activity_description_1754430677342180064:
A fixture of Dublin’s underground rap scene while also being one of its most exciting emerging voices, Jeorge II has spent years honing a sound shaped by the city that raised him. His music captures the grit, humour and everyday realities of Dublin life mirroring classic Irish literature in how he uses wit and wordplay to communicate struggle and hardship.

Equally at home over hard beats and more melodic productions, Jeorge II blends personal storytelling with undeniable energy, creating works that resonate far beyond the capital. His ability to tell full stories within the limitations of a verse chorus structure has earned him a loyal following and the respect of Ireland’s hip hop community.

Now, with momentum continuing to build, Jeorge II is stepping onto bigger stages without losing the raw honesty that made his name.
activity_description_1754430697525170912: The Dirty Circus is a high-energy burlesque and cabaret experience featuring an electrifying mix of Burlesque, Drag, Circus, Divas, and Pole performances. Expect dazzling costumes, jaw-dropping talent, bold personalities, and unforgettable entertainment as world-class artists take the stage with glamour, comedy, and plenty of attitude. Sexy, spectacular, and delightfully outrageous, The Dirty Circus delivers a thrilling night of variety entertainment that celebrates confidence,diversity,  creativity, and pure show-stopping fun
activity_description_1754430717699773152:
EMORAH Collective is a collaborative dance project exploring the space between ritual, tribal fusion, contemporary performance and visual storytelling. Founded by two long-time collaborators and friends, the collective draws on improvisation, theatrical performance and alternative arts culture to create immersive, otherworldly experiences through movement, striking costuming and atmospheric soundscapes.

Inspired by transformation, connection and the stories that shape us, EMORAH Collective invites audiences into a darkly beautiful landscape where movement becomes language and symbolism takes physical form.

Blending choreography and improvisation, the duo creates performances that feel both intimate and expansive, ancient and strangely futuristic. Whether appearing at festivals, live music events, alternative arts spaces or immersive productions, EMORAH explores the places where personal experience meets collective imagination, inviting audiences into worlds that are at once familiar and unknown.
activity_description_1754430730450457312: Nuclearmaso is usually found behind the sound desk at gigs but will be gracing the Glow Depot stage. Having started DJing at 6 years old on a set of Denon decks Nuclearmaso is ready to bring the best vibes and the grooviest tunes.
activity_description_1754430740013470432:
vasuki red blends breaks, bass and speaker-rattling kicks to create bassline poetry. Genre-fluid and never sticking to one sound, she crafts a unique and immersive experience that lasts way after the set is over. The low-frequency explorer has carefully curated a journey filled with energy, unpredictable rhythms and passion. Known to shake dance floors everywhere she plays.

vasuki red mixes between genres like UK Bass, Electro, Breakbeat and Techno to fill the space with heavy dubs and trickling hi-hats, designed for movement.
What started in Galway has grown far beyond home. She has lit up stages internationally with her signature sound, building her reputation for an unapologetic flow and relentless energy.

Beyond the bass, vasuki red is passionate about tearing down traditional gatekeeping, prioritizing inclusive and safe spaces for the community behind the sound.
activity_description_1754430755263959776:
RNL are a DJ Collective of 3, bringing big nights of 90's Old School Dance Classics and Ibiza Anthems 
to the Dublin dance scene . Made up of Robbie Dixon , Niall Regan & Liam Kieran, the lads plan to bring 
big house vocal and dance/trance favourites with them on the night for their Electric Picnic debut. 

Check our their Instagram for more info @rnlclubnights 
and search RNLclubnights on Soundcloud.
activity_description_1754430765447729888: Ev Wilde is a producer, remixer and DJ hailing from Dublin, Ireland.
activity_description_1754430779951633120:
Floating Live burlesque show with Dirty Circus. Rooted in culture and driven by a deep love for music, Betzy Nina’s style blends the heat of world house music and unexpected sounds as a reflection of her multicultural influences and sharp musical instinct. 

A Caribbean artist based in Dublin bringing sun-soaked vibes to cold nights, delivering sets that are as dynamic as they are unforgettable.
activity_description_1754430794153546464:
Smokey is a Swiss army knife in Irish music - a rapper, DJ, producer, and event curator. Hailing from Ballybrack, Dublin, he first made waves as part of the hip-hop collective The Rog Poets before stepping away from performing to organize events with Lord Apex, manage rising talent Curtisy, and collaborate with Hens Teeth. Now he's back - bigger, bolder, and wiser.

Over the past year, Smokey has worked with acclaimed producers like StrangeLove (Negro Impacto) and Isaac Jones, supported UK rapper Lord Apex, and solidified his role in Rory Sweeney's supergroup "Irish Hash Mafia."

Combining precise wordplay with production that challenges expectations, he is rapidly emerging as one of the most versatile voices in Irish contemporary hip-hop, continuing to push the boundaries of Irish rap.
activity_description_1754430807751480032: Fresh off a new mixtape and sold out Academy 2 headline, Fortune Igiebor joins the bill along some of the biggest artists in the world at Electric Picnic. Igiebor has spent recent years building momentum. Named Artist of the Year by Black & Irish in 2023, he has delivered sold-out headline shows in Dublin and London, performed at Forbidden Fruit, appeared at Breaking Sounds in Paris, and been selected for RTÉ 2FM Rising 2025. Two number one releases and a self-directed documentary premiere have marked a career built fully on his own terms. His live shows, whether intimate listening rooms or packed-out venues, have become a key part of that rise. Visually, Igiebor treats every release as a full world of its own, with artwork, fashion, music videos and production all tied together.
activity_description_1754430817817809632: Lil Skag, from Enniscorthy County Wexford, has quickly carved a niche for himself on the Irish rap scene. Taking influence from contemporary trap and drill, Skag infuses his music with bold irreverence, provocative cultural references, and a sense of storytelling and wit that feels uniquely and authentically Irish (or rather, Wexfordish). Skag first made a name for himself with his debut single Cunning Linguist in April 2023. Since moving to London in September, he’s played all across the city but has still found the time to return home to perform a sold out headline show at Whelans alongside regional shows in Galway, Cork, Limerick and Wexford. On stage, his performances match the personality and confidence you hear in his music. Skag knows his audience; knowing when to keep the energy high, when to crack a joke, when to tell a story, and when to show his genuine appreciation for the people who’ve turned out to see him. Most importantly, he knows how to hit every bar as hard as he hits it on the record.
activity_description_1754430827758310112: Catacombs is Ireland's premier Underground Rap event series. Platforming both established and emerging artists within the Irish Underground Rap scene, Catacombs delivers high energy shows to sold out crowds with artists set to become future stars in their own right. Curated by Omen and Kate, Catacombs shows provide a variety of subgenres reflected in the line-ups. Catacombs shows are Hosted and DJ'd by Omen, who has managed Catacombs from its inception, and built it into the internationally recognised series and platform that it is today.
activity_description_1754430840928424672: Omen is a producer, DJ and visual artist from Wicklow, Ireland, known for his work with Ireland's premier underground rap event series Catacombs. Omen manages, curates, DJs and hosts Catacombs, while also DJing and producing music in the genres of Witchhouse and Electro-clash. A DJ set from Omen will range from the distorted 808s of underground rap hits to the screaming saw waves of Witchhouse and Electro-clash bangers. With over ten years of DJing experience, Omen cut his own path in Dublin's music landscape and set the standard for grassroots events in his scene.
activity_description_1754430853796549344:
Manwelli is a queer DJ born in Italy, seasoned in London, and now based in Dublin.
 
His multi-influenced sets fuse electro, Italo, disco, synth-pop, HI-NRG, house, and techno-pop into a euphoric, joyful sound, rooted in a love for the dancefloor and the freedom found there.
 
He has brought his energy to Electric Picnic, All Together Now, and Audio Garden festivals, as well as some of Dublin, Cork, and Bray's favourite venues and queer events in Ireland.
He has also made exciting international appearances in London, Berlin, Barcelona, and Bangkok.
 
He is also active in organising events, particularly fundraising parties for the queer community.
activity_description_1754430872779969248: The Mo Cultivation set is a takeover of multiple DJs, MC and dancers
activity_description_1754430884247196384:
Between Berlin and Dublin, JenTen is carving out her space within Europe’s shifting techno landscape. Rooted in her Nigerian heritage, she crafts a sonic identity defined by hypnotic repetition, intricate percussion, and minimalist tension.
Her long, seamless blends and atmospheric restraint create journeys built for late-night rooms. With a style that connects her cultural roots to Berlin’s electronic underground, JenTen brings a distinct voice shaping the scene’s next wave.
activity_description_1754430903037678304: Jess Maciel is a Dublin-based DJ and radio presenter with a passion for live sets. Known for her fun, feel-good mixes and love of house and dance music, she brings high energy to every gig.
activity_description_1754430924420240096:
The ethereal and magnetic Saibhin, is a Mexican-Irish singer who's creating a stir in the Irish music scene. Saibhin's charisma is described as infectious as she effortlessly flows from one emotionally evoking melody to a symphony full of life, bouncing off of her band - a five piece of Ireland's most talented upcoming musicians and instrumentalists.

Saibhin's genre bending music ranges anywhere from vocally soothing Sean- nós ballads "as Gaeilge" to soul inspired anthems and everything in between, creating a multicultural fusion of music and language.

The intent to create a safe space where people feel compelled to explore their own emotions, definitely translates. It's not uncommon to see a tear shed with Saibhin's personal life highs and lows being conveyed in the music and performance.
activity_description_1754430949166633696:
Salamay is a Nigerian born, Cork raised artist challenging genre conventions of today with his unique brand of contemporary Hip Hop. His music is best described as a fusion of rhythm, and poetry shaped by the sounds of Hip Hop, Soul, R&B, Afrobeat, and more.
 
Since his debut in 2021, Salamay has received critical acclaim earning a No. 2 position on District Magazine’s ‘Top Ten Tracks” for “Take it Easy”, while receiving placements on various playlists including Spotify’s immensely popular Fresh Finds Hip Hop. His innate ability to captivate and connect with audiences has also landed him on some of the world’s largest stages from Electric Picnic to Other Voices Cardigan in Wales, and most recently Beyond the Pale.  
 
Set to release his next project in 2026, Salamay is intent on showcasing the rich and varied Hip-Hop talent Ireland has to offer with the world.
activity_description_1754430968527540960:
Outstraight Records is both a record label and artist collective from Dublin, Ireland. Predominantly operating in the hip-hop space, the label comprises various MCs (Don Kobz, Beano, Panda Drey, Conkan & Lú Ke) & Producers / DJs (No Venom & 404NOTFOUND) alongside our Label Director (Aaron
Connery), Creative Director (Dylan Jackson) and our Founder (Lewis Kenny).



The group, established in 2015, have built a formidable offering via their live show productions and consistent musical releases. 2025 was one of the most successful years to date, seeing sold out shows at the Sugar Club alongside their most significant album release with “Dual Odyssey” - a 12

track, collaborative album with Verb T (The Four Owls / High Focus Records). From the success of Dual Odyssey, Outstraight undertook a number of UK dates which included Bristol, Bournemouth & culminated with a headline London show at the Camden Assembly in June 2025.
activity_description_1754430978635813600:
Once you’ve caught a glimpse, it’s hard not to become captivated by the weird and wonderful world of Mount Pyrus. 


What started as a retro-pop, indie-jazz inspired dream project has morphed beyond just music. Their unique combination of genres, visuals and samples creates a universe that explores psychedelia, nature and space, inviting listeners to travel through it all.


The band’s sound is brought to life by retro synth lines, soft vocals, groovy bass and driving drums. Immersive samples, soundscapes and visuals create an experience for the audience and piece together a unique and playful live show.


For fans of Crumb, Men I trust and Mild High Club
activity_description_1754430996704875232:
Boss Events & Friends is a collaborative showcase/performance with the B.I.M. (Believe In Me) music
collective. The Boss Events team will share the stage with some of the best emerging artists that the
country has to offer. The collective currently consists of 4 artists. Abbey Blu (Singer-Songwriter), Angel
Rose (Rapper-Songwriter), Shiloh Grey (Rapper-Songwriter) and the founder/leader of the collective
Mister K.Y.B (Rapper-Producer).
activity_description_1754431012165079776: Abbey Blu is a fresh new voice within singer-songwriter circles. As a newcomer to the scene, she released her debut single “Heal”. Abbey Blu proves she isn’t afraid to be vulnerable. “Heal” marks the beginning of what promises to be an inspiring journey from an artist determined to turn personal truth into universal connection. (FFO: Adele, Jorja Smith, Arianna Grande, Soulé, Amy Winehouse)
activity_description_1754431019865821920: Angel Rose is South African born, raised in Ireland, a hidden gem and a true lyricist in the making, a diamond in the rough. As a rapper, she delivers raw, gritty energy, but shows her versatility when she switches into her smooth, melodic side. Inspired by artists like Zulu Mecca, Scarlip, Shaybo, and Little Simz, her influence comes through in her sharp pen, confident delivery, and authentic artistry. She’s a force to be reckoned with, and she’s only getting started. (FFO: Cardi B, Little Sims, Mohdee, BBY MUTHA)
activity_description_1754431029252674272: Shiloh Grey is a versatile rapper emerging from the underground with a sound that moves effortlessly across genres. Whether he’s rapping like the rent is due or tapping into a more melodic lane, he brings intensity and range to every track. With several shows and headline sets under his belt, he’s steadily building a name for himself. Influenced by artists like Juice WRLD, XXXTENTACION, Fortune Igiebor, BBY MUTHA, and Yung Lean. Shiloh blends alternative roots with a style that can feel global while staying true to who he is.
activity_description_1754431036550763232: Mister KYB (Kay-Why-Bee) is a Zimbabwean-born, Dublin-based rapper and producer steadily making his mark. With over 700,000 streams and 3,000+ Shazams, his music is gaining real traction both locally and internationally. A former Hot Press ‘Big Break’ finalist, he’s gone on to perform across Ireland, at festivals such as Longitude, Indiependence, Electric Picnic and sharing stages with artists like Ne-Yo, Lloyd Banks, Major League DJs, General Levy, Lotto Boyzz, Machine Gun Kelly, and Tory Lanez. His work has also been supported on major radio platforms including RTÉ Pulse, 2FM, BBC 1Xtra, and Spin 1038. Known for his energetic, soulful performances, Mister KYB continues to grow as both an artist and collaborator, quietly building a strong and lasting presence in the scene. (FFO: Kendrick Lamar, Tommy Saint, Jafaris, J. Cole, AJ Tracey, Skepta, Odd Future)
activity_description_1754431045769843424:
Sloucho  is an anonymous producer, live act, and visual artist from Ireland. Known for immersive live shows, genre-melting electronic music, and world-building, the project connects Ireland’s tradition of myth-making with global electronic music culture.

Sloucho’s work exists within a fictional universe anchored by OUCH™: a corporate entity obsessed with the commodification of culture and the replacement of human creativity. The world of OUCH™ reflects our fragmented, data-driven world and the ongoing blurring of lines between the digital and physical realms.
activity_description_1754431057253847776: Asylum is a Dublin-born house music brand founded in 2024. Inspired by the city's underground scene and a long-standing love of vocal house, its sound sits somewhere between timeless records and what's coming next.
activity_description_1754431068838515424: New Era, performed by Ben Williams. Expect huge drops, non-stop energy and a set that turns the whole crowd into one massive moment. Unmissable.
activity_description_1755032184760505592: The boys are back in town! Super Average DJs return with 'Courtside' Caravan Mambo at GlowDepot. The DJ trio - Dolfin, Johnny M, and Dilicious - have teamed up once again to share their signature high-octane energy. Combining a love for a great party atmosphere with infectious dance grooves, their mission remains beautifully simple: have fun and make people dance. Following great events in 2022 and 2023, the lads are making their anticipated return to Electric Picnic this year. They have built a dedicated following on the music festival circuit, earning a reputation for creating a fun, welcoming party atmosphere wherever they play. With their blend of funky beats and individual styles, Super Average DJs are ready to bring the music back to Electric Picnic once again. Bring your energy and join the party!
activity_description_1755032196009628920:
Aneta Moran is a saxophone player based in Ireland, who mainly performs alongside house music
DJ's. Influenced by jazz improvisation and experienced in performing with different international
DJ's, she brings the spontaneity of live music to electronic music ranging from deep house dark
melodies to soulful laid-back sets, from upbeat dance music to experimental underground.
As solo saxophonist or in collaboration with other instrumentalists and singers, she connects with
the crowd and brings excitement and party vibe to every event.
activity_description_1755032210362537208:
Formed in 2017, SX2 is the musical project of brothers Scott & Clive Sullivan. Born from a
shared love of all things sonic, their sound draws from an eclectic range of influences,
blending club, psychedelic, rock n' roll, indie, afro and melodic sounds into something entirely
their own.
This unique palette caught the attention of Moscoman in 2021, who signed the duo to Disco
Halal. Since then they've been steadily building their portfolio, with tracks like "Leave Them
All Behind" and "Steady Up" earning support from industry giants like Keinemusik, John
Digweed, Moscoman, Acid Arab, Dave Seaman and Maxi Meraki, while also being featured
on Tomorrowland and Adidas.
That momentum carried them onto the festival circuit, with regular closing slots at Electric
Picnic and All Together Now, alongside a residency at Waterford's Electric Avenue.
For SX2, things are only just getting started. Expect to see the name on your radar and
lineups in the near future.
activity_description_1755032225109710072: Hailing from Waterford, Chartini is a vinyl selector whose sound moves effortlessly through rare funk, disco, world music and disco house. Her sets are soulful, high-energy and carefully curated—designed to connect crowds, lift moods and keep dancefloors moving from start to finish.
activity_description_1755032234697889016:
Ciara Daly, AKA Kiki D, is a 22-year-old DJ from Galway, Ireland, with a passion for House, Hardgroove, and Techno. Since starting her DJ journey two years ago, she has developed a sound built around driving grooves, energetic rhythms, and crowd-focused selections. Known for her fun personality and high-energy sets, Ciara brings a vibrant atmosphere to every dancefloor, creating unforgettable moments and keeping the energy levels high from start to finish.
With a deep love for underground electronic music and a constant drive to evolve her craft, Ciara continues to establish herself as an exciting rising talent within Ireland's growing dance music scene.
activity_description_1755032241819817208:
Mick Gill is an award-winning Irish club DJ and mashup artist known for packing dance floors with high-energy, multi-genre sets. Based in County Laois, he seamlessly blends current club bangers with nostalgic 90s and 00s dance anthems.
A former winner of "Kildare's Finest DJ," Mick has supported major international acts like Sigala, and irish legends like Al Gibbs and holds residencies across the Midlands in iconic venues like the Foundry in Carlow and the Naas Court Hotel. Expect fast-paced mixing, heavy basslines, and exclusive custom bootlegs designed to keep the festival crowd moving.
activity_description_1755032249939989752: Mookie is a young energetic DJ from County Laois, Ireland. Having started her music journey at age 12, she has quickly gained widespread recognition across the Irish festival scene. Known for her high-energy sets, she spins commercial house, dance, and pop, regularly performing at major events like the Greenfields and Blackthorn Festivals, Making her Electric Picnic Debut having just turned 15, She is one to watch for the future.
activity_description_1755032261021340920:
Fergal D’Arcy is one of Ireland’s most recognisable broadcasters and live event personalities, with a career spanning some of the country’s biggest radio stations including Today FM, RTÉ 2FM and iRadio. A six-time Hot Press National DJ of the Year, he has built a reputation as an electrifying performer, accomplished DJ and crowd-hyping MC who brings energy, charisma and quick wit to every stage he steps onto.

A veteran of Ireland’s festival circuit, Fergal has performed at some of the country’s most iconic events including Electric Picnic, Oxegen and Indiependence, while also taking to major stages such as Dublin’s 3Arena. Most recently, he entertained a crowd of over 20,000 people at Pints In A Field alongside The 2 Johnnies in St. Anne’s Park, Dublin.

Whether he’s behind the decks, hosting a live event or commanding a festival crowd, Fergal is known for his infectious energy, razor-sharp audience interaction and ability to read any room. From scratching to sampling, house to techno, indie anthems to chart-toppers, his versatility allows him to seamlessly mix across genres and create unforgettable moments on the dancefloor.

As one of Ireland’s most experienced event MCs, Fergal hosts and presents at events nationwide, bringing professionalism, spontaneity and an unmistakable stage presence that keeps audiences engaged from start to finish. Whatever the crowd, whatever the occasion, you’re in safe hands when Fergal D’Arcy takes control.
activity_description_1755032269082793208: Bren Curtis is an experienced Irish DJ with over 20 years behind the decks, specialising in house and commercial music. As a resident DJ at The Barracks, Carlow, Bren has built a reputation for delivering high-energy sets that keep dancefloors packed. Throughout his career, he has performed at venues and events including Foundry Carlow, Coppers Portlaoise, Naas Court Hotel, Encore Naas, Factory Waterford, Greenfield Festival, and many more. Combining experience, crowd awareness, and a passion for music, Bren creates unforgettable atmospheres for every audience.
activity_description_1755032277412680952: Thxtti is a Dublin based DJ with a Nigerian background whose sound is a fusion of black diaspora rhythms with electronic sounds. Her goal is to introduce you to songs and genres you’ve never heard before.
activity_description_1755032285658682616:
Nancy Wilde is the host of radio shows Time Capsule and Polar Disco Radio on Flirt FM. 
Following her Balearic and Balkan Summer tour across Southern and Eastern Europe, she’s solidly finding her own style and sound, identity and creative tapestry, curating sonic journeys that captivate and transport, with selections that always reflect the current mood (and even the mood swings in between).
Nancy has brought her distinctive sound to venues across Europe, such as Koncept in Zagreb, Lemonade in Budva, Kosovo Kolektiv Radio in Prizren, Agimi Underground in Tirana, and Chillin Bar in Skopje. She has also featured in the Éalú Le Grá x Reclaim the Mainframe takeover at Pawn Shop, and standout sets at KUKI and The Magic Room, leading to slots at Éalú Le Grá and Rewild.
Nancy is part of the Mná Mná Collective and Polar Disco.
activity_description_1755032293074212088:
Nia_Byrd is an Irish DJ with a love for house music, afro house, and anything that gets people moving. Her sets blend soulful vocals, uplifting melodies, deep percussion, and infectious grooves, creating the perfect soundtrack for a day in the field or a night on the dancefloor.

Drawing inspiration from house sounds across the globe, Nia_Byrd brings together feel-good favourites, fresh discoveries, and afro-inspired rhythms in sets that are packed with warmth and energy. Whether it's a sunny festival session, a packed tent, or a spontaneous dance with strangers who become friends, she knows how to keep the atmosphere buzzing.

Expect house music with soul, afro house with rhythm, and plenty of tracks that'll have you saying, "just one more song."
activity_description_1755032301018223864:
"Ireland dopest/Illest Urban Dj - Dj Ozz G is a resident Dj & host of Urban Saturday at Electric Nightclub Galway city.

Originally from Angola & living in Ireland since the early age of 16, Ozz G has been known for his uniquely party-rocking style with a smoooth touch of turntablism. 

Dj Ozz G has played for some of the biggest venues around the world, along side some of the biggest names in the music industry, ever since he embraced the entertainment world back in 2010.
activity_description_1755032307888493816: A Galway based DJ who’s maintained club residency before the pandemic up to date. Building off the experience of mixing hiphop, Rn’B, and afrobeats regularly in Four Four before lockdown, Bongani has developed a unique style blending different genres at Electric Galway where he’s showcased his talent almost every Friday night for the past two years. Not a stranger to electric picnic either as he’s been a support dj in trench town for the past 3 years where he’s mastered the art of performing live with other DJs and rappers. Expect to hear an international blend of music you can dance to when you attend any of his sets.
activity_name_1755792081001170928: SERENITY GARDENS STAGE OPENS with AOS Sí NA TINE
activity_description_1755792081001170928: Aos Sí na Tine opens the Serenity Gardens stage area with a celebration of fire, voice and Fae magic. Rooted in the mystery of Irish fairy folklore, this atmospheric performance brings together fire, movement, live vocals and the deep, continuous drone of the shruti box. As flames rise and voices gather, the space is awakened and the weekend begins. Part invocation, part spectacle, Aos Sí na Tine honours fire as a source of warmth, transformation, creativity and connection. Step closer, enter the circle and witness Serenity Gardens come alive through flame, sound and a little Otherworld magic.
activity_description_1755792088886462448: A vocalist and multi-instrumentalist originally from southern France and now based in Ireland, Pauline Garcia blends influences from highlife, reggae, Brazilian music, soul and acoustic folk into rhythm-driven live performances. Combining voice, guitar, bass and layered percussion textures, her music moves between intimate acoustic moments and groove-led soundscapes inspired by world music traditions.
activity_description_1755792104665434096: Ru O’Shea is a folk musician and songwriter whose work journeys through love, death, resistance, folklore and history, all delivered with passion and grá. He performs both solo and alongside members of his band, Ru O’Shea agus Cairde. Ru is the host of the Teach Ceoil folk music events and works professionally across arts and healthcare, community music and political activism. His collaborative practice has brought him together with Erebidae Circus, aerialist Polina Shapkina, Ensemble Balfolk Dublin and folk-rock band A Clatter and Drone. Rooted in storytelling and the living folk tradition, Ru’s performances carry songs of memory, struggle and connection, inviting audiences into music that feels both timeless and urgently alive.
activity_description_1755792125142026224: Emma Lohan is a song writer, performance artist and producer based in the west of Ireland.
