activity_description_1756618693217194944:
The Evergreen Brothers are a Galway folk band drawing from American roots, country, Irish traditional elements and blues. Formed in 2025, the band found its sound the natural way - playing pubs, sessions and venues, learning what carries in a room and cutting anything that doesn't. The music is just music: folk-led, harmony- driven, built on rhythm and feel. American influence sits in the bones, Irish in the 
grain, country and blues running like threads through the middle, just songs played honestly. 
In the last year The Evergreen Brothers have travelled and performed across 
Ireland and Germany, bringing energy, and always people-facing. Small rooms, street corners, wherever suits - that's where it belongs.
activity_description_1756618723323909056:
Maicín are an Irish five-piece folk rock band making what they like to call “Channel-Surf Rock”: A flickering eclectic blend of jangle pop, folk, new wave, and even boogie woogie.

 

Maicín began as a creative escape for songwriter Matt Hurley and drummer Aidan Kelleher, two young architects worn down by London life. What started as weekly jams to escape the mundanity of corporate life quickly became a fully fledged band. Well not quite “fully fledged”. Upon returning to Ireland, the band was completed by a mix of childhood friends and family: Darragh McNamara (bass), Méabh Fitzgerald (keys), and Ryan Daly (lead guitar).
activity_description_1756618736066204608: A musical collective built on rumours and word of mouth. We just create and hope you can relate.
activity_description_1756618753472566208:
Out on Bale are a young Irish trio bringing high-energy live performances that blend country, pop and trad. Formed in March 2024, the band have already played to crowds of over 6,000 and built a rapidly growing online following, with their videos reaching over 2.4 million views.

Combining guitars, keyboards, bodhrán, accordion, bouzouki and harmonica, Out on Bale deliver a lively mix of music, energy and plenty of craic — guaranteed to have the crowd up, dancing and hopping from start to finish. Known for their fantastic crowd interaction. 

After an exciting few years building their name across Ireland, Out on Bale are set to make their UK debut in 2027.
activity_description_1756618760669991872: Raz Olsher & Afla Sackey: a bond that fuels a dynamic and effortless musical relationship. Their music represents a harmonious union of African influences with electronic music, full of soul, vibrant energy and captivating rhythms.
activity_description_1756618782287434688:
The Dublin Ukulele Collective (DUC) is a thirty-five plus piece ukulele harmony band with a high feel-good-factor and watching them perform, the fun is obvious.

Members range in age up to 70+ and they perform a diverse repertoire of songs which reflects their age span.

Within are a seriously talented range of Dublin musicians including; experienced choir harmonisers, sexy middle-aged rockers and electric teenage funksters.

Expect upbeat, fun and rhythmic songs with loads of harmonies and a little nostalgia including songs from; Elbow, Cold Play, Radiohead, Talking Heads, Amy Winehouse, Erazure, Bob Dylan, Leonard Cohen, Jason Mraz and more. DUC is very much an audience join-in band.
activity_name_1756618793251345344: RELUCTANT BOB AND THE LONELY LOVERS
activity_description_1756618793251345344:
Reluctant Bob & the Lonely Lovers is the new project from Irish songwriter and producer Robert Baker. Backed by the Lonely Lovers, the band make dreamy-sounding indie pop, shaped by classic 1960s production and psychedelic pop. Radio X’s Jim Salveson described them as “The Flaming Lips meets The Beach Boys”, and there’s also echoes of Super Furry Animals, Grandaddy, Beach House, Spiritualized, Stereolab, Tame Impala and The Velvet Underground.
Their debut single, “Dreamager”, received radio support from RTÉ Radio 1, BBC Radio 6 Music, BBC Radio Ulster, WFUV in New York and Triple R in Australia, while producer Steve Lillywhite (U2, Talking Heads, Morrissey) selected it as his Track of the Week.
activity_name_1756618804013929408: JEAN PACK AND THE SLAY BABIES
activity_description_1756618804013929408:
Jean Pack is one of the year’s most idiosyncratic new voices - a songwriter whose work blends camp flair with raw feeling, structured chaos with cinematic charm. Her debut EP Allora, recorded at Big Child Studios in Cork with producer Caoilian Sherlock, introduced her as a bold, emotionally saturated presence: a cocktail of melancholia and mischief, poured neat.

Describing her sound as “a dirty aperitif with the first pint of the night,” she weaves lush harmonies, lo-fi textures, and sly lyricism into storytelling that is part cabaret, part confessional. Breakout single “Ruby” offered velvet bite and gem-cut polish, while “Birthday” traced a tragicomic friendship unravelling with dry wit.

Drawing influence from The Shangri-Las, Nancy & Lee, and The Velvet Underground, Jean Pack’s voice remains unmistakably her own - vulnerable, glamorous, and half-laughing through the ache.
activity_description_1756618822829577152:
From the foothills of Bray Head comes the irrefutable finest live band in the country. Their shows are
a sex driven, love laden, heartbreaking, tear jerking look into modern society. They have taken the
country, folk and bluegrass genre and moulded them into their own brand of boom grass. The
versatility of the band means that they can captivate a theatre crowd or send a wedding party into a
frenzy . Hold on tight to your mammas, your sisters and your brides to be, cause they are gonna be
led astray at a Luna Boys show.
activity_description_1756618834431022016:
DOGPOND, the dynamic ensemble known for their electrifying performances, are ready to captivate
audiences anew with their signature blend of short, snappy, and irresistibly catchy tunes.
Straight out of Dublin’s music melting pot, DOGPOND are a genre-defying force who’ve emerged
from the ashes of former rock and roll sensations The Hot Sprockets.
Their first single ‘KILNAMANAGH BLUES’ received a generous amount of National radio play, was
critically acclaimed by HotPress magazine and other print media, and was featured in a popular
Channel 4 TV Series.
This isn’t just a band; they’re a sonic journey, a musical kaleidoscope bringing the soul of Dublin to
life. Their fourth single ‘PAW IN DA POND’ is out now on all platforms.
activity_description_1756618845705311168:
David Geraghty is a member of SCGI (Screen Writers Guild of Ireland). He is also a five time Choice Music Prize-nominated multi-instrumentalist, composer, producer and writer of songs. 

He is a founding member of Bell X1 who have released nine studio albums to date.  Bell X1 are festival and arena headliners in their native Ireland playing to ever growing numbers on their regular North American and European tours.  He has released two solo albums under his own name with a third and fourth under the moniker Join Me in the Pines. 

2025 sees Geraghty return to the live scene under his own name, and with the promise of a new album, set for release in 2026.
activity_description_1756618852097430464: School-formed London four-piece the Jades bring a chaotic blend of Pulp’s poppy wit and the raw rock ‘n’ roll energy of Pixies and Ramones. Expect a riotous dance floor.
activity_description_1756618863086506944:
Baka Beyond are on the road again with their mix of African and Celtic music. promoting their new  album, Sing the World Awake. 
Inspired by the Baka Pygmies of Cameroon, founders Martin Cradick and Su Hart were deeply  moved by the Baka's music during their first visit to the Cameroon rainforest, prompting them to  share this experience with the world. Their album Spirit of the Forest catapulted them to global  fame, but they've stayed true to their roots. To ensure the Baka people benefit from their music,  they set up the charity "Global Music Exchange" and still visit the same Baka extended family  every year to ensure that they continue to benefit. 
From humble beginnings to a multicultural phenomenon, Baka Beyond's stage shows are a  testament to the power of music to unite us all. With band members hailing from across the globe,  each bringing their own unique flair.
activity_description_1756618876030129088:
We are FunkyTown, and we are here to make your clothes feel suddenly optional

We deliver pure unfiltered soul music driven by a guitar, bass and drum groove that locks you in while our trumpet and trombone duo blow enough heat to melt the stage. Up front, the vocals are pure velvet, delivering sexy soul singing that will make you look at your partner, or a random stranger, a little differently

We do not do subtle, and we do not do polite. We bring the sweat, the groove and bad decisions
activity_description_1756618883789591488:
Delush is a four-piece indie rock band hailing from Tallaght, Dublin. They burst onto the scene in September 2024, opening for Aslan at The Academy , Dublin. Since then they've taken to some of Irelands most iconic live music venues such as The Olympia, Electric Picnic, Whelan's, The Grand Social, The Workmans Club, Roisin Dubh, Sea Church Ballycotton, Works festival as well as gigs in Newcastle and London.

Formed by frontman Scott Leigh and guitarist Sean Corcoran, they duo began writing songs and performing together at 15. When drummer Keeghan and bassist Aaron joined, the band became a force with exciting live shows and a refined distinct sound.
activity_description_1756618890383037376: A group of men from Timahoe Co Laois in the Midlands of Ireland, who love singing.
activity_description_1756618901313393600:
The Pearly Whites bring a high-energy blend of powerful vocals, exceptional musicianship and a huge brass sound to stages across Ireland. Known for their infectious stage presence and crowd-pleasing performances, they have built a reputation for creating unforgettable experiences wherever they perform.

Drawing inspiration from across the decades, their setlist seamlessly blends artists such as Paolo Nutini, David Bowie, The Cranberries, Blur, Lionel Richie, AC/DC and Chappell Roan, alongside Irish favourites, dance classics and timeless party hits. The result is a show that appeals to all ages and keeps audiences singing and dancing from start to finish.

Having performed at major events and venues throughout Ireland, The Pearly Whites bring a feel-good energy and genuine connection with their audience that sets them apart. Expect huge choruses, soaring brass, plenty of crowd participation and a soundtrack packed with songs you know and love as they bring their unique show to Electric Picnic 2026.
activity_description_1756618909366457280: The Bootleg Beach Boys perform selections of classic hits, & cult  favourites, from California's most famous band. From surf themed  anthems such as "Surfin' Safari" & "Surfer Girl" to classic muscle  car memorabiles like "Shut Down" & "Fun Fun Fun", the band  have gathered an impressive repertoire of west coast, harmony  laden songs, that evoke the spirit and essence of the pursuit of the  1960's American dream.
activity_description_1756618917553738688:
McCartney: All the Best' is a live music tribute show that perfectly captures the essence of McCartney’s stellar years as a member of the groundbreaking and iconic band, The Beatles. But it doesn’t stop there; it goes beyond, exploring McCartney’s pioneering foray into Low-Fi, his million-selling band, Wings and the solo treasures.

Prepare to be enthralled as the stage comes alive with timeless hits like 'Hey Jude', 'Get Back', 'All My Loving', 'Can’t Buy Me Love', 'Lady Madonna', 'Band on the Run', 'Live and Let Die', 'My Love', 'Silly Love Songs', 'Pipes of Peace', 'No More Lonely Nights' and countless others, anthems that have earned Paul McCartney the status of the most successful recording artist of all time.
activity_description_1756618924138795968: Their sound being described as “endearing, daisy-fresh and effortlessly romantic”, Eppie is a four-piece band from Dublin that blends their love of 60s and 70s psychedelic rock with modern alternative and bedroom pop artists to create music that stands out amongst the sea of rock bands across the Dublin scene. Named after frontwoman Palomi’s younger sister, the band has seen early success, most recently having been listed among Hot Press Magazine’s “Hot for ‘26” artists. They have performed multiple successful shows across Ireland, and recently made their international debut in London. Fans can catch them live at Electric Picnic at the end of August, or at Ireland Music Week in October.
activity_description_1756618933877969856: Pop Gods are a nostalgic 80s and 90s band who have played over 1,000 shows, including Electric Picnic, the Google Summer Party (three years running), and many international gigs such as Bugatti Rimac in Zagreb and New Year’s Eve balls in Bahrain and Oman.From Whitney, Wham!, Spice Girls, Take That, and Westlife—Expect Trailer Park to bounce the way only Pop Gods can make it bounce.
activity_description_1756618944439227328:
Esmeralda Road are a Belfast band quickly establishing themselves as one of the most exciting new live acts to emerge from the UK and Ireland.
Built on sharp songwriting, restless rhythms and an instinct for turning small rooms into full-blown parties, the band first gained attention through a string of sold-out shows in Belfast and early releases that spread quickly online. On stage, their reputation grew just as quickly. Esmeralda Road began taking their high-energy live show across the UK and Ireland, sharing stages with artists including Liam Gallagher and Primal Scream, while building a devoted following through touring.
Off the back of a support tour with Irish indie risers Basht., with new music on the horizon, and big live plans for the rest of the year, 2026 is shaping up to be a landmark year for Esmeralda Road.
activity_description_1756618970041258944:
Hank & The Lads are a three-piece Irish band whose sound has been shaped in the pubs of Drogheda — soulful, honest performances and stories that connect straight with a crowd. Soulful vocals meet alt-folk and country, blended into a catchy, genre-crossing pop-acoustic sound that's all their own.
Their debut single "Animal" is already gaining serious traction — over 100,000 views on TikTok and airplay on 2FM — backed by a strong and growing social campaign, with a cohesive visual identity carried right through from their single artwork to their socials and Spotify. Catch the lads performing live most weekends around Ireland.
activity_description_1756618976097833920: For 8 years Irish rock 'n' rollers The Strypes tore up stages around the world from Glastonbury, Fuji Rock and the David Letterman show to tours with the likes of Arctic Monkeys, Foo Fighters, Blur, Stone Roses and many more. Now drummer and founding member Evan Walsh has brought the band's legacy forward with The Savage Hearts, mixing psychedelia and garage rock sounds with the tight, experienced musicianship of Darragh Muldoon, Stef Byrne and Sam Morrissey. In the short time since forming the band has scored 5 No. 1 singles on the Irish downloads chart and gigged heavily including shows with iconic acts The Boomtown Rats, The Undertones, Dr. Feelgood, Jerry Fish and The Would Be's amongst others. The band has also hit some of the UK's most iconic stages from London's Hope & Anchor, Hawley Arms and Dublin Castle to the iconic Cavern Club in Liverpool. Now signed to UK indie label Blaggers Records and working on their debut album, The Savage Hearts' future is looking brighter than ever.
activity_description_1756618994921870272:
Shakalak are an Irish psychedelic hip-hop band who have built a dedicated cult following over the last number of years. Their music is built with live electronic beats, synthesisers,  psychedelic electric guitar, and saxophone, coupled with the lyrical dexterity of poet John Cummins. They have performed sold out headline shows in Dublin (Whelan's, Workman’s Club, Grand Social, Button Factory) and many other venues and festivals around Ireland.

Their most recent album Kulture Bikki is a global, local, lyrical, musical, rhythmic trip.
Trigger warning: May Contain Love Bullets - Enjoy the dip!

"Cummins is the real deal; a curious, musical, staccato flow, and brilliantly nostalgic and visceral tales of festival, childhood, football and chippers." 
 - The Irish Times on Shakalak frontman John Cummins
activity_description_1756653084714807492: The soundtrack to glitter, wellies and ice creams. DJ Will Softly brings festival-sized singalongs to the Ickle Big Stage with clean edits of today’s hits, indie classics, and 70/80/90/00s nostalgia. From rock anthems to dancefloor fillers, he’s got parents + kids dancing in the same tent. Bubbles, big choruses, zero stress. The daytime party everyone attends. Amazing prizes for the best dancers.
activity_name_1756653096920232132: Hype Man Jackson feat. Calum Kieran
activity_description_1756653096920232132: Hype Man Jackson feat. Calum Kieran is an energetic brother duo from Dublin, bringing big festival energy, crowd interaction and feel-good music to audiences of all ages. Nine-year-old Jackson leads the entertainment as the act’s charismatic hype man, while his older brother Calum Kieran delivers dynamic DJ sets tailored to every audience, blending a wide range of genres while staying true to his signature electronic sound rooted in techno, trance and acid-driven music.
activity_description_1756653104394481860: DonKing Rongavilla is a dynamic force in the world of dance and performance, bringing creativity, energy, and expertise to every project. With experience in both small and large-scale productions across various genres, he has established himself as a dancer, choreographer, director, instructor, teacher, presenter, and performer. A true creative visionary, he is dedicated to pushing boundaries and delivering unforgettable experiences. He can make everyone dance , inclusivity is the key. Whether on stage, behind the scenes, or in the studio, Don King Rongavilla continues to inspire and elevate the world of dance and performance.
activity_description_1756653119267483844: Grab your seats early and hang on tight… Niall de Búrca returns for a hooley of tales! Niall is a Seanchaí with a unique style that appeals to audiences worldwide. As a kid in the West he listened to scéals aplenty. Nowadays he performs and investigates stories in amazing countries like Korea, Lithuania and Ghana. Get ready for a talefeast that will take you on a rollercoaster ride of the imagination! Niall has performed in such wonderful places as Áras an Uachtaráin and Kronberg Castle in Denmark where Shakespeare set Hamlet. He’s even performed aboard the Sea Stallion; a replica of a 1000 year old Viking ship that was built in Ireland with wood from Glendalough!
activity_description_1756653119619805380: Ballymore-Eustace Concert Band presents an array of music with a repertoire featuring movie scores, pop classical and rock pieces. Expect everything from Bon Jovi to Sondheim to Abba from this 40 strong community band.
activity_description_1756653131640680644: Baby Boppers & Rhythm Rascals is a music-filled dance class with lots of colour and fun involved. It’s a class where parents and little ones move together to the beat! And don’t worry those beats aren’t just all the baby preferences, a lot are tunes parents absolutely love! Wear babies comfortably in their baby carriers for gentle movement, while allowing little crawlers and walkers explore rhythms in a safe, supportive, feel good space. Designed to boost fitness, coordination, and bonding, each session promotes well-being for both parent and child. Move to the groove, prism to the rhythm, connect and bop one beat at a time at our workshop.
activity_name_1756653146564014276: Kowgirl Kourtney - Aerial and Hula Hoop Extravaganza
activity_description_1756653146564014276: Kowgirl Kourtney is bringing the Wild West to Electric Picnic with an action-packed aerial and hula hoop show, followed by a fun, interactive hula hoop workshop for all ages. Expect big tricks, big smiles, and plenty of fun for the whole family!
activity_description_1756653167745249476: Sons of Éire are a trio of Irish musicians — Liam Lynch (Bailieborough, Co. Cavan), Mark Haines (Birr, Co. Offaly) and Andrew Beirne (Carrigallen, Co. Leitrim). The group has represented Ireland internationally, performing at the Irish Embassy in Zambia for St Patrick's Day celebrations in both 2024 and 2025 — a rare honour reflecting their standing as ambassadors for Irish traditional music abroad. Drawing from three different counties, Sons of Éire bring a shared passion for Irish music and culture, blending tradition with a modern edge that resonates with audiences at home and overseas.
activity_description_1756653175051727044: Performing originals and covers, Abigail is preparing her debut album and is delighted to be bringing her sound to Electric Picnic this year. Inspired by the likes of boygenius, Big Thief and Elliott Smith, her set will shift from quiet and vulnerable to bold and powerful.
activity_description_1756653190755201220: Mark Langtry, aka 'Mark the Science Guy', - the nation's favourite science teacher. Mark is a Scientist, Author, Educator and Presenter of RTE's award-winning science series, 'Let's Find Out'. Through exciting live shows, television, media content and educational resources, Mark brings science to life for audiences of all ages. His work inspires curiosity, encourages people to explore how the world works, and empowers young people to learn, grow and realise their potential through education.
activity_description_1756653199882006724: Crann is Ireland’s oldest trees charity, celebrating our 40th anniversary this year. Our mission is to educate and promote the beauty and true value of Ireland’s trees. Crann’s education team visit schools across Ireland. The Little Picnic shows are aimed at giving all the young Picnic-ers and their families an authentic Crann experience and to explain our schools’ programme. The workshops and performances promise to be practical, exciting and action-packed outdoor learning experiences for tree-planting and story-filled, inclusive and musical, arts-based adventures. In the words of our founder Jan Alexander, this will be a ‘hearts and minds’ experience where our young people will learn how to “Re-leaf Ireland”- from Stradbally to the rest of the world. Crann’s education officer James Lowry is a primary and inclusive educator with 25 years of work in Irish schools and their woodlands and gardens. He is also a member of the Irish Wildlife Trust and the Climate ambassador programme.
activity_description_1756653208211894468: Ruth Shine School of Dance, established for over 20 years, is a forward thinking, creative dance school based in Blessington and Palmerstown. We firmly believe dance is for everyone and push ourselves to provide the highest quality classes for our community.
activity_description_1756653221029687492: Learn the skills needed to handcraft a unique instrument from recycled materials.
activity_name_1756653238368940228: Zine Making Workshop with Etereal Magzine
activity_description_1756653238368940228: Collage Workshop with Ethereal Magazine. We'll dive into the art of combining print media using simple paper tools in a relaxed setting. Come alone and makes friends, or bring someone with you. It's a fun and playful hour of creativity to indulge your inner artist this weekend. A patient artist guides you through the session, where you'll cut and paste together an original art piece. All materials are provided but feel free to bring your own magazines or any fun printed materials you've gathered over the weekend. You can bring your collage home or we can send you a scan via email.
activity_description_1756653254131134660: Hosted by Atlantic Technological University and Offaly County Council, this workshop will give attendees the chance to pilot VEX Robots built for the primary school VEX Robotics competition on a VEX Arena. These robots will all be unique and will be able to complete different tasks moving field elements to give each participant their own distinctive experience with piloting these robots. For those with an interest in any aspect of STEM or just want to have some fun piloting automata this showcase is the right choice. A Robotics workshop where kids will get the chance to control a variety of different robots all with different capabilities for a different driving experience with each. The workshop will be an interactive demonstration of the VEX Robotics programme.
activity_name_1756653272074367172: Little Irish History Heros with Niamh Donnellan
activity_description_1756653272074367172: Join children’s author Niamh Donnellan for storytelling and crafts based on her book, Little Irish History Heroes. Niamh Donnellan is a writer and poet. She won the Anthology Short Story Award 2020 and in Kilkenny with her young family and two mischievous cats. This a fun, rhyming introduction to the heroes of Irish legend. Hear stories about the giant Fionn Mac Cumhaill, pirate queen Grace O'Malley, high king Brian Boru, bold Queen Maeve, kind St Brigid and young hurler Cú Chulainn for a new twist on ancient tales of bravery. Then make your own hero's crown to take home! Age 4-8.
activity_description_1756653278902694084: Crann is Ireland’s oldest trees charity, celebrating our 40th anniversary this year. Our mission is to educate and promote the beauty and true value of Ireland’s trees. Crann’s education team visit schools across Ireland. Crann’s education officer James Lowry is a primary and inclusive educator with 25 years of work in Irish schools and their woodlands and gardens. He is also a member of the Irish Wildlife Trust and the Climate ambassador programme.
activity_description_1756653297869336772: Get ready to stretch it, squish it, bubble it, and BLAST it! Planet Science Kidz: Slime Labs is where kids dive into the wild world of chemistry and polymers through messy, magical, hands-on fun. Create Slime Monsters, blow Giant Slime Bubbles, and watch epic Slime Falls ooze before your eyes! But that’s not all… young scientists will also witness erupting test tubes, jaw-dropping Coke geysers, and even an exciting rocket launch! It’s the ultimate lab for gooey creations, big reactions, and curious minds.One seriously fun, hands-on science adventure not to be missed!
activity_description_1756653307054862532: Join us for a hands-on T-shirt customisation workshop where a plain tee becomes something uniquely yours. Using fabric paint, ribbons, beads, eyelets, tulle and simple cutting techniques, you’ll transform a blank T-shirt into a one-off festival outfit ready for the evening’s music and celebrations. Whether you want bold graphics, statement sleeves, fringe, colour, sparkle or something completely unexpected, we’ll provide the materials, inspiration and guidance to get you started. No experience is needed and all materials are included. Suitable for all ages—just bring your imagination and leave with a custom piece you’ll actually want to wear.
activity_description_1756653316970197188: Discover the art of lino printing while creating a colourful string of festival bunting. Carve your own design or print with pre-carved stamps, then decorate your campsite or bring your bunting home as a unique reminder of the festival.
activity_name_1756653328865243332: Lino Print Your Own Wooden Bookmark
activity_description_1756653328865243332: Create a unique wooden bookmark in this fun, hands-on lino printing workshop. Carve your own stamp or choose from a collection of pre-carved designs inspired by nature and storytelling, then print your bookmark to take home as a lasting festival keepsake.
activity_description_1756653340760289476: Roll up your sleeves & get ready for messy sensory fun! Using all our senses we'll splash and squish and squash getting creative and learning how playful activities can help manage big emotions! All Abilities Ireland working out of Portlaoise for the last 15 years are here to help parents connect and little people make friends.
activity_description_1756653351279603908: Lollipop Apparel creates vibrant, handmade tie-dye hoodies designed by you and brought to life with colour, care and creativity. Choose your palette, pattern and intensity, and we’ll craft a one-of-a-kind piece that celebrates individuality and self-expression. Made from durable cotton-poly blends using eco-conscious materials, every design is infused with love, energy and a little bit of magic. Join the new tie-dye revolution and wear your creativity proudly.
activity_description_1756653364357443780: Crann is Ireland’s oldest trees charity, celebrating our 40th anniversary this year. Our mission is to educate and promote the beauty and true value of Ireland’s trees. Crann’s education team visit schools across Ireland. Crann’s education officer James Lowry is a primary and inclusive educator with 25 years of work in Irish schools and their woodlands and gardens. He is also a member of the Irish Wildlife Trust and the Climate ambassador programme.
activity_description_1756653379716985028: Shiv Hickey is a writer, actor, and Artistic Director of After Midnight Theatre. She firmly believes playing pretend is one of the best things you can do - no matter how old you are! Through games, stories, and a whole lot of "what if," Shiv helps kids to find their voices, dream up characters, and build entire worlds... out of (seemingly) nothing!
activity_description_1756653386025218244: Roll up your sleeves & get ready for messy sensory fun! Using all our senses we'll splash and squish and squash getting creative and learning how playful activities can help manage big emotions! All Abilities Ireland working out of Portlaoise for the last 15 years are here to help parents connect and little people make friends.
activity_description_1756653394506100932: Fighting Words is a creative writing organisation established in 2009 by Roddy Doyle and Seán Love in Dublin. Our aim is to help students of all ages to develop their writing skills and to explore their love of writing. All programmes are free of charge and offered in locations all over Ireland. We offer a wide range of workshops, all of which are designed to promote creativity and writing as a fun and powerful means of self-expression. Join us for fun, creativity and sharing.
activity_description_1756653403196698820: Let your little ones dive Under the Sea or step into the Circle of Life in this enchanting, interactive musical workshop. Packed with fun and magic, it’s the perfect experience for young Disney fans!
activity_description_1756653411182653636: Get ready to take a big Bite out of Broadway! From Hamilton to Sister Act—and, of course, the spellbinding WICKED!—this high-energy workshop brings the magic of musical theater to life.
activity_name_1756653417583161540: Little Irish History Heros with Niamh Donnellan
activity_description_1756653417583161540: Join children’s author Niamh Donnellan for storytelling and crafts based on her book, Little Irish History Heroes. Niamh Donnellan is a writer and poet. She won the Anthology Short Story Award 2020 and in Kilkenny with her young family and two mischievous cats. This a fun, rhyming introduction to the heroes of Irish legend. Hear stories about the giant Fionn Mac Cumhaill, pirate queen Grace O'Malley, high king Brian Boru, bold Queen Maeve, kind St Brigid and young hurler Cú Chulainn for a new twist on ancient tales of bravery. Then make your own hero's crown to take home! Age 4-8.
activity_description_1756653424646369476: School Fitness Ireland is all about Making Fitness Fun. As Ireland's No.1 provider of PE coaches nationwide, trusted by over 900 principals they deliver workshops in Gymnastics, BoxAerobics, Fun Fitness and more
activity_description_1756653432422609092: Burning Circus brings hoops, and playful movement to the Little Picnic. Blending rhythm, colour, and audience interaction into shows built especially for younger crowds. Expect juggling, hula hoop tricks, poi spinning, and plenty of laughs. Find them roaming Little Picnic with spinning, balancing, high energy, big smiles, and a genuinely joyful introduction to flow arts for the next generation of festival-goers.
activity_description_1756653432925925572: The Bubble Guys are Ireland's premier bubble performance act, combining artistry, precision and playful interaction to create breathtaking large-scale soap bubble displays. Returning to Little Picnic, they will transform the festival landscape with enormous floating bubbles, intricate bubble garlands, shimmering webs and beautifully choreographed multi-string creations that drift effortlessly through the air. Their performances invite audiences to pause, look up and experience a moment of pure wonder. Blending visual theatre with spontaneous interaction, The Bubble Guys create an atmosphere that is both magical and joyful—equally captivating for young children, teenagers and adults alike. FREE unlimited sword balloons for children with every performance.
activity_name_1756659457473221412: DJ Sonic Boom B2B Jammy Dodger
activity_description_1756659457473221412:
DJ Sonic Boom B2B Jammy Dodger is the sweet-and-sour collision you didn’t know your Electric Picnic needed.
Two selectors. One set. Absolutely no calorie counting.
Sonic Jam brings the rhythm, Jammy Dodger brings the filling, and somewhere in between the two lies a highly questionable but undeniably delicious journey through dancefloor favourites, forgotten gems, guilty pleasures and the occasional tune that has absolutely no business working until it does. A lot of the music comes directly from thrifted CD’s played live from a portable walkman…
It’s sweet. It’s sticky. It’s got a bit of crunch.
And once they’ve started, there’s no putting the packet back in the cupboard.
activity_description_1756659466289648420:
Madonna Kebab is Cara Parc: performer, DJ, disco enthusiast and one of the wonderfully uncontainable forces behind Ireland’s Ping Pong Disco.
Born from DIY parties, queer club culture and a love of doing things just a little bit differently, Madonna Kebab brings together disco, house, camp, chaos and an infectious sense of fun. Her sets are less about behaving yourself and more about giving yourself permission to completely lose the run of yourself.
As part of the Ping Pong Disco family, she has helped create some of Ireland’s most joyful and outrageous festival experiences, spaces where disco bangers meet wild performance, glitter meets sweat and absolutely nobody is quite sure what’s going to happen next.
There’s a strong Irish streak running through it all: humour, mischief, irreverence and the ancient art of having the absolute craic.
Bring your dancing shoes. Leave your dignity at the door.
activity_description_1756659472019067684: DJ Battery Acid delivers the high-corrosive fuel needed to keep the festival pistons pumping. Expect a volatile cocktail of wonky techno, belligerent bass, and bombastic tekno, all heavily blessed with raw, chaotic Amen breaks. Pure high-voltage rave adrenaline designed for structural dancefloor damage.
activity_description_1756659479333933860:
Global DJ and NTS Radio host of nine years, Donna Leake has also spent the last two years running three weekly shows on ROVR. Driven by an evolving love for sound exploration, her eclectic sets span global traditional folk, jazz, hip-hop, dub, UK bass, and cinematic library music.
Recently, Donna has injected heavier electronic sounds into her late-night club sets, diving deep into vinyl-only selections of dubstep, jungle, grime, dancehall, and experimental percussion.
Every performance adapts entirely to the venue, system, and crowd energy. Using music as a healer, teacher, and sonic portal, her ultimate mission is to craft a storytelling space where dancers can unite, reflect, and move freely through life's many moods together.
activity_description_1756659486288089892:
THXTTI is one of Dublin’s freshest young selectors, bringing a fearless, playful energy to the dancefloor and a serious instinct for knowing exactly what a crowd needs.
A regular around Dublin’s newest and most exciting club nights, THXTTI has appeared at Mo Cultivation, Club Comfort and Rathaus, quickly building a reputation as one to watch on the city’s underground circuit.
For this Metro set THXTTI has a one way ticket to bring Afro-electronic sounds to the platform.
activity_description_1756659494911578916:
DJ PCP (Colm Olwill) is a riotous record obsessive hijacking the dancefloor since the early ’90s. Forget borders and genre rules—this set is a chaotic dive into rare, weaponized 21st-century carnival music.
As the mastermind behind Gramophone Disco, The Haunt, and Trad Rave, Colm has brought his sonic mayhem to Glastonbury, Electric Picnic, and All Together Now. Expect big beats, strange wax, and absolute musical anarchy.
activity_description_1756659501530190628:
FESSA is a Berlin-based artist bringing a raw, unapologetic edge to the dancefloor. Born as a DIY solo project during lockdown, her sound lives somewhere between synth-punk, darkwave, electronic pop and the dirtier side of the underground.
Drawing on 80s-inspired bass loops, fuzzy guitars, distorted synths and infectious pop instincts, FESSA creates music that feels both nostalgic and completely of the moment. There’s darkness, humour, confrontation and plenty of attitude.
Her work refuses to sit neatly inside one genre, moving between driving electronic rhythms, post-punk energy and warped pop sensibilities. Recent appearances on underground European line-ups have seen her share space with artists from the techno, electronica and alternative scenes.
For Electric Picnic, expect something loud, strange and brilliantly unpredictable: dirty synths, heavy bass, punk spirit and enough attitude to shake the Metro out of its comfort zone.
FESSA doesn’t do background music.
activity_description_1756659507653874468:
Gaff-e is mutating her signature, neon-drenched chaos into something far more sinister. Known across the global circuit for her wild energy and boundary-pushing showmanship, this specific outing sees her descending straight into the shadows.
Ditching the euphoric pop structures, Gaff-e is weaponizing a stark, late-night darkwave disco style set. Expect a hypnotic, pulse-pounding collision of industrial-tinged basslines, moody synthesizers, and bleak, driving electronic grooves. It’s gothic attitude meeting a sweaty dancefloor, dark, danceable, and a completely unpredictable DJ set you dont want to miss.
activity_description_1756659514255708964:
B.AUGUSTUS B2B Milis is a high-stakes meeting of underground tactical minds.
B.AUGUSTUS is a seasoned selector and Dundalk free-party veteran. He spent years hammering out blistering hard tekno with the DRATPAK sound system before anchoring the heavy, bass-driven hip-hop, reggae, and electronic rituals at the Spirit Store’s Backroom Bashment.
Flanking him is Milis, the rogue sonic architect and former core producer of the Tír na gCasta movement. For this collaborative assault, Milis isn’t just trading tracks, he has been deep in the trenches handling the underlying field research, mapping out a chaotic blueprint specifically tailored to maximize B.AUGUSTUS's explosive trajectory.
activity_name_1756659522073891620: DJ Dewalt B2B DJ Hanibal Selector
activity_description_1756659522073891620:
DJ Dewalt is boarding a transatlantic flight very soon, trading Dublin build sites for big-money skyscraper contracts in New York. For his final Irish gig, he's bringing structural damage to your eardrums. Expect a wet mix of raw Irish trad, blistering hardcore, and jackhammer tempos. As his foreman noted: "His mixes have cracked more foundation walls than an earthquake. God Bless New York."
Flanking him for this Friday closing demolition is Hanibal Selector, the underground’s most elusive phantom. Rumored to be the main hitman and heavy fixer for the Dundalk TPM gang, Hanibal is a part-cartoon villain, part-evil genius who weaponizes bass like an acoustic mad scientist.
activity_description_1756659529120322340:
Tailor Birds is the dream-folk world of Sophie Kinston — a place where electric violin, live looping, vocals, spoken word and the sounds of the natural world collide.
At the heart of the project is a five-string electric violin, layered live with looping pedals, electronics and an ever-growing collection of sounds. Sophie’s music moves between folk, experimental electronics, classical textures and something altogether harder to name: music that feels like wandering through a strange forest at dusk.
Her fascination with the natural world goes even further. Through plant-music biosonification, electrical signals from plants, food, trees and even buildings can become part of the music, creating soundscapes that are genuinely rooted in their surroundings.
Sophie has spent years touring between Australia and Europe, appearing at festivals including Glastonbury, Vantastival, Rewild and Boyle Arts Festival. Now based in West Cork, she continues to create music that tells stories of love, loss, hope and possibility.
For the Metro, expect a little magic.
activity_description_1756659534732301092:
Over 20 years of friendship has led to this collaboration, creating bilingual lyrics and hip hop/trip hop beats with a twist of abstract echoing their sound system days. They have played at various venues & festivals since 2020, including Only Your Footprints, Body & Soul, Future Limerick, Fred Zeplins, Triskel Arts Centre, Brú Bar, Crane Lane, Electric Picnic 2023/2025,The Grand Social, Levis’s, Róisín Dubh
 and The Pav. They are currently working on their first album. You can find their tracks to date on Bandcamp. SLC have been played on Raidió na Gaeltachta and Raidió na Life.
activity_description_1756659540772098852:
Emma Lohan is an Irish songwriter, producer and performance artist whose music sits somewhere between ancient folk traditions and the electronic future. A musician with deep roots in the west of Ireland, Emma has spent years exploring the meeting point between voice, storytelling, rhythm and technology.
She calls her sound “Techno Folk”, a fitting description for music that takes the warmth and storytelling of folk and throws it into a world of synths, loops, electronic beats and unexpected textures. Her live performances are immersive and often created in real time, using hardware, loop stations and vocals to build evolving soundscapes around the audience.
Formerly of Rivers & Crows and New Pope, Emma has also released her acclaimed solo album Black Atlantic, drawing inspiration from Irish folk, West African rhythms and her travels through different musical cultures.
For the Metro at Electric Picnic, expect something organic, hypnotic and wonderfully difficult to categorise… folk music for the 21st century, with a beat underneath it.
activity_description_1756659547759809316:
“…Yet was it not my master to the very extent that it was my creature, had I not breathed into my own spirit” 

Colm Olwill(DJ PCP, Trad Rave) and well-known piper Eoin Ó Briain.

With a shared love of the pipes, the sesh and breakcore. Colm and Eoin met up to practice and explore how the sonorities of rave music can meld with the drones and tones of the Uilleann pipes. Bolting Irish and club music together to hear what monstrosities result.
activity_description_1756659554210648868:
DJ Karmawi (the slang name for a rebel from Tulkarm, Palestine) is an Irish-Palestinian DJ and producer tearing up the rulebook. He doesn't just play tracks; he weaponizes the dancefloor as a portal into global lives and shared struggles.
Armed with a relentless passion for sonic expression, Karmawi hijacks Irish club culture to blast diverse electronic sounds from every corner of the underground. Expect heavy, driving basslines meant to make you groove and aggressive highs designed to make you move.
Pure solidarity, heavy frequencies, and absolute dancefloor liberation.
activity_description_1756659560200114980:
Лукас Огма, the Bruto Soviet Alter Ego of Lucas Ogma, Fuinneamh Festival founder, who takes us on a special journey curated especially for The Brutopolis State.
Since 2011, Lucas has been producing electronic music and DJing, crafting a richly textured, atmospheric, and hypnotic style of techno focused on stimulating raw emotion and guiding hypnotic dancefloor journeys.
This performance is a raw trip into post-Soviet times. It masterfully blends driving techno with post-punk industrial textures and retro synthwave. Think of this as a hot and sweaty Cold War music set.
activity_description_1756659573277954852: Magz has been deploying eclectic party bangers as weapons of mass disruption for the last decade. Not specific to one style but with an industrial, germanic and punk influence. She’ll be keeping it dark and dirty with a stomping set. No compromise, No regret, just relentless bangers
activity_description_1756659580039172900:
DJackulate is one of Ireland’s most distinctive turntablists, a Dublin-born musical polymath whose approach to DJing stretches far beyond the traditional decks. Also known as Jack Dempsey McMahon, he is a two-time world freestyle turntablist champion, renowned for his inventive use of samples, scratching and live manipulation.
A lifelong record obsessive, DJackulate digs deep into everything from Irish traditional music and folk to hip-hop, electronic music, jazz and experimental sounds, turning unexpected fragments into something entirely new. His work has seen him collaborate across the worlds of improvised music, theatre and electronic performance, while projects such as H-Ci and OKO showcase his restless, genre-defying approach.
He has also brought his unique take on Irish music to the dancefloor through Trad Rave, blending classic and contemporary trad with beats and bass alongside DJ PCP. 
Expect a set that refuses to stay on one track once the train leaves the Balkans.
activity_description_1756659586154468132: Grab your whips and buckle up for one hell of a ride through the Wild Wild West—an afternoon of country classics, dusty trails and a fistful of country bangers.
activity_description_1756659597151933220: Dundalk’s Laurence Kapinga, aka StrangeLove, has slowly been carving out a distinct space in Ireland’s music community as both a DJ and producer. With releases on 3024 and Reasons To Dance, as well as his work in the alternative R&B duo Negro Impacto, he’s become known for a sound that fluidly crosses genres while maintaining a singular identity within the Irish scene.
activity_description_1756659603174953764:
ÉABHA is the electronic solo project of Éabha Campbell, known as a member of Irish post-punk outfit Madrúa. Based in Belfast, ÉABHA inhabits the darker, stranger edges of electronic music, pulling together industrial electronics, synth-pop, EBM, no-wave and post-punk into something both visceral and hypnotic.
There’s a beautifully unsettling quality to the project with detached vocals, pulsing electronics, cold synth textures and rhythms that seem to emerge from somewhere between a basement club and a dystopian nightclub. It’s music with atmosphere, attitude and a healthy disregard for genre boundaries.
Campbell’s background in sound-based performance and experimental art feeds directly into the project, where music becomes part of a wider world of texture, imagery and sensation.
For the Metro at Electric Picnic, expect something dark, physical and immersive. A set that shifts the temperature of the room and invites you into ÉABHA’s own electronic universe.
activity_description_1756659609684513572:
HYYKEN is one of Ireland’s most exciting contemporary electronic artists, bringing a distinctly groove-led sound to dancefloors at home and far beyond. His music sits somewhere between stripped-back minimal house, rolling basslines, UK garage, techno and euphoric club energy, with a healthy dose of nostalgia running through it.
With releases on Patrick Topping’s Trick, DJ Haus’ UTTU, Southern Fried Records and Reboot Records, HYYKEN has developed a sound that manages to feel both underground and immediately infectious. His productions are built for movement, chunky grooves, memorable vocals, driving rhythms and those moments that turn a packed room into one big dancefloor.
His international journey has taken him from Irish festivals and clubs to Ibiza, Amsterdam, Bristol and Tenerife, including appearances alongside some of the biggest names in contemporary house music.
For the Metro at Electric Picnic, expect groove, nostalgia and serious dancefloor pressure. HYYKEN is here to get you moving, and he’s not planning on letting up.
activity_description_1756659615934026532:
INFLUX is an American electronic artist whose sound exists somewhere between the hypnotic, the psychedelic and the completely unexpected. A long-time explorer of the outer edges of electronic music, INFLUX moves effortlessly through acid, trance, techno, IDM and experimental sounds, creating sets that feel less like a DJ performance and more like stepping into another dimension.
There’s a distinctly old-school spirit running through the music with analogue textures, warped rhythms, hypnotic sequences and a fascination with the possibilities of machines. But INFLUX is never simply looking backwards. The sound is constantly mutating, pulling strange and unexpected influences into the mix.
INFLUX is for those who like their dance music a little stranger… Sound that gets under your skin, bends the edges of the room and keeps you up later than you should be.
activity_description_1756659622049321764:
Azu Tiwaline is a Tunisian producer and DJ whose hypnotic sound draws deeply from her Saharan roots and Tunisian heritage. Based between Tunisia and France, she creates an immersive meeting point between dub, techno, trance, experimental electronics and the raw, organic rhythms of North Africa.
Her music is shaped by the landscapes of El Djerid, incorporating field recordings, polyrhythmic percussion and deep bass into richly textured, psychedelic soundscapes. The result is both meditative and deeply physical — music that invites movement while creating a sense of place.
Azu has released acclaimed music through I.O.T Records and Bristol’s Livity Sound, including her albums Draw Me a Silence and The Fifth Dream. Her hybrid live/DJ sets have taken her to major festivals and clubs around the world, including Dekmantel, Dimensions, Freerotation, MUTEK, Unsound and Berghain.
activity_description_1756688758914580236: The Baka believe that "spirits" live in the forest who like to dance with people. Their music is designed to call these spirits to come and dance, and make peoples’ problems disappear. Festival favourites, Baka Beyond, certainly live up to this. With musicians from Cornwall, Wales, England, Congo and Sierra Leone, they mix the Spirit of the Forest with Celtic, African and modern sounds to create a positive feel-good vibe that you can’t help but move to. Let’s dance!
activity_description_1756688772554456844: Raz Olsher & Afla Sackey: a bond that fuels a dynamic and effortless musical relationship. Their music represents a harmonious union of African influences with electronic music, full of soul, vibrant energy and captivating rhythms. The balance between Raz’s production style and Afla’s Afrocentric flavours ignited dance floors and earned the duo a glowing reputation from the very beginning. Their debut album, ‘The Cycle’, came out late 2022 and has gained critical acclaim from the likes of Gilles Peterson, Lauren Lavern, Jamz Supernova and was play listed on BBC Radio 6,1Xtra, FIP, Radio Nova as well as obtaining fans from their peers and remixing the likes of Glass Animals, Batida and Crate Classics
activity_name_1756688782864056076: Luke Thomas and Paul Dunlem Big Band
activity_description_1756688782864056076: Ireland's KING OF SWING Luke Thomas and his band The Swing Cats - Specializing in uptempo swing music and VINTAGE POP MUSIC with two No.1 albums, Three TV Concerts Specials, countless sold out tours and 9 personally requested performances for President Higgins Luke Thomas & The Swing Cats are one of the most in-demand live bands in Ireland. As seen on Late Late Show, Ireland AM, SIX O'Clock Show, Today Show and heard on every major radio station in the country!!
activity_description_1756688792192188172: Step into the mesmerising world of The Circus Ponies, a 16-piece band reimagining 90’s club classics with their own unique flair. Taking inspiration from Dec Pierce’s Block Rockin Beats, Jenny Greene and the Concert Orchestra & MEUTE, this musical collective delivers electrifying performances that have astounded audiences at venues and festivals across the country. Prepare for a dazzling visual and auditory feast as The Circus Ponies take the stage, igniting an explosion of colour, energy, and nostalgia. With their unstoppable presence and infectious beats, they bridge the gap between the past and the present, creating an unforgettable experience that will leave you yearning for more.
activity_description_1756688800278806284: The New Brass Kings is a 6-piece brass band from Dublin, Ireland. The band came together 8 years ago, finding common ground out of a love/hate relationship with brass, and music, and each other. The line-up of musicians differs here and there but fear not, the quality always stays at the highest level imaginable. Like, really imagine it. Often found busking in the centre of the city, they’re no strangers to festivals, parties, corporate functions, weddings, you name it.Thanks to the acoustic nature of the band and their mobility they’re easily the most versatile band in the entire world. Their setlist is comprised of the best songs you’ve ever heard, but played better, on brass. This is all sarcastic, please do not use it as a blurb for our gigs. We once played in a parade with an announcer who read this blurb to the whole crowd all the way to that last sentence before he realised what he had done. It was very funny.
activity_description_1756688812459065100: Based in the vibrant city of Galway, Los Wachos is a spirited Latin band that celebrates the diverse sounds of Latin music. Our talented musicians hail from various countries, each bringing their unique flavour to our performances. As a close-knit group of friends, we share a passion for creating joyful, infectious rhythms that inspire everyone to hit the dance floor. We are on a mission to spread happiness through our music, touring across Ireland and lighting up pubs and festivals with our lively tunes. Join us for an evening of unforgettable fun, where our beats will surely make you move your feet!
activity_description_1756688829018177292: Nine salsa musicians. One mission: make you move. Tumbao Dublin brings the sounds of Cuba, Puerto Rico and Miami. Powered by deep hypnotic Afro-Cuban polyrhythms of rumba, punchy brass and groovy keys and tres cubano. The drums make you pound the ground. The Brass make you shimmy your shoulders ... and the bass ... that gets into your hips!!  Rooted in salsa tradition but played with the energy of a modern festival band, we bring azúcar, serious funk and even more serious sabor. . Electric Picnic — ¡a bailar!
activity_description_1756688838421806860: Largo da Cumbia are on a mission to spread a message of unity through the rhythm of Latin America: Cumbia. With members from Chile, UK, and Portugal, each member brings a unique influence, mixing danceable grooves, psychedelic effects, and a Punk-Rock energy. The band has performed in Portugal, Spain, and Ireland, and they just released their debut EP that explores their roots of migration and cultural exchange. As musicians who have performed across Latin America and Europe, the band brings a unifying energy and positive vibes to each stage that never fails to get a crowd bouncing and turn casual crowds into committed Cumbia converts. The band creates a huge sound with only 5 members: effects pedals on Keyboard, Accordion and Clarinet meet the pounding groove foundation of Drums, Bass, Vocals and Guiro to bring audiences together dancing with an irresistible energy and message.
activity_description_1756688854024617740: Havana Roots is a mash-up of traditional Son Cubano with the nearby Jamaican Reggae and Ska.
activity_description_1756688862346116876: Code of Behaviour are an Irish brass band from Cork City. Their style is a blend of street jazz, jump-around pop and enough madness to make every moment a party. Originally known for "livening up the streets of Cork", the band features trumpets, trombones, mellophone, saxophone, sousaphone and drums, occasional vocals and – fortunately – just a little choreography. Get ready for mayhem.
activity_description_1756688876715802380:
The Sea of Change is not your average choir. We’re a vibrant, mad craic, bunch of women brought together by cancer, friendship, music and a mad determination to enjoy life. We’ve featured on Ireland’s Got Talent, Britain’s Got Talent, we debuted at Electric Picnic last, recorded at Windmill Lane, received a standing ovation in European Parliament, Brussels for World Cancer Day, and sold our two concerts in the National Concert Hall

Out of a possible 120 boobs we have 109 and a half so if you see is dancing lopsided, bear with us.

Behind the sequins, singing and occasional chaos we fundraise through the incredible Strip & Dip, we have raised €1.5 million for Aoibheann’s Pink Tie, Ireland's Childhood cancer charity.  We are proud three-time Guinness World Record Holders.

We sing loudly, laugh even louder and believe life is for living. We are the Sea of Change – Come visit us
activity_description_1756688887746821900:
O.KAYE is a London/Brighton-based DJ and selector, carving out a name with explosive energy behind the decks. Expect to be surprised and fully immersed: his performances seamlessly fuse hardgroove, breakbeat, underground rap, electro, jungle, and hardcore into a raw, high-energy force.

Founder of the rising event label All Be Equal (A.B.E.), O.KAYE has brought boundary-pushing parties to venues across the UK, with the collective now standing as a backbone of the London underground. 
He has lit up major festivals including Boomtown and Latitude, is part of the legendary Disco Shed, and has shared stages with icons such as Phil Hartnoll (Orbital), Hedex, Chamber 45, and many more.

Every performance is unpredictable and intense, a surge of rhythm and energy - built to move bodies, keep crowds locked in, and hit with bass that shakes sound systems to their core.
activity_description_1756688888409521932: Born in 2023, the Propaganda Van served as the Trailer Park headquarters for the highly incompetent festival political party, the Propaganda Machine, led by brutal dictator Naoise Ó Muirí. In 2023 he fought off democratic opposition to maintain power. In 2024, as the nation thrived, the ageing leader sought a successor from the festival crowd, but none would suffice. By 2025, other factions began to feel the power of the Propaganda Machine, and citizens rose in rebellion, led by Radio Providencia, who overthrew the regime—though Ó Muirí's fate remains uncertain. The shattered remnants of his party regrouped in Providencia, rebranding themselves as T.A.M.P.O.N.S.(Truthful Agenda Ministry of Powerful Organised National Socialists), However, beneath facade, their authoritarian nature lingered. As they resumed operations, Radio Providencia uncovered their deception, igniting a secret war of propaganda, mischief, and sabotage that spread throughout Providencia, 2025 in a chaotic clash of ideology and ego.
activity_description_1756688889055444748: Identical twins My Bad Sister are a turbo-charged, all-singing and all-dancing duo that have now teamed up with there little sister DJ Minki. The East London-born sisters are a creative force to be reckoned with, mashing up traditional cockney-style performance with memorable melodies and heavy beats of all genres. A truly unforgettable live act, MBS’s razor-sharp mirrored choreography, boundary-pushing style and subversive lyrics have earned them some serious love on the underground freeparty scene.
activity_description_1756688898517794572: A duo with your eyes open but a full band with your eyes closed. Your best describing them yourself when you see and or hear them.
activity_description_1756688907971755788: French singer, guitarist and songwriter Elise FRANK blends Blues, Rock and Soul with a contemporary edge. Rooted in deep American blues and inspired by the raw energy of 90s garage rock, her music favours authenticity over polish. On stage, she performs with intensity and emotional depth, shaping a sound that is both direct and unfiltered. Following acclaimed appearances across Europe, including Ireland, the UK and major blues stages, and her signing with Ruf Records in 2025, Elise FRANK continues to build her presence on the European blues scene.
activity_description_1757143955931640828:
Kyla Cobbler is a Cork-born stand-up comedian, and one of the fastest-rising names on the international comedy scene.

Known for her raw, unfiltered storytelling, rapid-fire crowd work, and magnetic stage presence, Kyla first built a massive digital following through viral Instagram reels, amassing over a million followers and 100 million video views, before taking the live stage by storm in 2021.

Since then, her rise has been meteoric. After selling out her debut tour, Gone Rogue, across Ireland, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, and Canada, Kyla is bringing her follow-up tour, Not My Lemons, to Dublin’s iconic 3Arena. Unapologetic, razor-sharp, and effortlessly relatable, she continues to solidify her reputation as a must-see live performer and one of the most exciting new voices.

Beyond the stage, Kyla is a sought-after guest across major broadcast television and top comedy podcasts, including The Tommy Tiernan Show, Ireland AM, Uncharted with Ray Goggins, Have A Word, Talking Bollox, Tea With Me, and Alan Carr’s Life’s a Beach.

She adds another major milestone to her career this September with the release of her debut book, Happy, Thank You. More, Please.
activity_description_1757759033131233056: Celebrating 10 years of Transmission feels incredibly special. It's been an amazing journey to watch it grow from essentially nothing into what I genuinely believe is one of the most creative and distinctive electronic music stages in Ireland, constantly backing creativity, taking risks, and creating an incredibly intimate atmosphere that's completely its own. This year I'm excited to bring some of my own productions into the set for the first time, alongside a selection of deep, dark, rhythmic and hypnotic techno. Looking forward to celebrating a decade of Transmission with everyone who's been part of the journey. Every year at Transmission is special, but this year feels that extra bit.
activity_description_1757783672570153932:
When a DJ has been at the helm of the party for 25 years, you know they’re doing something right. Sally Cinnamon exemplifies a golden age of the Irish party, which some may be too young to remember. For over two decades, she has been a mainstay in Irish nightlife institutions and now she’ll be performing at Beyond The Pale this weekend. 
You don’t have this much skin in the game without becoming a scholar of various sounds. The beautiful thing about a Sally Cinnamon set is that each one draws from a different world. Ranging from the psychedelic to the electronic to afro-sounds, no two sets are alike. A strong current of retro sounds run through her sets giving her selections the quality of unifying generations. 
There are two types of DJs, one that give an avalanche of bangers and ones that take you on a musical journey. Although Sally’s sets are far from devoid of stellar sounds, we’re also taken on an expedition, almost touching every continent with her selection. Nothing exemplifies this more than her Cabal, All aboard set. Skim through and you’ll be swung from jungle to italo-disco in a heartbeat, all whilst on a Viking ship. 
A DJ in their purest form, Sally Cinnamon is representative of a persistent culture of nightlife joy even against all the odds in Ireland.
activity_description_1757783700193840076:
Grá are a 6 piece doom-folk project creating a new sound within the Irish folk scene, Grá combine acoustic and synthesised sounds that reimagine Ireland’s traditional music. 
Grá have captured a following early on that refuse to look away, the band host a weekly residency in Egan’s pub in Dublin.
activity_description_1757783712617368524:
Fresh from RTE's Late Late Show, a special performance in an Amazonian Opera House, performing at Paris Fashion Week and opening for Snow Patrol on a series of massive outdoor shows this summer, Morgana’s momentum is undeniable. Before releasing any music she had already supported CMAT across North America and Europe and opened for Dermot Kennedy. Her recent single "I’m Not Going Anywhere" hit 100k streams in just two weeks and her Other Voices St James’ Church performance was selected for broadcast on BBC4, ahead of sold-out headline shows in Dublin and London. Her new single "Fix Your Heart For Free", out May 20th, sees Morgana flex her full vocal range as she showcases operatic vocal techniques over luscious indie pop instrumental.

Praised by Una Mullally in Irish Times as “a hugely sensitive performer… you can feel the 10,000 hours behind her,” Morgana brings a voice that stops rooms.

She first gained attention as a solo artist before co-founding Saint Sister, whose journey included opening for Robbie Williams, Keane, Tori Amos, Hozier and The National, plus a spellbinding NPR Tiny Desk Concert. With millions of streams and a devoted following, Morgana’s next chapter is a solo journey into kaleidoscopic popstar-dom. Her music is a mantra: prepared to party, ready to cry. Fans of CMAT, Kate Bush, Sharon Van Etten, and Chappell Roan will fall in love with Morgana’s technicoloured, tearful disco.
activity_description_1757783725560990668:
The Mo Cultivation crew are bringing a feel good party to the Lovely Local on Friday evening. Packed with R&B, hiphop, soul, disco and 00s throwbacks... the kind of bangers you forgot you knew every word to, alongside gorgeous songs you might just be discovering for the first time.

Come with an open mind, stay for the great tunes and wonderful people. This music is for everyone, come enjoy yourself!
activity_description_1757783725972032460:
Hailing from the Comeragh Mountains of County Waterford, The Wran are four brothers: Tommy, Danny, Seán and Stephen Dunford. They bring a fresh voice to Irish music, blending trad with punk and a hint of psychedelia to create music that feels both timeless and new. Drawing inspiration from Planxty, The Pogues and Lankum,  
The Wran combines traditional and modern instrumentation, including banjo, harmonium, acoustic guitar, bass VI and drums. They are dedicated to keeping the Irish language, traditional songs and storytelling alive while continuing to push it forward in their own way.  
After an explosive live debut in 2025, including accoladed performances at Glastonbury, Green Man, All Together Now, and Electric Picnic, the band went on to support The Scratch and Kíla, play Dublin’s Notable NYD festival, and sell out their first Irish tour. Beginning 2026 with a sold-out UK tour, The Wran are fast establishing themselves as one of Ireland’s most vital new bands.
activity_description_1757783745559432140:
KK Lewis is a Dublin singer-songwriter blending soul, R&B and cinematic pop. Her single 
Pigeon Man went viral with over 3 million views, while follow-up One Step Behind landed as 
RTE Radio 1's Track of the Week. New music recorded with producer Joseph Rodgers (Beabadoobee, Rina Sawayama), drawing comparisons to Olivia Dean and RAYE, is due in the coming months. 
 
Live with her five-piece band, KK turns a stage into a living room, equal parts tearjerker and singalong, the kind of show where you leave feeling like you've made a new best friend.
activity_description_1757783760457599948: BLKCNVS, the Dublin-based Nigerian-Irish DJ whose sets draw on a rich, global palette shaped by years of collecting and blending sounds across clubs, festivals, day parties, and even family gatherings. As founder of The Sweet Spot (@sweetspot.mp3), who currently host a monthly get together in Dublin City’s Project Arts Centre, he's focused on creating warm spaces that welcome dreamers & dancers to let loose, unwind & SHAKE RUMP — because it's good for you. Using riddims to spread much love from Ireland to The World.
activity_description_1757783770792365004:
Surka is a Dublin-based DJ, known for her distinctive house sound and instinctive approach to the dancefloor. In just three years, she’s taken her sound well beyond Ireland, with standout sets in London and Colombia and a Berlin debut at Renate. At home, she’s become a familiar name across the country’s biggest festivals, including Electric Picnic and All Together Now, and has shared lineups with Leftfield, Caribou and many more.

Her sets are confident, melodic and built around momentum, moving between deep and progressive house, trance and euphoric club music with a sound that’s distinctly her own.

A resident with Reclaim the Mainframe, Surka has established herself as one of the names to watch coming out of Dublin, with a growing international profile and an increasingly strong presence on the Irish festival and club circuit.
activity_description_1757783788785929164:
Graham Smyth is a Broadcaster, Musician and DJ who you can catch both on-air on 2FM and at your local club or national festival. 
 
You might know 2FM’s Graham Smyth from presenting with Emma Power on Saturdays and 
Sundays. Or you might recognise him from his cover slots for Dave Fanning, Jenny Greene, Dan Hegarty and the like... Graham has on-air chats with the likes of Jungle, Erol Alkan and Jazzy as well as producing remixes for Irish artists such as Tolu Makay and Dark Tropics! 
 
Graham released his debut album, ‘Music For Babies To Rave And Sleep To’ via Practise Music in 2025, an ambient LP to introduce young ears to the soundscapes of electronic music. His live show in support of the album debuted at End Of The Road Festival in Dorset just before its release. 
 
As an in demand live DJ and as part of Dublin Record Club you can catch Graham spinning at 
Dublin venues like Fidelity, Lucky’s and The Devlin as well as at festivals such as All Together Now, Electric Picnic and Other Voices! With no restriction on genre but always an ear to the feet on the dancefloor (and a grá for an Irish tune), you can expect an eclectic set of records, no matter what type of set Graham is mixing! 

One of the most loved and sought-after DJs in Ireland, Claire Beck is a must-see fixture of Ireland’s
music festival and club scene. She is best known for award winning radio shows on TodayFM, and her joyful DJ sets where her signature style blends
House, Disco, Indie and Queer anthems designed to keep the dancefloor full.
Each performance is designed to tell a story, serving you music that you forgot you loved, music you
will love, with a sprinkling of spicy curveballs to keep you on your toes.
activity_description_1757783798189558732: Darren Regan got into DJing as a teenager. He had a 3 year residency in his hometown in County Mayo while studying at Dublin City University. During his time in Dublin, he started to dabble in production and also began DJing at college events. After college he worked as a Host and Music Director on SPIN South West for a number of years while playing clubs and festivals across Ireland including Longitude and Electric Picnic.
activity_description_1757783846885428172: Little O is a DJ based in Dublin. Her sets are full of rhythmic and progressive sounds from around the globe. Expect to hear a blend of afrohouse, baile funk, batida, gqom, kuduro and more. A long term resident of Dublin Digital Radio, hosting and producing The Little O Show monthly on the digital station and is a regular on the Irish festival circuit, making appearances at All Together Now, Body & Soul, Electric Picnic, Haunted Dancehall and Open Ear. She has joined a great list of international acts on support duties including Ahadadream, Badsista, Brenda, C.Frim, DJ Danifox, Evehive and INVT.
activity_description_1757783862907669452:
and he, the fool are emerging as one of Ireland's most intriguing new bands, a seven headed entity with a sound that is ambitious, inviting and altogether distinctive. 

Hailing from all over the island and based between Dublin and London, their live show seamlessly shifts in style, perspective and language with a singular energy that holds crowds to every word and beat. 2025’s re:place the thought EP began to reflect this nature in their studio output, a record of moments confessional and raw. 2026 will see the release of some of their most hyped up tracks from their live performances to date, as well as a string of new gigs taking them across Ireland and
activity_description_1757783887310130124:
Over the past number of years, George Feely has cemented himself as one of Ireland's most sought after party starters. With an upfront and energetic ethos, George's approach to music is that of a house purist, while also ensuring that everyone on the dancefloor is having a bloody good time!

With his early disco edits regularly appearing in the sets of industry leaders, George was handpicked by the German label Random Mind State for his first official release. With his debut record selling out in a matter of days, George went on to secure a string of successful EP's on powerhouse labels such as Unknown To The Unknown, Permanent Vacation, Nervous Records, Shall Not Fade, Edible, and Henry Street Music to name just a few.
activity_description_1757783893601586124:
With his raw, anthemic storytelling and indie-folk edge, Dave Lofts has drawn comparisons to a young Van Morrison and the soulful authenticity of Paolo Nutini. Through songs that feel deeply personal yet universally relatable, he has built a reputation for honest songwriting and captivating live performances, earning a fiercely loyal following both online and on stage. 
 
Dave’s story is as grounded as his music. A former member of the Irish Defence Forces, he brings a unique real-world perspective to his songwriting, adding depth and authenticity to his work. That connection with audiences is reflected not only in his rapidly growing streaming success — now surpassing 500,000 monthly listeners on Spotify — but also in his impressive live track record. He has sold out 25 consecutive Irish headline shows and completed a fully sold-out debut UK tour in April, including dates in London, Manchester and Glasgow. 
 
Earlier this year, Dave performed at the 20th Anniversary Oscar Wilde Awards in Los 
Angeles during Oscar Week, alongside Dermot Kennedy. The event honoured actor 
Domhnall Gleeson, and an impromptu performance of his latest single Holy with Sarenna 
Farrell generated over 10 million views across social media platforms. As a live performer, 
Dave has shared stages with artists including Gavin James, Wolf Alice, Picture This and Kingfishr, while standout appearances at Electric Picnic and All Together Now have further cemented his reputation as one of Ireland’s most exciting new talents.
activity_description_1757783900564130764:
A fixture in Ireland’s underground scene, Minikimono has spent the last 4 years curating dance floors that feel like home. With roots in promoting and party planning with her company H&G Creations she’s been shaping the sound and spirit of Irish nightlife for 18+ years — now channeling that same joyful community energy into her DJ sets.

Her sound moves between house, disco, and soulful grooves, blending warmth, rhythm, and emotional release. She curates her set to bring big energy, emotional storytelling and positive messages to uplift, energise and spread love to every person and every dance floor.

She’s played stages alongside Jungle and The Blessed Madonna, and performed at the likes of Electric Picnic (Smirnoff / Sound Nation), All Together Now, Beyond The Pale, Mother Club, and Love Tempo, among others.

At her core, Minikimono plays for connection — moments where strangers become friends, where joyful self expression feels inevitable.
activity_description_1757783939034287052:
Esmeralda Road are a Belfast band quickly establishing themselves as one of the most exciting new live acts to emerge from the UK and Ireland.
Built on sharp songwriting, restless rhythms and an instinct for turning small rooms into full-blown parties, the band first gained attention through a string of sold-out shows in Belfast and early releases that spread quickly online. On stage, their reputation grew just as quickly. Esmeralda Road began taking their high-energy live show across the UK and Ireland, sharing stages with artists including Liam Gallagher and Primal Scream, while building a devoted following through touring.
Off the back of a support tour with Irish indie risers Basht., with new music on the horizon, and big live plans for the rest of the year, 2026 is shaping up to be a landmark year for Esmeralda Road.
activity_description_1757796725487341220:
The luck of the Irish is no coincidence when it comes to David Sheerin aka SHEE.  
 
Playing his first DJ set aged 16, SHEE has spent near 10 years grafting and developing a fanbase on the Emerald Isle. Though these days, his sound is travelling much farther than that…  
 
Barry Can’t Swim, Fred again, Disclosure, salute and Mochakk are just a few names on the long list of SHEE’s supporters. His tracks have aired on Boiler Room, Cercle, Mixmag and more. While SHEE himself has gone from playing the Irish pubs in his local town, to packing out a 5k+ tent at All Together Now (Aug 2024), as well as supporting the likes of Bicep, Sofia Kourtesis, and Sally C.  
 
Outside of Ireland, SHEE has avid fans in Vancouver, London, Berlin and beyond, with recent appearances at Lost Village, Warehouse Project, Drumsheds and Amsterdam Dance Event. He heads into 2025 with big plans already - an Australian Tour in February (including plays at Lost Sundays and xe54 Club), a headline show at NTs Loft (London), a set with FLY in Edinburgh; plus support plays for Barry Can’t Swim in Sydney, Kettama at DEPOT Cardiff, and Laureunce Guy at Lakota, Bristol.  
 
His productions are also causing waves… ‘Win You Love’ (July 23) tallies over 4.4mil streams on Spotify and features in the EA Formula 1 video game. But this momentum suggests that SHEE’s next releases will set new levels. All his releases in 2024 featured in New Music Friday UK, and his most recent single ‘LEAVES’ landed with playlist cover of Breakthrough Electronic on Amazon Music. More works in progress with Denis Sulta, Sam Alfred, Laurence Guy mean that SHEE’s sound will become ever more unavoidable.
activity_description_1757796744286211748:
Life is all about balance, and for every dream experience that shakes up your world, there’s often a sacrifice to be made. NewDad have had plenty of the former since releasing their debut single ‘How’ in 2020 and steadily building an ever-burgeoning fanbase around their spellbinding dream-pop. They’ve released a critically-acclaimed debut album in 2024’s ‘Madra’, gained a fan in their ultimate hero, The Cure’s Robert Smith, and toured parts of the world they never thought they’d get to visit.
