But for all that to be possible, the Galway three-piece have had to give up some things, too.  
 
Around four years ago, the band – singer/guitarist Julie Dawson, guitarist Sean O’Dowd, drummer Fiachra Parslow – left their home behind and moved to London. It’s a relocation that’s helped them thrive as a group, but is also something that Dawson still has mixed feelings about. “Most days I wake up and I’m like, ‘Yes, let’s fucking do this’, but I do still miss home,” she explains.  
 
That tension between knowing you’re where you need to be right now and longing to be somewhere else colours ‘Altar’, NewDad’s highly anticipated second album. Started shortly before the release of ‘Madra’, it’s deeply informed by Dawson’s yearning for home, for family and the place that she truly belongs. In some ways, the record is a tribute to Galway, the singer in reverence of her hometown.  
 
“The album itself is where I divulge my love for home,” Dawson shares, nodding to its title. “It’s the idea that Ireland is the altar and it’s the thing that I worship, in a way.” The meaning that imagined altar takes on has multiple layers to it, too. It’s a reference to the sacrifice the band has made in putting hundreds of miles between them and the people they cherish most – “Sacrifice is another thing that happens at altars; I haven’t seen it, but I’ve heard that happens,” Dawson laughs. ‘Altar’ also taps into some of the themes in the lyrics of “appeasing people, and that’s what you do at altars – appease a higher power”.  
 
“I think of where / I’d like to be / Anywhere but here / Is fine by me,” Dawson sings on the twinkling slow build of opening track, ‘Other Side’. Across that song and the album in general, that burning for home – for the place Dawson feels most at ease and like her true self – grow darker and more anxiety-ridden, themes of survival and needing to be saved repeatedly piercing through. “Kneeling at the altar / Hope I get to heaven,” she sighs on ‘Mr Cold Embrace’, an acoustic-guitar-led, string-laden beauty that also finds the singer questioning “don’t know if I should have left her”.  
 
‘Misery’, meanwhile, finds her interrogating her role in her unhappiness, acknowledging the sometimes self-inflicted nature of her gloom. “It’s all these cyclical things that we do and these patterns we fall in and out of,” she explains. “I was like, ‘Can I go home? Do I need to be here? Why am I doing this to myself? Why am I putting myself in these situations where I’m becoming deeply unhappy?’” Dawson wanted to make the song sound “surreal and alarming”, inspired by the imagery in Dante’s Inferno. “It’s very whispery and freaky.”  
 
Finale ‘Something Broken’, though, breaks the dwelling and yearning, Dawson asking to feel at home in her current location, to laugh harder, to forget what’s tormenting her. “It’s a more hopeful message in that it’s like, ‘I’m here now, let’s make the best of something that can be really hard’,” she says.  
 
‘Altar’ – recorded in January 2025 between studios in Ipswich and London – isn’t simply an album about where one comes from and wants to get back to, though. It also charts Dawson’s journey as a musician, coming to terms with the realities of her hobby and passion becoming a profession, and navigating the industry as a woman. “When you start doing music, you do it because you love playing music, you love making music,” she reasons. “I hadn’t really considered the other aspects – touring is so fun, but it’s intensive. It’s difficult. Doing social media, I hate it. Just a lot of inside pressures and politics – it’s a lot more pressure than I thought it would be.”  
 
Music, though, is still the outlet Dawson uses to alleviate the stresses in her life – even when they come from music itself. You can tell how impactful songwriting is for her just by looking at her catalogue of work so far – and the prolific levels at which she writes. ‘Altar’ was written before NewDad’s debut album had even been released, and between that record and this, she found the time to release her first solo album, ‘Bottom Of The Pool’, too.  
 
Across all of her writing, but particularly on ‘Altar’, her artistry has helped her to find more understanding of both who she is as a person and her relationship with being a musician. “These songs have definitely helped me understand that and become a stronger person,” she nods. “I can be bad at standing up for myself. But you really need to do that in music, otherwise people will take the piss. I definitely realised that through songwriting.” 
 
That side of ‘Altar’ finds the singer grappling with her people-pleasing tendencies on ‘Entertainer’ and tackling the expectations put on female musicians on ‘Heavyweight’. 
‘Roobosh’, a tightly-wound song that’s driven by a propulsive, rumbling bassline and Dawson’s sudden yells, plunges us into the confusing quagmire of being a woman in society, pulled deeper and deeper down by the expectation to be “so patient and understanding and nice all the time”.  
 
“That is placed on us, but I also definitely play into that,” Dawson explains. “I’m a people pleaser, and I’m trying not to be, but I want to make people happy. I just wanted to have one song where I just went, ‘Fuck you, fuck this’. I wanted to just have a whinge and one song where I just fucking went for it. I wanted it to be slap bang in the middle of the record, just completely off-kilter, like, ‘What the fuck?’” 
 
For NeFittingly, given the love for home on ‘Altar’, the continued ascent of the three-piece on this record will also continue to further Ireland’s current standing as a hotbed of world-beating creative talent. NewDad are bringing something fresh to the new wave of original, formidable young acts from the country, distinctive from their peers as they join them in making waves around the world.  
 
Whether live or on record and regardless of where listeners are tuning in from, Dawson hopes ‘Altar’ helps people gain the courage to stand up for themselves and be proud of themselves, and gain the strength that this confident new album has given her. “Nothing’s perfect,” she reflects, “but if you just work hard and are true to yourself, it’ll be alright.” Sacrifices might still have to be made in the balancing act of life, but ‘Altar’ at least has helped Dawson accept that and is about to take NewDad to even greater heights.  wDad’s second album, the band enlisted rising producer Shrink – aka Sam Breathwick – to work with them in the studio, as well as reuniting with writer Justin Parker. The relationship with Shrink began in writing sessions, coming up with ‘Entertainer’ and ‘Safe’, the title track from the band’s 2025 EP, together. “These songs that we spent two days writing and he produced sounded perfect, so I was like, ‘I want to see what else we can do’.”  
   
The results are a record that’s as beautiful as it is crunchy and in-your-face, deftly skipping between sparkling, gentle moments and heavy blasts of guitar and bass whenever the songs demand. It’s more pop-leaning in its scope, drawing from Dawson’s appreciation of the current pop landscape and “cool rock bands with a lot of brightness to them” like R.E.M. and The Sundays.  
 
The expansion of the NewDad sound will be reflected in the band’s new live show – an already acclaimed setup that’s gained them slots at every major UK festival, landed them support slots for Pixies, Fontaines DC and The War On Drugs, and taken them as far afield as Japan and China. “I think our biggest headline show was in Shanghai, and the whole crowd were singing ‘White Ribbons’,” Dawson recalls. “I burst into tears. That’s the only time that’s ever happened to me, but I was like, ‘How is this real?’”  
 
The next phase of NewDad touring – which sees them return to China, Japan, North America, Europe and the UK over the rest of 2025 – will see Shrink join their on-stage line-up too. His addition will, Dawson says, make the songs sound “much more full”: “It’s a big step up. The songs that we have struggled with before – getting them across live – we have that now because we have another person.”  
 
Fittingly, given the love for home on ‘Altar’, the continued ascent of the three-piece on this record will also continue to further Ireland’s current standing as a hotbed of world-beating creative talent. NewDad are bringing something fresh to the new wave of original, formidable young acts from the country, distinctive from their peers as they join them in making waves around the world.  
 
Whether live or on record and regardless of where listeners are tuning in from, Dawson hopes ‘Altar’ helps people gain the courage to stand up for themselves and be proud of themselves, and gain the strength that this confident new album has given her. “Nothing’s perfect,” she reflects, “but if you just work hard and are true to yourself, it’ll be alright.” Sacrifices might still have to be made in the balancing act of life, but ‘Altar’ at least has helped Dawson accept that and is about to take NewDad to even greater heights.
activity_description_1757796763605175972: BROOKI are a four piece band from Dublin, Ireland, blending raw emotion with atmospheric guitars, heavy rhythms and infectious melodies. Drawing comparisons to the emotional honesty of Jeff Buckley and the grit of early PJ Harvey, the band create a sound that is both intimate and cinematic. Moving between moments of restraint and explosive intensity. Driven by distorted guitars, bass-heavy textures and dynamic live energy, BROOKI’s sound is anchored by Sarah’s striking vocal performance, which cuts effortlessly through the noise. With emotionally charged songwriting and powerful live performances, BROOKI leave a lasting impression long after the final note fades.
activity_description_1757796780348837540: Big Sleep are a Dublin-based rock band making their name the old-fashioned way; through tireless gigging and a shared passion for live performance. From underground tunnel shows beneath the M50 to sold-out European tours, their journey is one of instinct, connection, and constant evolution. Formed by lead vocalist Rónán Connolly and Italian drummer Matteo Poli, the band later solidified with bassist Aidan Gray and guitarist Naiara Clarke LaFuente, who joined after a chance encounter involving an illegal rave, a forest, and a homemade stage. Their debut album ‘Holy Show’ is a conceptually rich and emotionally vulnerable collection that explores love, loss, and identity. In Ireland, a “holy show” refers to a messy situation, and each of the album’s ten tracks delves into its own emotional chaos.
activity_description_1757796780709547684:
Sarah Crean is an Irish singer-songwriter and producer based in Brighton. Her sharp eye for life’s intimate details and moreish voice shine through her dreamy, slow-burn Indie Pop. 

With a fast-rising catalogue including her 2023 EP Death by Laundry, home to viral single “02:00 am” (20M+ streams) and widespread international support, Crean has become unstoppable. Recent singles ‘22 Angel’ and ‘Baby (I'll Always Be the Lead)’ have continued that momentum, landing on Spotify's New Pop UK and marking Crean's first releases returned as a fully independent artist. 

Fresh off SXSW Austin, Crean is now on the cusp of releasing her sophomore album, Heirloom - entirely made by women. Sarah Crean has toured extensively with the likes of Florence Road, Bombay Bicycle Club, Pillow Queens, Haley Blais, U.S. Girls and more, and played standout shows including opening for Blackpink in Hyde Park and CMAT at London's O2 Forum Kentish Town.
activity_description_1757796789442088612:
Le Boom are Irish brothers Andy and Christy Leech, an electronic act known for their immersive live shows that sit somewhere between a gig, a rave and a house party. 
 
Instead of performing on a stage, they play from the floor in the middle of the room, surrounded by the crowd. With Christy and Peter Fleming building the music live and Andy’s spoken word cutting through the tracks, the audience becomes part of the show rather than just watching it. 
 
Over the past two years, Le Boom have built a loyal grassroots following through their secret Gael Rave events and dedicated WhatsApp communities. What began as a handful of intimate nights has grown into a community spanning Ireland, the UK, Australia and New Zealand, with pop-up events in Glasgow, Liverpool, London and beyond. 
 
Musically, Le Boom draw as much from trad, indie and spoken word as they do from electronic music. Their songs move naturally between Irish and English, reflecting the bilingual community that’s grown around the band.
activity_description_1757796813810994852:
F3miii is an Irish singer, songwriter and producer creating a distinctive blend of alternative R&B, electronic music and soulful songwriting. Known for his cinematic production and emotionally honest lyricism, he has quickly become one of Ireland's most exciting new artists. 
 
Over the years, F3miii has received support from many publications including; BBC, RTÉ and Hot Press. No stranger to the big stage either, having performed at international festivals including Forbidden Fruit and Electric Picnic.  
 
F3miii reached an international breakthrough in 2026 with his hit single "Noble." The track has since amassed over 100 million Spotify streams, charted across multiple countries and earned him his first appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 - making him the first solo Black Irish artist to achieve the milestone.
activity_description_1757796830504324772: Fresh from supporting Wet Leg in Dublin & Just Mustard across their UK tour, Cruel Sister quickly emerges as one of the most exciting voices in Ireland's alternative scene. A self-produced force within the new wave of shoe gaze, and alternative rock, her live show is massive, where delicate vocals hang in suspension against unrelenting guitar distortion. Her 2025 EP A CORPSE IS TALKING, featuring 6 Music favourites IRON PILLS and WINDOW SEAT, received the support of The Irish Times, NME, Clash, DIY, Wonderland, Notion, The Line of Best Fit, 1883 Magazine, District Magazine, The Forty-Five, Hot Press and Nialler9.
activity_description_1757796853757546148:
SELL EVERYTHING. Rooted in Dublin city’s DIY music scene and shaped by late-night sessions, worn-out tape decks, and a deep love for raw, honest songwriting. Formed in 2023, the group is led by frontman, guitarist, and songwriter Tom Kelly, whose creative vision drives their music, visual art, and clothing projects. He collaborates closely with lead guitarist Jack Usher, bassist Fionn Mac Lochlainn and drummer Oisín Cavanagh— a group of multi-instrumentalists, songwriters and producers. Also including Toby Whelan, a wizard on the modular synth. He adds a soundscape of dub delays and sirens which act as the glue that hold the band together.
With influences like King Krule, Toro y Moi, and Bar Italia, SELL EVERYTHING blends swirling textures with off-kilter grooves to create music that feels both intimate and expansive. Their tracks have landed on major Spotify playlists, including Pollen and Fresh Finds UK & Ireland, connecting with a growing audience of psychedelic and indie fans worldwide.
activity_description_1757796870635425444:
anna leah is an indie artist and singer-songwriter from Dublin. The solo artist blends folk elements with indie rock vibes, dreamy pop, and stripped-back acoustic sounds to create her musical style. Through her masterful songwriting and honey toned vocals front and centre, Anna invites her listeners on a relatable and poignant journey through themes of nostalgia, self-discovery, and navigating her coming-of-age journey, solidifying anna leah's status as an artist to watch in 2026 and beyond.

She has featured on some impressive lineups such as All Together Now Festival, Other Voices, Ireland Music Week, The Ruby Sessions and has opened for Sombr, Florence Road, James Vincent McMorrow, jasmine.4.t and Nell Mescal. Finding influence in her favorite artists such as Beabadoobee, Lizzy McAlpine, Phoebe Bridgers and everyone in between.
activity_description_1757796894140305060:
Aifric is a singer and songwriter from Galway whose music feels driven by something elemental – a kind of creative and emotional exorcism she describes as “holding a ball of fire that wants to be thrown somewhere.”
Raised in the rugged west of Ireland, immersed in the Irish language and a strong storytelling tradition, Aifric’s musical instincts took shape early. She began singing at an Irish-speaking convent school in Dingle, and later lived between a caravan on a dairy farm, a narrowboat in London, and an old grain mill in East Galway.
It was at the mill, that writing became the way she steadied herself. Songwriting that explored the complexities and richness of ordinary life, the beauty and brutality of landscape, the shifting identities of girlhood and adulthood, and a quiet resistance to the noise of modern culture.
activity_description_1757796904793837220:
Whether via her DJ sets or label Big Saldo’s Chunkers, Sally C has developed one of the most distinctive sonic signatures in electronic music. The Belfast-born, Berlin-based artist traverses the gamut of vintage house, hip house, acid and breakbeat, all with that unmistakable Chunker sound. 
 
Sally’s DJing journey begun in 2010 at the Reading Rooms in Dundee, Scotland, an iconic local club, playing host to the likes of DJ Pierre, DJ Sneak and Green Velvet. It was here she met an open-minded and accepting community and gained a crucial education in digging, mixing and all things dance music culture, an experience that would set her up for the rest of her career.  
 
These guiding principles of authenticity, community and independence lie at the core of who Sally is as an artist and have defined her brick-by-brick journey since day one. Moving to Berlin in 2015, she etched out a spot in the city’s thriving club scene, throwing parties at Griessmühle and her own open-air raves, all the while building a fanbase for her raw and chunky style. When she was tapped for her debut Boiler Room in 2019 at AVA Festival, it was a noticeable levelling up. No longer a developing talent, RA lauded her as a festival highlight, noting her “musical range and technical acuity”.
activity_description_1757796919993994916:
From a small, dark room on the northside of Cork city - a rehearsal space that is “very cold in the winter and very hot in the summer” - Cardinals have emerged with a debut album that appropriately swings from one extreme to the other. Darkness to light. Light to darkness. Hopefulness to despair. Compassion to chaotic indifference. 
 
A band forged through both family and friendship - brothers Euan (vocals, guitar) and Finn (accordion) Manning, their cousin Darragh (drums, tambourine, glockenspiel) and their former schoolmates Oskar Gudinovic (guitar) and Aaron Hurley (bass) - the five-piece have already positioned themselves at the vanguard of the Irish independent rock scene. And with Masquerade, they have flung off the shackles of their early influences to craft something entirely their own.  
 
“This feels like a natural progression,” says frontman Euan. “The early years feel like a band still finding ourselves and trying different things. 
Whereas the album's a bit more cohesive and a little bit more sure of itself.” 
 
Euan’s description of these songs as “soft ballads whipped into urgency out of a panicked necessity” aptly captures Masquerade’s mood; these are emotionally expansive songs, some simmering with an undercurrent of violence, cynicism or fervent discontent (Anhedonia, The Burning of Cork, Barbed Wire) others gleaming with a bright-eyed vulnerability. Crafting a record with an A-side and a B-side is a nod to the band’s collective love of vinyl, and Masquerade’s tonal shift takes its cue from a variety of contrasting influences - from Townes Van Zandt’s “soft and beautiful melodies” to heavier fare like Nine Inch Nails, Danish punks Iceage and goth-metal icons Type O Negative, as well as their previously-noted love of hip-hop. 
 
“For the most part, the B-side is a darker and grittier exploration of the themes than what comes before,” explains Euan. “I always appreciated it when a record could have that juxtaposition. Bowie's Low comes to mind; to have Warszawa on the same record as Be My Wife is brilliant. 
Sometimes an artist might be made to feel like they should write something that works and then reproduce it as many times as they can for the record, but exploring and experiencing different states of emotion is a human thing. 
That's something that interested us when it came to making this record.” 
 
Recording the album without a click track proved crucial to capturing the “beautifully imperfect” sound of Masquerade. With most songs written over the past 18 months, the band recorded in the legendary RAK Studios in London, with their fellow twentysomething producer Shrink at the helm. Studio engineer Isabel Gracefield suggested that Euan record his vocals for As I Breathe in the studio’s stairwell, which further stripped back the singer’s defences. 
 
“Office workers in RAK would descend the stairs after their day’s work and I'd greet them with a full mic setup,” he recalls, smiling. “It was a jarring experience, at first. Feeling scrutinised by the band or producer is usually enough to throw me off, so with strangers it was a whole other experience. But eventually you just let go and fight through it. And the end result is a take we were very happy with.” He nods. “Its vulnerability occurred in real time, as the song was laid down.” 
 
When it comes to lyrics, Euan is conscious of leaving songs open to the listener’s interpretation. He rails against the idea of songs having to be borne from personal experience, describing it as ‘reductive’ to assume that songwriters cannot write from a place of fiction or imagination, like any other writer. “I wish that my life was as interesting or as romantic as some of the songs make it out to be,” he laughs. “But a lot of them are just stories.” 
 
One real world element that did unintentionally become a running theme on the album was the multitude of religious references littered throughout Euan’s lyric sheet, whether it’s “Bask in the relief/ At the throne of Jesus Christ” on She Makes Me Real, “Don’t you think I’m holy? / The way the cross is on my neck” on Over at Last, or As I Breathe’s “You can wear the chain, I'll wear the collar of my clerical order”. 
 
“We all probably have different ideas individually of what our faith might be - but I think we're all really interested in the beauty of churches and religious symbolism, and stained glass,” says Finn. “I do think we all have some form of faith on the spectrum somewhere. I think the shift from a seriously Catholic country to a fairly secular country after the Murphy Report in 2009 probably had an effect, as well. Big social changes that happen when you're a child do affect you more than you realise.” 
 
Euan nods. “I try not to look too closely at what it is or why it appears so much in my songwriting,” he shrugs, “but it's there, and we're definitely connected to it - whether we like it or not.” 
 
There are other subtle nods to real life, whether drawn from personal experience or not. Cardinals rebuff the notion of being branded as a “Cork band” or even an ‘Irish band”, shirking off the ‘fetishisation’ of Irish culture that is being brazenly embraced by other acts and embellished by certain factions of the media. Nevertheless, their adopted city is in their creative DNA. The ferocious jolt of Anhedonia was inspired by a violent incident that Euan witnessed not long after moving to the city from the band’s hometown of Kinsale. Barbed Wire, with its lyric “Alcohol and ecstasy / And Aperol and THC / From City Hall / To George's Quay” was partly inspired by the acclaimed Irish writer Kevin Barry’s work, notably an essay that he wrote about his time in Cork. The Burning of Cork is an inadvertent protest song of-sorts, which draws parallels between the ongoing genocide in Gaza and the British forces’ decimation of Cork in 1920, as the lyrics despair at the patterns of violence repeated “again and again and again.” 
 
Other external touchpoints include the band’s discovery of the work of 
Norwegian-Irish artist Oda Sønderland. Her painting Fristeren was formative in creating the world of the record and shaping its themes, and which now graces the cover of Masquerade.  
 
“It’s such a striking image: it's like a refuge in what is otherwise a harsh and cold environment,” says Euan. “When I think of listening to records, or watching movies or art in any way, that's the way that I see it; as this place of refuge and intimacy. I think we all fell in love with that piece. It’s completely beautiful. And I think we just kind of knew that it had to be the cover.” 
 
It’s clear that Masquerade marks a new era for Cardinals. The making of the album has revealed something new of themselves, opening them up as a more collaborative entity - as evidenced by closing track As I Breathe, written just one week before they entered the studio. While much of the record’s lyrical content deals with the trials and complexities of navigating life, the album ends on a tentatively hopeful note with the striking line “Even as we fall / I have learned the world is small / And I proceed.” 
 
“I think you can definitely put the emphasis on ‘band’ now more than ever, for the five of us as a working unit,” nods Euan. “The first album is daunting, but I feel like you’re not going to look at anything the same afterwards, artistically. The work that goes into it is an awful lot, and you're putting a lot on the line in terms of vulnerability and opening ourselves up, emotionally.” He sighs softly, smiling. “It'll change whatever we decide to do next, musically or otherwise. I think it'll have that effect on all of us.”
activity_description_1757796934263017124:
Formed in 2025 from the debris of initial musical projects and a collective need to create something fresh, black nylon bring a polarising yet deeply emotive sound that feels distinctly authentic. Warped by sonic shimmers and fuelled with a heavy rhythm section, even their earliest work feels timeless, with their live performances carrying an unwavering, effortless cool.  
 
From supporting the likes of Inhaler, Bleach9:3, THEATRE and Kneecap to selling out London’s ‘Third Man’ and securing coveted slots at All Together Now and Electric Picnic, black nylon have proved their place as pioneers of the new generation of alternative music from the outset. Now with a weekly DJ set at the well-known Workman’s Club in Dublin and a headline show at Camden’s Elephants Head booked with So Young for September, black nylon’s versatility and growing live presence has already named them “Dublin noisemakers” (Hot Press).
activity_description_1757796946963369636:
Over the last year, the quartet - comprised of Tom Pollock (guitar, vocals), Ben Ashley (guitar), Charlie Arnison (bass) and Roy Lowe (drums) - have meticulously honed their craft, becoming one of the most talked-about new bands in the country for their riotous live shows which fuse anthemic US alternative, second-wave emo and garage rock. 
 
Building a devoted live following for a show that’s well-drilled yet off-kilter, as prone to erratic, noisy breakdowns as it is to shout-along choruses, they've racked up an impressive resumé that’s seen them open for the likes of Keo and Sunny Day Real Estate and hit up festivals including Live At Leeds, Sŵn, Mutations, Kendall Calling and Tenement Trail.
activity_description_1757796959797939876:
Burglar is an alternative rock band based in Dublin, Ireland. Willow and Eduardo formed Burglar after meeting in college in 2021 and bonding over their love of alternative acts such as Stereolab and Smashing Pumpkins. Their backgrounds couldn’t be more different; Eduardo grew up around the punk rock scene in his hometown of Goiânia, Brazil, while Willow comes from the indie-pop scene in Dublin. However, their blend of inspirations has given Burglar a unique and addictive sound. Willow’s dissociative lyricism and Eduardo’s confessional style result in energetic and catchy songs with interchangeable vocal leads and omnipresent harmonic work, alongside distorted guitars and buzzing synths.
 
They’ve been a mainstay of the Dublin gig scene for the last few years. Following their much-anticipated showcase at Ireland Music Week in 2024, they have gone from strength to strength, selling out their first two headline shows in Dublin, and completing support tours with US Girls, Adore, The Belair LipBombs and Theatre Band. Their own headline shows saw them playing in iconic London venues such as Windmill Brixton and Moth Club. They marked 2026 as their breakout year with the release of the absolute ear-worm 'Lovey' in January, closely followed by being named as one of The Irish Times 50 people to Watch for 2026. They've toured Bristol, Manchester, Glasgow and Leeds with their most recent single 'Star-Crossed', also winning over new fans at this year's The Great Escape, Brighton. They're now working on their debut album.
activity_description_1758847272768411488: Darren Kiely is an Irish singer-songwriter from Co. Cork whose emotionally rich, folk-infused music has earned him a fast-growing international following. First drawn to guitar as a teenager, Kiely began by learning the songs he loved before gradually challenging himself to write his own. After building a career performing covers, he realised he wanted to create music that felt more personal, honest and meaningful. His songs explore self-doubt, home, growth, relationships and the search for belonging, often blending folk-pop warmth with raw emotional detail. Now based in Nashville, Kiely continues to develop his craft within the city’s songwriting community, following time spent in New York that shaped his resilience and work ethic. From viral debut single “How Could You Love Me” to EPs Lost and From The Dark, Kiely remains focused on writing authentic songs he believes in — music that connects through sincerity, hope and heart.
activity_description_1759314552954302736: Abraham aka (DJ Ab-Stylez) began finding his way around the decks back in 2006 and it wasn't long before his natural talents were recognized. His unique ability to blend the most obscure songs with today's chart toppers into a perfect mix is flawless. He has developed his own unique style of Mashup in Hip Hop , R&B, Afrobeat, Dancehall, Latin & House. Ab-Stylez is a well rounded & technically skilled dj from Dublin..
activity_description_1759314571602178320: Allie Sherlock is an Irish singer- songwriter whose remarkable voice, emotional honesty, and captivating performances have earned her a global audience. What began as busking on Dublin's famous Grafton Street quickly grew into an international career, with millions of people discovering her through performances that showcased not only her exceptional vocal ability but also her natural connection with audiences. Over the years, Allie has built a community of more than 15 million followers across social media and amassed over one billion combined views, establishing herself as one of Ireland's most recognised young musical talents. Her music has reached listeners around the world, leading to sold-out headline shows, international touring opportunities,and collaborations with leading global brands.
activity_description_1759314589771903248:
Code of Behaviour are an Irish brass band based in Cork City. Their style is a blend of pop, jazz and overall madness, striving to make each moment a party. The set consists of their own arrangements of modern covers, traditional New Orleans standards, and original tunes.
Set up in September 2017, Code of Behaviour made their debut busking on the streets during the Cork Jazz Festival. Although known for “livening up the streets of Cork”, the band have also played at festivals, including Electric Picnic, weddings, college balls, charity events and other gigs.
The band is made up of trumpets, trombones, mellophone, saxophone, sousaphone and drums, with occasional singing (and dancing) thrown in the mix. “An exceptionally talented group of young lads” that you won’t want to miss!
activity_description_1759314605425045776:
Chris Watson is a DJ, musician, music producer, and artist who brings the spirit of 90s and 2000s dance music to life with a modern twist. With over 10 years of experience DJing around the UK, Chris has grown from a passionate newcomer to a sought-after name, drawing crowds that enjoy his unique blend of contemporary and nostalgic dance sounds.

Drawing heavily on the golden eras of dance, his sets are known for their infectious energy and emotional depth.
Chris’ videos has seen support from prestigious house music labels like Defected Records, a testament to his talent and authentic connection to the genre’s roots. His online presence is equally powerful, with his videos attracting millions of viewers worldwide and resonating with both seasoned fans and a new generation of dance music lovers. As he continues to innovate and evolve, Chris remains a force on the scene, creating moments on the dance floor which are unforgettable and true to the spirit of dance music.
activity_description_1759314616573505808:
Cody Wong is a Dublin-based DJ and producer pushing a fast, euphoric sound across hard bounce, trance and high-energy rave. With 15M+ streams across major platforms, he has built a catalogue that moves between underground club records and crossover moments, led by his breakout "N13" on Ben Hemsley's BEBE.

2026 has marked a major step forward in Cody's European profile. His "CLUB 808" EP landed on Franck's Carouse, followed by "Explode" on Polyamor Berlin and "Don't Play With Me" on Rave Alert, with further music forthcoming on Charlie Sparks' ELEKTRA. That run places Cody across some of the most relevant new-generation labels in the bounce, trance and rave space.

His productions have earned support from VTSS, Ben Hemsley, Hannah Laing, Chippy Nonstop, ØTTA, Pegassi, Azyr, Netta, Sim0ne, DATSKO, Karl MX, Winson and Mark Blair, alongside support from BBC Radio 1.

Away from releases, the momentum is translating directly to the dancefloor: sold-out headline shows, 700+ tickets at INDEX Dublin on four days' notice, Ibiza appearances and an Australian run, alongside sets and features with Rave Rotterdam, Let Him Cook and Radio Radina. His current sound is direct, energetic and emotional - hard bounce drums, trance-led melodies and rave pressure built for peak-time rooms.
activity_description_1759314632117596432: In a time where music is increasingly shaped by algorithms and artificial creation, Aimée stands for something real. A songwriter first and foremost, she creates music rooted in human experience - raw, emotional, and impossible to replicate. This is pop with purpose, and it’s only just beginning. In a world increasingly flooded with AI-generated music and manufactured artists, Aimée is cutting through with something real. Her songwriting is raw, human, and impossible to fake - the kind that feels like your best friend telling you exactly what you need to hear. If you’ve been craving unapologetic pop - big choruses, real emotion, artists who mean every word - Aimée is leading that charge. Inspired by 90s and 00s icons but never confined by them, she blends nostalgic energy with a modern Irish edge, pulling you in with the tempo and keeping you there with the truth.
activity_description_1759314640783028496:
Have you ever seen bubbles sparkling on a red hot bassline? PrYmary Colours are that sparkle- and are heating up stages all over the world. 
There's music & there's dance. There's performance & there's aesthetics. And there's PrYmary Colours, who fuse them all together in one neat pumping package!
Having played at the House Of Yes club in New York, and the Olympia in Dublin, along with a host of festivals such as Electric Picnic, Beyond The Pale, Forbidden Fruit, MOTHER Pride, Dublin Pride Parade, and All Together Now, and more recently Latitude UK, there's no stage these guys can't fill. 
PrYmary Colours offer, a duo performance in DJ & Singer for club events or the full live show experience for festival stages, with dancers, hula hoopers, costumes, confetti, bubbles, visuals, cold sparkles, lights and more. 
Named as “New Artist Of The Week” (twice!) in the Irish Times, PrYmary Colours’ music received airplay on BBC Radio 1, 2FM, Today FM, and many regional radio stations. Their songs “House Of Love“, and “Heaven On Earth”, featured on top playlists from the infamous Pikes club in Ibiza. Their song "Sky's No Limit" featured on Heineken's "Summer Of Sound" vinyl LP. Also, their song "The Movement" was shortlisted for Ireland's "Irish Music month" on 98FM. Many of their releases are found on HOTHOUSE LABEL and can be found on all streaming platforms. 
Their latest track “Spin It” is out soon on Mousse T’s German label Peppermint Jam Records, accompanied by a mini-documentary. Also coming soon, is a collection of collaborative releases with George Feely.
Their music has received support from many of the top DJ's, such as Laurent Garnier, Eliza Rose and David Morales, and the guys have played along side the likes of Kelis, Yaeji and Greg Wilson.
They look forward to sharing their magic with you
activity_name_1759314647997231376: Dave Treacy b2b Shane Sully (Coca Cola Dream Academy Winner)
activity_description_1759314670008938768: Dublin DJ & Producer, Rendezvous resident, 37 Dawson St, 4 Dame Lane, RIOT; Plays Hip Hop, RnB, Afrobeats, Salsa

spontaneousjaminabuzzingDublinclub,SteveO(DJ),AranJohnston(drums/percussion),

make them the perfect act for events of all types
activity_description_1759314693488652560: Glasgow-born DJ CiaraE brings a genre-blending mix of house, electronic classics and high-energy grooves to the dancefloor. After sets in Ibiza and across the festival circuit, she’s back at Electric Picnic this summer, ready to bring the energy.
activity_description_1759334624041344396: Emmie came onto the scene in October 2022 and has since played venues in Dublin including Tengu, Index, Block and Wigwam, supporting artists such as Saoirse, Gene on Earth and Dave Angel. She has also played across Galway, Cork, Liverpool, London and in Berlin. Her sound spans house, garage, minimal and techno, with a strong focus on nostalgic 90s–00s sounds.Emmie came onto the scene in October 2022 and has since played venues in Dublin including Tengu, Index, Block and Wigwam, supporting artists such as Saoirse, Gene on Earth and Dave Angel. She has also played across Galway, Cork, Liverpool, London and in Berlin. Her sound spans house, garage, minimal and techno, with a strong focus on nostalgic 90s–00s sounds.
activity_description_1759334640348798348: Karl Seery is a Dublin based DJ & producer with over 4 million streams across his releases, with music on respected labels including Nervous Records, Monki & Friends and Choki Biki Records. His productions have received support from heavyweight names including Patrick Topping, Jamie Jones and Carl Cox.A regular across Ireland’s electronic music scene, he has played venues and events including Index, Wigwam, Pawnshop and BD Festival, while internationally holding a residency at Space Café Ibiza with Abode Records.  Karl is also the founder of Multitude, a collective championing local and homegrown talent.His sets span house, hard house, progressive house and trance, delivering a dynamic, energetic and dance floor focused sound
activity_description_1759334648896789900: With a love for both underground and more commercial leaning sounds, LAWRENCE’s sets are all about high-energy dance music that crosses genres — from Trance and Garage to Dub Techno and everything in between. His productions carry that same energy, ranging from deep ambient cuts to club-ready rollers.
activity_description_1759334695814274444: Jamie Ennis is a house music DJ from Dublin who is no stranger to the music scene with over a decade of experience playing in some of Dublin's most iconic venues including the 3 Arena, Punchestown Festival, The Academy, Hangar, The Wright Venue and many more.Jamie Ennis brings energy to every set with a style built around infectious grooves, driving rhythms and carefully selected tracks. With a knack for reading the crowd, he knows how to create a set that keeps people moving from the first beat to the last. His return to the White Claw Stage this year is not one to be missed.
activity_description_1759334703858949516:
Hailing from the garden of Ireland, Wicklow. Yours Truly earned her stripes in Berlin, where she captured the art of mixing deep and cavernous hypnotic techno. 

Over the years, Truly has graced stages at Electric Picnic Rave in the woods, Fuinneamh Festival the last three years, District 8 festivals, Otherside Festival. Dublin clubs such as Index, Tengu, Celllar and wigwam and Berlins Aeden, Anomalie and Suicide club. Sharing the spotlight with renowned artists like Mall Grab, VTSS, Skin On Skin, CJ Bolland, Altinbas & Sjaak. Known for her high-energy performances she creates an immersive experience that keeps the crowd moving.
activity_description_1759334717356219788: Fun, feisty and fabulous - Maria Lawlor is your favourite influencer’s favourite DJ. Whether it’s at a festival, a PR event, or hanging out a window at Pride, she’ll have you bopping away all night long to a blend of pop throwbacks that make you say “I haven’t heard this song in AGES!” From times tables to turntables, this former primary school teacher has quickly taken parties all across Ireland and beyond by storm. Grab your pals and get ready to sing your hearts out with the Queen of Songs With Words
activity_description_1759334727204445580: Foxgluv brings creatives together to connect, share their work and take up space. Open to everyone, the platform was created to champion women, non-binary and trans artists from a diverse range of backgrounds.
activity_description_1759334734594809228: A regular behind the decks at clubs all over the country, including residencies at Fidelity and Pygmalion, DJ Deece has built a reputation for house-heavy sets rooted in disco and groove, bringing the late-night energy. Having played everywhere from a Boiler Room at AVA Belfast, to Ministry of Sound in London, to Arcadia at All Together Now, he's become a familiar name across the Irish club scene over the last 15 years. Fun without being too obvious is the vibe, and Deece is the word.
activity_description_1759351153633864120:
The Irish Times label him as the '45 King' and Baz Hickey has earned
the right to be described as such. As the only Irish member of the
worldwide 45 Live DJ crew alongside heavyweights like Mr. Thing, DJ
Format and Coldcut’s Matt Black, he continues to push vinyl culture
through new reviews on the 45 Live website as well as hosting a monthly show
on French station Radio Krimi.
activity_description_1759351161754036664:
Sarah Murphy cut her teeth as a Craic Mechanic with Sing Along Social, where she learned that the best dancefloors are built on joy, connection and a great song at exactly the right moment.
Now behind the decks, she brings that same spirit to open-format sets that move freely across genres and generations - mixing the familiar with the unexpected, and weaving in the forgotten songs you didn’t know you needed to hear again. Expect big tunes, left turns and collective joy.
activity_description_1759351173581973944: Tuáthla moves seamlessly between the studio and the stage as an open format DJ and radio presenter. A true vibe creator, she knows exactly how to build the energy and keep a dance floor moving. A fun blend of hip hop, R&B, pop, house & more.  She’s know for high energy sets that create memorable moments in the crowd.
activity_description_1759351198278035896:
Belfast-born Winnie Ama is a Northern Irish-Ghanaian singer-songwriter who blends soulful vocals and lyrics with pop, disco and dance music. Inspired by jazz legends Ella Fitzgerald, Billie Holiday and Nina Simone, she began as a poet before transitioning to songwriting and later pursuing singing with her debut release in 2020. She went on to catch the attention of Macy Gray and Sister Sledge, opening shows for both artists.
She also gained recognition from BBC Introducing as a rising star and headlined the BBC Introducing Stage at Latitude. She earned RTÉ 2FM ‘Rising Artist’ status, delivered a TEDxStormont talk and received a ‘Rising Star’ gold disc from Ditto Music in 2023. In 2024, she was recognised as ‘One to Watch’ by the Belfast Telegraph and The Irish Times. In 2025, she made her SXSW debut in Texas, showcasing material from her forthcoming debut album.
Beyond performing, Winnie Ama advocates for diversity and inclusion in the music industry through her work as a data analyst for the Why Not Her? movement. She is also a qualified Mental Health First Aider.
activity_description_1759351207279012280: Ireland’s premier Afrobeat orchestra, Yankari are led by Nigerian composer and bandleader Segun Akano. Blending Afrobeat, highlife, jazz and contemporary influences, the band delivers one of Ireland’s most powerful live shows. Their rhythm-driven, politically conscious music honours the legacy of Fela Kuti while pushing the genre forward—always with an irresistible groove at its heart.
activity_description_1759351214082173368: Pablo Santo is a DJ and selector who refuses to be boxed in. With roots in Brasília and a home in Dublin, his sound is a testament to his musical journey.  Known for his ability to effortlessly move between genres, styles, and tempos, he’s a favorite in the Dublin scene and has shared stages with some of the biggest names in dance music, including Palms Trax, Avalon Emerson, and Gerd Janson. As one half of the Different Rhythm crew, he's dedicated to introducing audiences to new sounds, both on the dance floor and through his monthly show on Dublin Digital Radio.
activity_description_1759351222495947192: Emma Buchanan is a Belfast-based DJ known for bringing infectious energy and eclectic sounds to dancefloors across Northern Ireland and beyond. With a seamless blend of Disco, House, and creative reworks, she’s built a reputation for crafting feel-good, high-impact sets that keep crowds moving from first beat to last. Holding residencies at some of Belfast’s top venues and performing at major events, Emma’s style is all about connection, vibe, and pure party energy - the perfect soundtrack for unforgettable festival moments.
activity_description_1759351229953419704: Hailing from the west of Ireland, Rookie has been a staple of the Galway scene for near on a decade now. He made a name for himself holding down residencies in both iconic Galway nightclubs, Carbon and Electric, playing a wide variety of genres from rap/hip-hop to house and techno. He’s also played country-wide, ranging anywhere from Donegal and Belfast to Cork and Dublin. He’s supported International names such as Groove Armada, Ben Hemsley, Richy Ahmed, Ejeca, Shee, Crosby and many more. On the festival circuit he’s played at Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE).
activity_description_1759351236697860536:
One of the most loved and sought-after DJs in Ireland, Claire Beck is a must-see fixture of Ireland’s
music festival and club scene. She is best known for award winning radio shows on TodayFM, and her joyful DJ sets where her signature style blends
House, Disco, Indie and Queer anthems designed to keep the dancefloor full.
Each performance tells a story, serving you music that you forgot you loved, music you
will love, with a sprinkling of spicy curveballs to keep you on your toes.
activity_description_1759351243937229240:
THXTTI is a Dublin based DJ with a Nigerian background whose
sound is a fusion of black diaspora rhythms.Her sets are all about
creating a high-energy vibe where everyone no matter their
background can get lost in the dance.
activity_description_1759351257325447608:
Forget Romance are husband-and-wife DJ duo Olivia Chau and Shane Serrano, playing the best of alternative indie from over the decades.
A tribute to Indie sleaze, ripped jeans and muddy Converse. Filling floors with nostalgia - the soundtrack to a generation that still knows every word.
activity_description_1759351266661968312: Stevie G is an Irish DJ who works at Corks RedFM and as a youth worker in cork and beyond.. He is one of Ireland's best known DJs and he is regarded as a pioneer when it comes to spreading music such as hip-hop, soul and afro-beats here. In his career he has DJ’d alongside Kanye West, Destiny’s Child, Jay Z, De La Soul, Kelis, Roy Ayers, Massive Attack, Public Enemy, Lauryn Hill and many more iconic acts. He continues to play all of the big Irish music festivals and he hosts nights such as Jam, Taboo and the Old School Party in Cork and beyond.
activity_description_1759357429260605144:
An icon of house music, Armand Van Helden has been responsible for some of the biggest dancefloor anthems of the past three decades. From “You Don’t Know Me” and “My My My” to “I Want Your Soul”, his recognisable blend of house, hip-hop, funk and garage has shaped club culture worldwide.
He’s also one half of Duck Sauce, the duo behind the global smash “Barbra Streisand”, and his influence can be heard across generations of DJs and producers. Never tied to one sound or scene, Armand’s sets dig through classic house, disco, hip-hop and electrifying club cuts, powered by the instinct and unpredictability that have defined his career.
With a catalogue packed with timeless records and a reputation built across the world’s biggest clubs and festivals, Armand Van Helden remains a master of bringing people together on the dancefloor. Expect huge tunes, deep cuts and hands-in-the-air energy at Electric Picnic.
activity_description_1759357447413552856:
Blending the rhythms of his Zambian heritage with the energy of Scotland’s club scene, KILIMANJARO has become one of electronic music’s most exciting rising names. His sound moves effortlessly through Afro house, amapiano and high-energy club music, driven by powerful percussion and an instinct for bringing a crowd with him.
His breakout collaboration with Irish dance star Jazzy, “No Bad Vibes”, became a global favourite, while recent releases including “Rise”, “Hold It” and “I Don’t Want To Go” — featuring Bloody Civilian and South African vocal group The Joy — have continued to push his sound forward. He has also recently linked up with John Summit on “TIME WITH YOU”.
With his forthcoming nine-track project THE ASCENSION (INKAWAMI) marking the next chapter in his journey, KILIMANJARO arrives at Electric Picnic in full flight. Expect rolling rhythms, huge basslines, Afro-diasporic sounds and the kind of infectious, high-energy performance built for a festival dancefloor.
activity_description_1759357455626000088:
A familiar voice on Irish radio and a regular behind the decks at clubs and festivals across the country, Dave Treacy knows exactly how to get a crowd moving. The Dublin DJ, producer and presenter is the host of 2FM Dance, where he brings listeners the biggest new tracks spanning commercial dance, house and club music every Saturday night.
That same energy powers his live sets, mixing current dance anthems, festival favourites and upfront discoveries with a fast-moving, crowd-focused style. A long-standing presence in Irish dance music, Dave has played Electric Picnic numerous times, alongside appearances at venues and events in Ireland, the UK and Ibiza.
Whether he’s introducing tomorrow’s breakout track on air or dropping a hands-in-the-air favourite in front of thousands, Dave’s instinct for what works on a dancefloor is hard to beat. Expect big hooks, driving house rhythms and non-stop energy when he returns to Electric Picnic.
activity_description_1759357463125415640:
Jade is an Irish DJ with over 12 years of experience, specialising in underground house and tech house. Renowned for her high-energy sets and deep, groove-driven sound, she has established herself as a respected figure within Ireland's electronic music scene.

Now entering her third consecutive year performing at Electric Picnic, Jade's career has seen her support some of the industry's most in-demand artists, including Josh Baker, KETTAMA, and Chris Stussy. With a reputation for expertly reading a crowd and delivering unforgettable dancefloor moments, Jade continues to be one of the exciting names emerging from Ireland's underground scene
activity_description_1759357476983396056:
Alice Ugbah brings a genre-fluid energy to every set. Based in Dublin, her selections connect the sounds of Ireland, Nigeria and the UK, moving freely through Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, UK garage and underground electronic music.
Known for an eclectic approach that puts rhythm and atmosphere ahead of genre boundaries, Alice has been building her presence across Ireland’s club and festival scene. She has previously played Electric Picnic, Beyond the Pale and brought her sound to London’s Radio 1001, where her mix explored Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop.
Her sets are shaped by a musical palette: expect familiar favourites alongside deeper discoveries, smooth transitions into harder club rhythms and plenty of unexpected turns. Whether setting the tone early or raising the energy on a packed dancefloor, Alice plays with instinct, personality and a clear love of music that brings different sounds and audiences together.
activity_description_1759357477973251800:
Two of Dublin’s most exciting rising selectors join forces as LIA goes back-to-back with Viki Dos Santos for a high-energy journey through house, disco, garage and beyond.
In just two years behind the decks, LIA has made an impact on Ireland’s dance scene, with residencies in Ibiza and appearances across the UK and Netherlands. Her sets balance uplifting, euphoric melodies and nostalgic favourites with funky basslines.
Brazil-born, Dublin-based Viki Dos Santos has become a dynamic presence across Ireland’s clubs and festivals, playing everywhere from Index and Wigwam to District X and Electric Picnic. She has also shared stages with Honey Dijon, Overmono, Armand Van Helden, Luuk van Dijk and Route 94.
Together, LIA and Viki bring infectious energy, playful selections and a shared refusal to be boxed into one genre. Expect big house rhythms, disco colour, garage swing, unexpected turns and two DJs feeding off each other — and the dancefloor.
activity_description_1759357491520853720: With her years in the game, a multitude of awards, accolades and achievements, global tours and widespread influence, Sam Divine is a powerhouse artist. Renowned selector, producer, label owner and all round inspiration to countless women worldwide, she has established herself as a formidable presence. With 25 years under her belt, Sam’s vision and determination remain as staunch as ever. Driven by the finite nature of life, she is instigating a pivotal shift in her lifestyle. What we might call ‘Sam 2.0’ is the next phase of her evolutionary path, utilising her knowledge and experience to reveal more of her truest self. Working on her personal growth, focusing on her wellbeing and exploring sobriety, while also pushing the boundaries of her creativity are key pillars of this internal, and external, development. As she reflects on the past couple of decades, Sam Divine is poised to push forward with the same energy and vibrancy that launched her onto the global circuit. This time with a fresh outlook and healthy Sam Divine habits that will facilitate longevity and ensure she retains her position as one of the Queens of electronic music..
activity_description_1759357529806460632:
Shauna Dee is an emerging force in Ireland’s electronic music scene, known for her high-energy, multi-genre DJ sets that seamlessly blend House, Disco, and Techno into a driving, crowd-focused sound. With over six years of experience behind the decks, she has built a reputation for versatile, fast-paced performances that adapt to any stage while maintaining a distinct identity.

In January, Shauna secured a standout milestone in her career when she was selected to support Ewan McVicar on his sold-out arena tour. She has performed at major festivals including Electric Picnic, Forbidden Fruit, All Together Now, and Longitude, alongside gigs across Ireland and international sets in Ibiza.

She is also set to perform at Éalú le Grá in Galway and Forbidden Fruit this May, with many yet to be announced festival bookings, continuing a trajectory of high-profile bookings and growing recognition within the Irish electronic music scene. Shauna Dee continues to gain attention for her technical ability, crowd control, and energetic delivery behind the decks.
activity_description_1759357544830457560: German producer, DJ, label and record store owner Cinthie has become one of the most sought-after artists in the contemporary electronic scene. Dubbed by many as the Berlin Queen of House, the last decade has seen her become an unstoppable force who has a touring schedule that takes her across the globe to perform at leading clubs and festivals across Europe, Asia, the Americas and beyond. Cinthie's knowledge of house music's foundations is second to none, as reflected by the vast vinyl collection she has been building since 1995. Her DJ sets cleverly join the dots between the past and the present and plot lines between the swing of New York, the rawness of Chicago and the energy of Berlin. They're stripped back and emotive, whether deep or vocal, and always married to an irresistible groove. In the studio, Cinthie has mastered the art of making maximum impact from bare musical essentials. For more than 20 years her timeless house sounds have come on labels like Heist, Aus Music and her own 803 Crystal Grooves, and in 2020 gave rise to her adventurous and accomplished debut album Skylines - City Lights. Cinthie's DJ-kicks mix in 2022 was another high-water mark. It's a revered series that had a big impact on her in the nineties, and her own entry is one of house music's best. House music isn't known for its live shows, and even less so for female live artists. But as always, Cinthie is breaking new ground and has recently taken her machines on the road to cult events like Sonar and Mutek. Her influential Elevate.Berlin store is also known for its exceptional taste: every record is handpicked by Cinthie. Such realness and authenticity have always been synonymous with proper house music, but they are also the values that stand Cinthie apart.
activity_description_1759357555911808728: Onai is an Irish-Zimbabwean DJ known for her deep, wide ranging musical knowledge and has been dominating decks across the globe. Based between Dublin and London, and currently an official Adidas DJ, she has shared stages with the likes of Sister Nancy and Tiffany Calver, becoming a staple at major festivals including Electric Picnic, All Together Now and Forbidden Fruit. From Alpine ski slopes and Irish club nights to international dance battles and poolside at the F1 Grand Prix, Onai continues to establish herself as one of Ireland's most versatile and exciting international DJs.
activity_description_1759357578787542744:
Lou Bru brings infectious energy and a love of the dancefloor to Electric Picnic. The Kildare-born, Dublin-based DJ moves through disco, house, electronic music and club-ready edits, connecting favourites, ’90s and 2000s dance influences, unexpected curveballs and deeper discoveries with confidence and personality.
Since making her Electric Picnic debut in 2018, Lou has become a familiar presence across Dublin’s clubs, festivals and arts spaces. Her sets are playful but purposeful, reading the room and building energy through driving rhythms, big vocal moments and tracks chosen to make people move. She has played alongside some of Ireland’s trusted selectors and is also part of the Pop Dungeon DJ duo.
Away from the decks, Louise Bruton is a journalist, author, playwright and creator of Legless in Dublin, where she champions disabled people and campaigns for better access. Behind the decks, her focus is firmly on connection, freedom and collective dancefloor joy.
activity_description_1759357586404398808: With a sound rooted in minimal and progressive house, Juslinis delivers energetic sets shaped by hypnotic percussion, atmospheric layers, and carefully curated underground selections. Moving seamlessly between deep, ambient moments and high-impact techno energy, her approach prioritizes emotion, movement, and the shared experience of the dancefloor.
activity_description_1759357596856604376:
A defining force in UK culture, Skepta has spent two decades reshaping the sound of the UK underground. From founding Boy Better Know and creating grime anthems including “Shutdown” and “That’s Not Me” to winning the Mercury Prize with Konnichiwa, his influence reaches far beyond music into fashion, film and art.
For this special DJ set, Skepta returns to where his journey began: behind the decks. Through Más Tiempo, the house-focused label and event series he launched with Jammer, he has channelled his boundary-pushing instinct into rolling grooves, deep basslines and high-energy electronic music built to bring people together.
Now leading a season-long Más Tiempo residency at Hï Ibiza, Skepta arrives at Electric Picnic in full DJ mode. This is not a live rap performance, but a chance to experience another side of a fearless British creative figure. Expect house, tech-house, UK club energy and complete freedom on the dancefloor.
activity_description_1759357605714974424:
From grime foundations to house music, DJammin brings the energy and attitude of London’s underground to every set. The Hackney-honed DJ, producer and MC first made his name through early releases and collaborations with the Boy Better Know collective before following his passion for electronic music into new territory.
Now a key part of Skepta’s house-focused Más Tiempo project, DJammin has become known for sets that connect his grime roots with rolling grooves, hypnotic basslines and high-impact club rhythms. Recent appearances have seen him play alongside Skepta and take his sound to dancefloors including Hï Ibiza, while his latest release “Drive By” with grime heavyweight D Double E brings both sides of his musical world together.
Arriving at Electric Picnic directly before Skepta, DJammin is placed to set the tone. Expect a fast-moving collision of house, UK club sounds and grime energy from an artist built for the dancefloor.
activity_description_1759357614338463448:
Paige Tomlinson is a UK-based DJ and producer whose rise through the club circuit has been
driven by high-energy sets and a growing catalogue of club-focused releases. With a sound that
leans into fast-paced house and hard-edged grooves, she’s become a regular fixture in
peak-time slots, building a reputation for sets that are direct, energetic and locked into the
dancefloor.
This year alone Paige has dropped a slate of standout tracks that reflect her evolving sound and
uncompromising club ethos. From the infectious club single Listen 2 Me — a staple in her sets
— to high-energy remixes including Always & Forever, CONTROL and Chiggy Chiggy (feat.
Inéz), each release showcases her ability to rework familiar material into something built for
impact.
2025 has also seen her momentum recognised on a wider scale. Paige was named one of
Mixmag’s Breakthrough DJs of the Year and received a nomination for DJ Mag’s Breakthrough
DJ as well as BBC Radio 1’s Future Star for 2025. Underlining the growing attention around her
work both in the booth and in the studio.
With a clear direction and a run of releases that hit where it counts, Paige Tomlinson continues
to carve out her place in the UK’s club landscape.
activity_description_1759357635586807512:
CAZ is one of Ireland’s fastest rising talents, a DJ/Producer hailing from County Wicklow, Ireland, with almost 10 Million streams across all platforms, CAZ is a big contender in the Irish Dance Music scene.
2022 was a great breakout year for this young talent. He re-released his track “My Eyes“ with 21NHG and was featured on that summers season of Love Island. This track also received heavy radio coverage from U.K stations such as BBCRadio1 and Capital Dance.
He finished off his year with a bang and was chosen by Belters Only to feature on their collective album , ‘ Irish Only: Volume 1 ‘ with his track ‘ Thought it be ‘.
Following his success on multiple platforms he has grew a strong following on Soundcloud and socials in which he launched his 'Sweet Tea' record that gained over 2 million streams and was signed to Patrick Toppings Trick Label.
Following the success of 'Sweet Tea' Caz has played shows in Belfast Telegraph, Belfast, Index, Headline Button Factory show, Ibiza Rocks, Mansion Mallorca, Eden Ibiza and many more.
activity_description_1759357646718490328:
Irish indie-electronic duo 49th & Main join forces with Dingle-born DJ and producer Caolan Ryan for a B2B built on real friendship, shared influences and an instinct for euphoric dancefloor moments.
49th & Main have taken their infectious blend of indie, pop and electronic music from Kilkenny to Glastonbury, a BBC Radio 1 Future Artists session and a sold-out Vicar Street headline show. Caolan moves between garage, breakbeat, drum & bass and atmospheric electronica, with his acclaimed debut EP LOVE and standout performances alongside Fred again.. marking him as one of Ireland’s most exciting new electronic artists.
Having already tested their chemistry across a series of B2B sets — including a sold-out hometown show in Dingle — the trio arrive at Electric Picnic with a forthcoming collaborative single on the way. Expect emotional builds, club-ready rhythms, big singalong moments and a set that brings together 49th & Main’s melodic energy with Caolan’s distinctive underground electronic edge.
activity_description_1759357647674791640: Marcus O’Laoire brings Sunday Service to Smirnoff Sound Nation, a 90min  journey through a lifetime of record collecting. House is the common thread, but that’s about where the rules end. Expect French touch, New York classics, West Coast oddities, overlooked disco, Balearic detours and the kind of records that don’t get played often enough.
activity_description_1759357657657235160:
GRL is the passion project of established techno DJ Cailín. As GRL she expresses her roots in House Music and shares another side of herself artistically via her record collection and hardware productions. 

Cailín’s GRL alias has enjoyed success since its conception with headline club gigs and appearances at festivals such as All Together Now, Electric Picnic, Éalú Le Grá, D8 in the Garden and Fuinneamh.
activity_description_1759363112760638268: Altan have long been established as being to the forefront of traditional Irish music for nearly forty years now. Frontwomen, fiddler and singer, Mairéad Ní Mhaonaigh and her late husband,flute player, Frankie Kennedy formed the band back in the early eighties after their highly acclaimed album on Gael Linn, "Ceol Aduaidh" (Music of the North) 1983, which focused on the music of their roots and background in Co Donegal and the North-West in general. The band have toured all over the world, bringing their unique sound to places as diverse as the Hollywood Bowl, The Albert Hall and to small dance halls and bars in the remote areas of Donegal and beyond. Their music spans an emotional spectrum from top energetic reels to sof sensitive love songs.This gives audiences a glimpse of the the depth and richness of our Irish music heritage. Such is the importance of Altan's popularity at home and abroad that the lrisr Government through An Post (The Irish Postal Body), honoured Altan by issuing a postal stamp featuring the band on November 7, 2006. This award showed Altan's immense impact on recent Irish culture at home and abroad and the growing popularity of Irish traditional music generally. Altan have also been recognised by the Donegal County Council, when they hosted a civic reception in their offices in March 2018, in recognition of their contribution to traditional Irish music for over 30 years and becoming globa ambassadors for County Donegal worldwide. With their excellent produced award-winning recordings, from their ground breaking 'Island Angel'-album going to no.2 in the Billboard Worlc Music Charts in 1993,to their more recent "Gap of Dream" 2018, Altan are going from strength to strength having over 2-7 million hits on tracks on Spotify ! Altan's latest album 'Donegal' on Compass Records Nashville TN (2024) has been received with great enthusiasm and shows their staying power even after 40 years on the roacWith Mairead NÍ Mhaonaigh on fiddle and vocals, Ciaran Curran, bouzouki, Mark Kelly guitar, Clare Friel on fiddle jand Martin Tourish, accordion, the band are in top form and are playing in top venues from New York to Tokyo.

location_description_1708782041623282700:
Welcome to Global Green, Electric Picnic’s pop-up ecovillage where art, activism, music, food, creativity and community come together. Home to artists, activists, growers, makers, musicians, campaigners and 50 organisations from across Ireland, Global Green is a vibrant space for connection, discovery and inspiration.

By day, explore hands-on activities, interactive stalls, community gardens, nature experiences, creativity workshops and thought-provoking conversations on food, energy, biodiversity, wellbeing and social change. As the sun sets, Global Green comes alive with live music, spoken word, DJs, dancing and performance.

Coordinated by Cultivate, the sustainability collective based in Cloughjordan Ecovillage, Global Green brings together cutting-edge ideas, community action and bold imagination on the green edge of the festival.

Elements of Change – our engagement and music stage, with yoga, panel discussions, spoken word, live music and DJs.
